Title: Manager, Loyalty Marketing, APEC
Description:
JOB SUMMARY
The Manager, Loyalty Marketing is a high-impact, commercially oriented role responsible for driving member growth, engagement and retention across Asia Pacific excluding China (APEC).
This is a new role sitting at the intersection of loyalty strategy, CRM, and experiential partnerships - built for a marketer who is equally comfortable designing a lifecycle journey and activating world-class partnerships. You will own the end-to-end member journeys for one of the world's largest hospitality loyalty programs, translating global strategy into locally relevant, measurable initiatives across a diverse and dynamic region. This role will report to the Director, Loyalty Marketing, APEC.
You will lead the evolution of CRM and lifecycle marketing for APEC — defining segmentation strategy, designing engagement programs, and driving measurable improvements in activation, retention and reactivation. You will work in close collaboration with global, continent and market teams, and play a central role in building the reach and scaling our loyalty program as a long-term growth driver for the business. Success in this role requires strong organizational skills, strategic thinking and a member-centric mindset.
This role is based in Singapore.
CORE COMPETENCIES
- CRM & Lifecycle Marketing: Deep, hands-on experience designing and executing programs across the full customer journey. Builds segmentation logic, personalisation strategy and automated flows anchored in commercial outcomes, not just campaign execution.
- Loyalty & Partnership Marketing: Solid understanding of loyalty program mechanics (earn/burn, tiering, member value proposition) and how to market them effectively across segments and channels. Proven ability to activate brand partnerships, event management and experiential moments from brief to delivery, with strong agency management.
- Data Analysis & Fluency: Comfortable working with member behaviour data, campaign analytics and dashboards to surface insight and drive continuous improvement. Tracks activity to outcomes, not outputs.
- Communication & Brand Stewardship: Executes customer-facing communications with a consistent, on-brand voice across owned and paid channels. Brings sharp copywriting instincts, strong creative review judgment, and the ability to influence and align across global, regional and local teams with different cultures and working styles.
- Execution & Project Management: Highly organised with a strong bias for delivery. Manages multiple workstreams simultaneously, ensuring projects adhere to timelines.
CANDIDATE PROFILE
We are looking for a marketer with 4+ years of experience in loyalty, CRM or lifecycle marketing, ideally within hospitality, travel, or a consumer brand environment.
Requirement
- 4-5 years of relevant professional experience in program management, marketing strategy, loyalty and lifecycle disciplines, digital or related function
- Experience managing and directing strategic partners / agencies /vendors. Demonstrated relationship marketing skills a must.
- Team player, proven ability to lead and work with cross-functional teams in support of specific business priorities
- Languages: Proficiency in English required; proficiency in reading and writing in other Asian languages strongly preferred.
JOB SCOPE
Loyalty & Lifecycle Marketing
- Drive member growth, engagement and advocacy across APEC through loyalty-led initiatives that build program awareness, deepen usage and deliver locally relevant member value
- Develop and execute the continent's loyalty marketing plan - spanning promotions, lifecycle programs and CRM strategy - aligned with global strategy and optimised for local market nuance
- Define and manage CRM strategy across the full customer lifecycle: acquisition, onboarding, engagement, retention and reactivation
- Plan and execute loyalty-led campaigns across owned channels (email, app, digital) and paid channels (social, digital) with audience analysis, targeting, segmentation and performance tracking
- Identify opportunities for segmentation, personalisation to deliver on deeper customer value optimisation; drive continuous improvement in CRM effectiveness and automation capabilities
- Leverage market research, member insights and data analytics to inform engagement strategies and personalised experiences
- Design, implement and optimise loyalty programs that drive advocacy and revenue, delivering tangible value to target member segments
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams including but not limited to MarTech, Enterprise Partnerships (Co-Brand, Airlines, Everyday Earn) and Loyalty Operations to integrate and orchestrate initiatives across key customer touchpoints
- Serve as gatekeeper for all loyalty member communications, ensuring on-brand, accurate and effective execution
Performance Operations & Governance
- Track and report program KPIs covering member acquisition, activation, retention, revenue contribution and repeat stay behaviour, with clear recommendations for improvement
- Oversee CRM data accuracy, integrity and compliance across programs
- Drive effective onboarding, training and adoption of loyalty programs and systems across property teams
Experiential Partnerships
- Support the activation of global and regional marketing partnerships translating partnership rights into compelling, member-facing campaigns that drive high member engagement, leveraging on Marriott Bonvoy Moments
- Ensure all partnership campaigns are executed in full alignment with partners, with rigorous agency management and end-to-end campaign planning
- Support end-to-end event management and logistics planning for partnership activations, ensuring seamless on-ground execution and member experiences
Working Relations
Key interfaces:-
- Area Directors of Marketing
- Field Marketing team
- Continent level agencies.
Integrated Marketing Planning
- Supports development of continent destination marketing strategy and focused on key source markets and KPIs.
- Monitor competitive activity in the category.
Promotions/ Partnerships
- Partners with Revenue Strategy, develops and executes promotions/offers that drive KPIs for the continent or market (eg. Enrollment goals, direct channel goals, driving leisure revenue, etc.).
- Partner with analytics team to ensure proper tracking and communication of all programs.
Integrated Marketing Execution
- Develops marketing brief with clear KPIs and conducts kick off for all new programs.
- Engages agencies in RFP process and project manages the creative design and execution process to bring a program to market. Ensures consumer messaging is clear.
- Is responsible for ensuring all key stakeholders of the program are aligned.
- Is responsible for communicating programs to the market and corporate teams and ensuring all channels are leveraged (social, digital, sales, etc).
- Reviews program performance in real time and modifies program as needed.
Area/ Hotel Support
- Partners with Directors of Field Marketing and other area marketing leaders.
- Provides strong guidance on positioning and pull through of brands.
- Advises field marketing on effective marketing communications planning, implementation and evaluation.

Title: Manager, Marketing and Communications
Description:
About Asia Climate Philanthropy Advisory
The Asia Climate Philanthropy Advisory (ACPA) is headquartered in Singapore and supported by several leading philanthropists and climate foundations. ACPA is mandated to support ultra-high-net-worth individuals to make philanthropic investments into the climate action space by providing bespoke advisory support, curated local climate knowledge, carefully vetted giving opportunities, and access to a diverse network of climate-focused experts, peers and partners.
About the Role
We seek a seasoned, outstanding individual to join as its Manager, Marketing & Communications and lead the implementation of ACPA’s communications roadmap, including content strategy, digital engagement, events planning, and media outreach. This is a hands-on role suited to someone who combines strategic thinking with strong execution, creative flair, and excellent project management skills.
Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Manager will help position ACPA as a trusted, visible, and credible partner in the Asian philanthropy ecosystem — translating complex ideas into compelling narratives that inspire giving and collaboration on climate action.
Responsibilities
The Manager, Marketing & Communications will engage in the following areas of responsibility.
Support the implementation of ACPA’s brand strategy, messaging framework, and tone of voice across all channels.
Work with external agencies to produce brand and communications assets (e.g., templates, decks, infographics, case studies).
Develop and manage ACPA’s editorial calendar and content pipeline across website, LinkedIn, and other platforms as required.
Research, copywrite, and edit high-quality content such as articles, donor stories, partner spotlights, and thought leadership pieces.
Oversee website updates and work with designers and developers to enhance user experience and impact storytelling.
Support media engagement, including drafting press releases, managing media lists, and coordinating interviews and coverage.
Cultivate relationships with key communications and ecosystem partners to amplify ACPA’s visibility.
Track and evaluate media performance and engagement metrics.
Develop communications plans and promotional materials for ACPA convenings, briefings, and flagship gatherings.
Create on-site and post-event content, including talking points, recaps, and visual assets.
Support the production of POS and knowledge materials
Support communications with donor clients as needed by the Climate and Philanthropy teams
Manage external vendors and freelancers (writers, designers, photographers) to ensure timely delivery of outputs.
Track communications KPIs, maintain documentation and asset libraries, and contribute to reporting and evaluation.
Qualifications and Requirements
10-12 years of experience and track record in communications – ideally with non-profit/non-governmental organizations.
Proven experience developing and executing communication and brand strategies.
Superb verbal and written communication skills in English, with proficiency in writing, editing and storytelling. Proficiency in other Asian languages is advantageous.
Excellent writing, editing, and storytelling skills,
with a strong grasp of tone and audience adaptation.
Experience managing social media channels and content calendars.
Strong project management skills and comfort working with external vendors and cross-functional teams.
While not mandatory, a genuine interest in climate change and social impact, and ability to quickly grasp related concepts are desirable.
Proactive, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a small, dynamic and collaborative team.
Excellent event, project management and coordination abilities.
Track record of working in environments requiring professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality.
Resourceful problem-solving skills with a proactive, ‘can-do’ attitude towards challenges and changes.
Alignment with ACPA’s mission and commitment to embodying ACPA values.
Bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, marketing, journalism, or related field.

Description:
foodpanda is part of the Delivery Hero Group, the world’s pioneering local delivery platform, our mission is to deliver an amazing experience—fast, easy, and to your door. We operate in around 65 countries worldwide. Headquartered in Berlin, Germany. Delivery Hero has been listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange since 2017 and is part of the MDAX stock market index.
Job Description
We are looking for a highly-driven and motivated Manager, Performance Marketing to join our regional team. If you are looking for a place where you can make a direct impact, then this may be the place for you!
The ideal person for this role has a strong understanding of how paid performance marketing works across search and paid social channels and thrives in a fast-paced and dynamic work environment. This posting spans a broad experience range, and the scope and level of the role will be calibrated to the successful candidate's experience.
What's On Your Plate
- Be responsible for performance marketing campaigns across several markets in APAC and Europe, launching and optimising high-impact evergreen and integrated campaigns across Google Ads & Apple Search Ads.
- Own and manage channel budgets, pacing spend against targets and reallocating toward the highest-ROI opportunities
- Leverage AI and automation tools to streamline manual performance marketing workflows (campaign setup, bid management, reporting, and creative iteration), freeing up time for strategy and experimentation

- Track and maintain campaign performance and benchmarks to measure effectiveness of digital media and gather insights continuously to build best-in-class practices

- Using data analytics, provide analysis to give stakeholders a clear view on media channel performance and ROI

- Analytical and structured way of working, with a practical mentality and strong logical thinking skills
- Verbal & written fluency in English
- You are highly proactive and well-organised, and thrive in fast-paced environments

Title: Manager, Social Media Content Officer (MXD) [Temp - 1 year]
Description:
The temporary staff will support the planning, development and execution of social media content for SWDA’s corporate social media platforms. The role will provide additional capacity to support the increased volume and scope of social media work following the formation of SWDA, including new employer-focused and youth/IHL content workstreams.
What you will be working on:
1. Social Media Content Development and Management
• Develop and adapt social media content, including copy, visuals and short-form videos, for SWDA’s social media platforms.
• Translate programme, policy and industry-related information into accessible and engaging social-first content for different target audiences.
• Support the end-to-end content development process, from ideation and scripting to production, clearances, publishing and post-publication monitoring.
• Adapt content and messaging according to the audience, format and role of each social media platform.
• Support event coverage and other time-sensitive social media content where required.
2. Stakeholder Coordination
• Work with internal divisions to understand their communications objectives and advise on suitable social media content approaches.
• Coordinate content inputs, timelines, reviews and clearances with relevant stakeholders.
• Ensure that social media content is accurate, timely and aligned with SWDA’s communications objectives and social media standards.
3. Employer-Focused Content
• Support the development and implementation of new employer-focused social media content for LinkedIn and Facebook.
• Work with relevant divisions to identify suitable workforce and skills insights, including information from the Jobs-Skills Portal, and translate these into accessible social-first content.
• Support the development and management of an ongoing employer content pipeline.
4. IHL and Youth Content Co-Creation
• Support partnerships with Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) to co-create social media content targeted at students, fresh graduates and younger audiences.
• Develop content briefs and coordinate with participating IHLs and students throughout the content development process.
• Review and refine co-created content to ensure alignment with SWDA’s messaging, communications objectives and social media standards.
• Support the evaluation of IHL co-creation pilots to assess their potential as a sustainable supplementary content model.
5. Content Production and Performance Monitoring
• Support social media shoots and content production, including scripting, coordination and basic content production/editing where required.
• Monitor published content and support community management across SWDA’s social media platforms.
• Track content performance and identify relevant insights to inform future content development and optimisation.
• Support social media reporting and other operational requirements as needed.
Requirements
• Diploma or degree in Communications, Marketing, Digital Media, Mass Communications or a related discipline.
• Good writing and editing skills, with the ability to translate complex information into clear and accessible social media content.
• Familiarity with major social media platforms, including LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok.
• Experience or interest in social media content creation, including short-form video and visual content.
• Good stakeholder management and coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and timelines concurrently.
• Able to work independently while collaborating effectively with internal stakeholders and external partners.
• Familiarity with basic design and/or video editing tools would be an advantage.

- Manage and continuously strengthen SMU's brand governance framework, ensuring consistent application of the SMU brand across internal and external communications.
- Manage and maintain the SMU Brand Guide and Brand Portal as key sources of brand standards, resources and guidance.
- Review brand-related requests and provide clear, practical guidance to schools, offices and other University stakeholders on brand application, visual identity and communications.
- Monitor brand compliance across SMU and work with stakeholders to address and resolve issues where required.
- Develop and deliver regular brand engagement and education initiatives to build awareness and adoption of the SMU brand across the University.
- Support the development and management of SMU's brand properties, e.g. SMOO SMOO, merchandise and events.

Title: Marketing & Communications Manager
Description:
Our Employee Value Proposition
Advancing our People
Advancing our World
At CrimsonLogic we put your Career and Well-being first. We are committed to advancing your career through a full spectrum of professional development programs with the support of a strong Total Rewards philosophy that focus on your well being. We believe that by investing in each and every one of our employees' professional and personal growth, we can collectively make a positive impact on the world as we strive for greatness together in a nurturing and inclusive workplace.
Role Purpose(s)
You will lead marketing and communications for an assigned region or market segment, with end-to-end ownership of go-to-market and demand generation, PR and media, budget, and the revenue target. You will manage a small team and report to the Head of Group Marketing & Communications.
CrimsonLogic builds the software that keeps global trade moving through customs and ports. It is a category few people know, yet one the world depends on, and we are now rebuilding it around AI.
The Role
The specific portfolio will be confirmed on appointment, based on your strengths and the needs of the business.
Your primary focus is go-to-market and demand generation: planning, budgeting, resourcing, execution, reporting, and optimisation, directed at building qualified pipeline across our commercial and government customers. You also lead the region’s external presence across media, PR, and messaging.
This is a hands-on role. You lead a small team while remaining close to the work yourself: developing the strategy, building the plans, and delivering the campaigns. You will also help build the templates and playbooks the wider team adopts, piloting them in your own market first.
Where This Leads
This is a lean team, which means real responsibility from the outset and broad exposure to how the function operates. There is scope to take on more over time, earned through delivery rather than tenure.
What You Will Own
- Go-to-market and demand generation. Own the end-to-end cycle across digital, paid search, content, account-based marketing, and events, from plan and budget through to channel mix and results. You are accountable for pipeline and revenue, and you measure the work on outcomes rather than activity.
- PR and communications. Lead external communications for your market, including media relations, press, messaging, and any local agency, in coordination with the central communications team.
- Product marketing. Lead positioning, product launches, and the sales narrative, supported by the competitive intelligence that differentiates us in trade and port technology.
- Sales enablement. Equip the sales team to win with the right pitch, collateral, and case studies, identifying gaps and addressing them to a high standard.
- Events and field marketing. Own major industry events and field marketing end to end, from positioning through to measurable results.
- Team leadership. Lead and develop a small team: setting objectives, supporting development, managing performance, and raising the standard of the team’s work.
- Performance and optimisation. Own measurement and reporting, including dashboards, attribution, and analysis, and use the findings to improve marketing performance.
- Budget. Own the marketing budget, allocate it against priorities, and account for the return it delivers.
Who You Are
- You own the result. You are measured on pipeline, revenue, and adoption, and you manage to those targets. You plan back from the goal and adjust the approach when the numbers are not moving.
- You work independently. When you encounter something unfamiliar, you research it, test it, and make a decision, then document what worked so others can build on it.
- You speak your mind. When a strategy is weak or a forecast does not hold up, you say so, to peers and to leadership alike, and you support your position with reasoning. You revise your view when the evidence changes, and you expect the same of others.
- You hold a high standard. You expect a great deal of yourself and your team, and you see work through until it is right. You give direct feedback, and those around you improve for it.
- You lead across functions. You align sales, product, and the wider business through influence and credibility rather than authority. You manage upwards and sideways as effectively as you manage your own team.
About the Group Marketing & Communications Team
The Group Marketing & Communications team is small but broad in scope, covering demand generation and go-to-market across our commercial and government customers, in both trade and ports, together with corporate events, internal communications, and PR. Everyone here owns a substantial portfolio rather than a narrow function.

You have communications experience across media, PR, and external messaging, and you write well. Product marketing experience is an advantage. Ideally you have run a region, segment, or product line, managed a budget, and led at least one direct report. Title: Marketing & Media Senior Manager Asia & AMEA
Description:
We're seeking a senior regional transformation leader who can redesign how marketing operates across Asia and AMEA. The role is ideal for someone who has led marketing effectiveness, media, agency, and operating model transformation initiatives and enjoys influencing across a complex stakeholder environment.
What we ask
- Bachelor or Master in Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field.
- 15+ years of experience in senior marketing, media or transformation roles within large, multi-market organisations, including experience in B2B and B2C environments.
- Proven track record in marketing operating model transformation, media transformation, agency consolidation and end-to-end process improvement.
- You have a broader view than your own role, identify with our purpose "Nourishing by Nature", are customer-focused and act with speed and decisiveness to deliver results.
- Strong stakeholder management, commercial acumen and change leadership skills, combined with experience in data-driven decision-making, AI-enabled marketing tools and cross-functional collaboration.
What We Offer
- Unique company culture of Dutch heritage and international presence. At FrieslandCampina you work on strong, globally loved brands enjoyed by millions every day, like Friso, Campina, Chocomel and Frisian Flag. As a farmer-owned cooperative, we combine an international environment with a clear social and sustainable purpose. We support your growth through training, coaching and internal career opportunities. With trust and autonomy, you can make real impact.
- Competitive bonus scheme, flexible working hours, and the ability to work from home.
- Exceptional support of cross disciplinary movement within the company to broaden your knowledge and growth paths.
- A friendly and informal working environment
- Autonomy and trust to create longer term impact that helps bring better nutrition to the world
Vacancy Description
FrieslandCampina is executing a company-wide transformation to accelerate profitable growth, improve margins and strengthen global competitiveness. Marketing and media are key levers in this transformation and must become more focused, effective and efficient to ensure investments drive commercial impact. As Marketing & Media Manager Asia & AMEA, you will play a critical role in making this ambition a reality.
You will lead the creation and activation of the vision for marketing across the region, ensuring marketing remains relevant, competitive, efficient and a strong growth engine for the business. In close partnership with leadership and global stakeholders, you will be responsible for the design and delivery of strategic marketing transformation initiatives.
In this role, you will co-create the marketing transformation roadmap, align priorities with enterprise strategy and business objectives, and ensure measurable business impact through clear milestones, governance and performance tracking. You will drive the implementation of media transformation initiatives, lead the consolidation of creative agency ecosystems and production operations, enabling a more simplified, scalable and efficient operating model. Through the implementation of new governance structures, workflows and ways of working, you will improve transparency, speed, consistency and cross-functional collaboration across teams and markets.
A key part of the role is translating and embedding the new marketing operating model across Operating Companies. You will work closely with Marketing, Sales, eCommerce, IT, Data & Analytics, Procurement, Finance and external agency partners to drive alignment and execution in a highly matrixed and decentralised environment. Success will depend on your ability to influence without direct authority, build strong relationships and bring stakeholders together around a shared vision.
In addition, you will support organisation design, capability building and change adoption efforts. By identifying capability gaps, enabling upskilling and embedding new behaviours, you will ensure transformation is fully adopted and delivers sustainable results. You will continuously identify opportunities to improve media, creative, production and marketing operations while fostering a test-and-learn culture focused on ongoing efficiency and effectiveness gains.
This is a highly visible international role within Global Commerce with impact across Asia & AMEA B2C businesses. It offers the opportunity to shape the future of marketing at FrieslandCampina while working with senior stakeholders across the global marketing ecosystem.
For thousands of people every day, FrieslandCampina means more than just a dairy company. We provide high-quality nutrition while creating value for our member farmers, customers, consumers and communities around the world.
You will join the Global Commerce organisation and work at the centre of FrieslandCampina's marketing transformation agenda. The team is responsible for shaping the future of marketing through operating model excellence, media transformation, capability development and process optimisation. Working across Business Group Europe, B2B, Operating Companies and global functions, the team partners with senior commercial leaders, marketing teams, eCommerce, Sales, IT, Data & Analytics and external agency partners to build a more agile, data-driven and performance-focused marketing organisation.
Together, we are building the capabilities, ways of working and partnerships that will enable marketing to become a true growth engine for FrieslandCampina.

Title: Marketing & Partnerships Manager
Description:
Dr Scalp is a Singapore scalp and hair care brand with two studios, at Raffles City and The Centrepoint, and our own range of scalp and hair care products.
We use AI scalp scanning to show people what’s actually happening on their scalp, then treat it. It’s genuinely interesting to look at, and almost nobody has seen it before. We’re rebuilding this brand from the ground up, and a second AWHL brand joins in the next 6 to 12 months. What you build here is the foundation for both.
The Role
You own how Dr Scalp gets sold. The plan, the calendar, the promotions, the events, the partnerships, and the two people who execute them.
This is not a brief-writing job. Half of it is offline: roadshows, mall activations, visual merchandising, and picking up the phone to companies who have never heard of us. The other half is online, where you set the offer and the mechanic and your team builds it.
What You’ll Do
Plan it:
• Own the marketing plan and a rolling campaign calendar at least a quarter ahead
• Decide what each month is trying to achieve, and what the promotion is
• Brief every campaign properly: objective, audience, offer, mechanic, dates, channels, who does what by when
• Keep the calendar clear of collisions, between Dr Scalp promos and later between AWHL brands
Run it online:
• Set every website and marketplace promotion. You decide the offer, dates and target, e-commerce builds it
• Brief and approve every EDM
• Manage the performance marketing agency: budget, targets, weekly review, and the call on whether to keep them
• Decide when paid media comes in-house, build the case for it, and run the transition when it does
• Own the acquisition numbers. Cost per lead, cost per customer, return on ad spend
Run it offline:
• Plan and run roadshows, launch events and in-mall activations, from permit
application to teardown
• Own visual merchandising across both studios
• Own in-studio collateral. What exists, where it sits, when it gets refreshed
• Work the mall marketing teams for tenant campaigns and promotional slots
Open new doors:
• Build and work a pipeline of referral, collaboration and corporate partners
• Corporate wellness packages, workplace screening events, staff perk programmes
• Referral partnerships with salons, clinics, gyms, bridal studios and postnatal
services
• Negotiate the terms, hand them up for signature, and own the renewal
• Carry a partnership revenue target, reported separately from retail
Manage creators and suppliers:
• Source, brief and manage KOLs and paid creators, and measure what each one
actually delivered
• Source, onboard and manage affiliates, including commission structure and
tracking
• Manage the freelance brand designer and any agency we engage
Lead the team
• Manage the Social Media & Content Designer and the E-commerce & CRM
Executive
• Grow the team as the brand does. Scope the roles, write the briefs, and hire
the people
• Run the weekly marketing meeting, the monthly review and the quarterly plan
• Hold the quarterly performance reviews against each person's role standard
Own the numbers
• Spend the quarterly budget and answer for the return on it monthly
• Check every promotion for margin before it goes live
• Approve health and results claims across every channel, once you know the brand
well enough that we hand that over
• Report weekly on spend and campaign status, monthly on revenue against plan
and the partnership pipeline, quarterly on the plan for the next three months
Who We’re Looking For
• 4 to 6 years in marketing, including at least one year owning a plan and a budget
rather than executing someone else's
• You've run both sides. An offline activation and a paid campaign, not only one of
them
• You've closed a partnership or corporate deal yourself. Tell us how you found them
and what you offered
• You've managed people or agencies, and can tell us what you did when someone
underdelivered
• You can hold a media agency to account. You know how a campaign is structured,
what attribution is telling you, and what a well-run account looks like, even if you
are not the one building it
• You read the numbers before forming the opinion
• You can write a brief that a designer and a media buyer both understand
• Retail, beauty, wellness or F&B experience is a plus, not a requirement
This Role Is Not For You If…
• You were hoping someone else would do the cold outreach
• You need a big budget to be effective
• You've only ever briefed agencies and never built a campaign yourself
• You think marketing ends when the campaign goes live
• You want a clean, finished brand to work with rather than one being rebuilt
• You're looking for a slow, structured corporate environment
DrScalp is a pioneer in advanced scalp health solutions, and is a Singapore-based, science-driven scalp-care clinic offering AI analysis and advanced treatments for healthier hair and scalp.
Our mission
To provide our customers with customised treatments that address the root cause of scalp issues like hair loss, dandruff and inflammation. We combine state-of-the-art technology with personalised care to help you achieve healthier hair from the scalp up.
Our Vision
We believe that everyone deserves healthy, beautiful hair and that starts with proper scalp care. Our vision at DrScalp is to make cutting-edge scalp treatments accessible to everyone, ensuring long-term health and visible results. We’re here to transform the way you think about scalp health.
Our Commitment
We are committed to not only providing the best treatments but also educating our customers. We believe in empowering everyone with the knowledge to maintain a healthy scalp long after they leave our centre. From your first consultation to ongoing care, we’ll be with you every step of the way.

JOB SUMMARY
The Marketing and Communications Manager is part of an important team that creates and executes property-level communications to our customers. Under the leadership of the Director of Marketing and Communication, this role promotes on-brand messaging to customers through traditional, digital, and social media channels all with the goal of enhancing the image of the hotel. This role helps build direct marketing plans, targeted campaigns, and activated channels to the end of driving consumer awareness and preference, increasing market share, and building broader portfolio and brand awareness. This role focuses on showcasing Food and Beverage promotions, both to hotel guests and to local patrons. As part of the Marketing and Communication team, this role is fully connected into resources in their region; Marketing and Communication Managers liaise and build deep partnerships with their regional eCommerce and Marketing teams to verify all local, social, and digital marketing efforts are effectively integrated with the selling efforts for the organization. This role also gets to do a little bit of everything, from balancing traditional and digital marketing and eCommerce activities to contributing to public relations (PR) activities for the hotel. Success is measured by how well they help drive the sales and revenue strategy of the property, social media engagement and also by how effectively leveraged the resources around them are to create truly compelling marketing and communications campaigns.
CANDIDATE PROFILE
Education and Experience
Required:
• 2-year degree from an accredited university in Marketing, Public Relations, Business Administration or related major and 4 years experience in the sales, marketing, digital or related professional area; hospitality marketing or digital advertising experience preferred
OR
• 4-year bachelor's degree in Marketing, Public Relations, Business, or related major; 2 years experience in the sales, marketing, digital or related professional area; hospitality marketing or digital advertising agency experience preferred.
CORE WORK ACTIVITIES
Hotel Marketing and Advertising
• Executes annual marketing plan to budget, in consultation with the GM, Food and Beverage leader, Operations leaders, Director of Marketing Communications, and cluster marketing and ecommerce teams.
• Partners with Operations, Food & Beverage and Sales teams to execute promotions and campaigns to target in-house guests with promotions that drive incremental revenue to the hotel.
• Acts as the liaison between the marketing department and advertising agency on the tactical advertising campaigns' creative and media plans, particularly for food and beverage promotions.
• Manages F&B media schedules and verifies prompt settlement of accounts.
• Partners with property Revenue Management to verify correct offer loading, verifying advertisement targeting is correctly directed at relevant consumer groups
• Executes email marketing, and display advertising.
• Maintains frequent, active engagement with Cluster eCommerce manager to verify alignment, pull-through, and 2-way communication about the status, performance evaluation, opportunities, and issues related to online programs and initiatives.
• Verifies all advertising for the hotel in digital channels is in alignment with brand voice.
Social Media Content Management
• Facilitates social media engagement and updating content in local digital channels (e.g., hotel website, travel sites).
• Develops and executes promotions campaign in F&B, weddings, spa, rooms and conferences through relevant digital and social media channels.
• Engages in proactive online reputation management by surfacing relevant guest comments (positive or negative) in social media channels and responds accordingly.
Public Relations and Visual Asset Management
• Develops a comprehensive PR plan per quarter along with agency and and executes post sign-off from GM.
• Maintains a comprehensive list of local media contracts, with particular emphasis on food critics and bloggers.
• Manages assigned accounts as per the media account management system.
• Writes and distributes all press releases for property events, promotions, and outlets.
• Manages the execution of hotel sponsored events, community/government relations activities, and press promotional activities.
• Supports pull through of impactful PR strategy & activities to drive quality press coverage through media engagement, in alignment with communications objectives.
• Verifies the news clippings and other online, print, and social media mention report is completed on a monthly basis for property distribution.
• Manages external vendors and media agencies; works with agency partners and continent PR leader to identify strategic media buys for their hotel(s).
• Surfaces and vets PR leads from the continent PR Leader regarding which are the best media to promote the hotel.
• Supports the co-ordination of photography for F&B advertising, collateral and public relations purposes between the hotel, advertising agency and the regional field marketing teams.
• Manages photo shoots for seasonal or festive promotions in partnership with the cluster or area marketing team.
• Acts as central point of contact for regionally approved local photographers for food, amenity, and property imagery; coordinates with area or cluster marketing to verify all photography adheres to brand voice.
Direct Marketing and Collateral Development
• Coordinates and executes Hotel and F&B printed materials.
• Controls quantity and inventory of all Hotel marketing collateral and verifies copies are filed in a comprehensive manner.
• Assists in the production of all property, F&B display, and temporary signage in hotel public areas.
• Promotes collection of competitors collateral and publicity on a monthly basis.
• Manages the execution of F&B direct marketing activities.
• Verifies all collateral is as per brand standard guidelines and in compliance with Brand Standard Audit (BSA).
General
• Assists and manages the development, co-ordination and execution of all communications activities with a strong emphasis on property F&B promotions and campaigns.
• Helps with the publication of hotel’s newsletter(s).
• Supports communications duties and functions as deemed necessary.
• Assists in the liaison and execution of joint F&B promotions.
• Works with eCommerce to verify the Hotel’s website and related websites are updated on a regular basis.
• Partners with Director of Marketing to create marketing plan aligned to hotel sales and revenue strategy.
• Provides training and marketing leadership and act as a marketing subject matter expert for GMs, Sales Leaders and Managers, and Revenue leaders.
• Coordinates with property and above property eCommerce and Revenue Management teams to report success of property marketing and eCommerce performance.
• Keeps abreast of competition and its collateral, advertising, and marketing efforts and constantly evolving digital and marketing trends.

Title: Marketing Content Executive
Description:
About the Role
We are looking for a creative, energetic and hands-on Marketing& Content Executive to join the Viomi Singapore team under KWH Group.
This is not a purely desk-based marketing role.
You will be involved in bringing the Viomi brand to life in Singapore — creating social media content, developing promotions, supporting roadshows and events, working with KOCs and creators, and capturing real customer experiences.
If you enjoy TikTok and Instagram, like creating content, are comfortable meeting people and want the opportunity to see your ideas turn into real campaigns, this could be the role for you.
What You’ll Be Doing
1. Social Media &Content Creation
· Plan and create engaging content for TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and other relevant platforms
· Conceptualise, shoot and edit short-form videos, including TikToks and Reels
· Create product demos, lifestyle content, customer stories, event highlights and behind-the-scenes content
· Write captions and manage content posting on Viomi Singapore’s official social media accounts
· Keep up with social media trends and bring fresh content ideas to the team
· Track content performance and identify what resonates with our audience
· Build and maintain a content calendar to ensure regular and timely posting
2. Promotions, Roadshows& Events
Viomi participates in consumer fairs, IT shows, mall roadshows and other events throughout the year.
You will:
· Support the planning of promotional calendars, themes and campaign ideas
· Help develop promotional mechanics, giveaways and consumer engagement activities
· Coordinate with agencies on promotional, roadshow and event materials
· Liaise with event organisers and mall management on event locations, booth layouts and requirements
· Support product training and briefing for promoters before events
· Attend selected roadshows and events to capture photos, videos and customer interactions
· Turn event footage into engaging social media content
· Review event and campaign performance with the team and identify areas for improvement
3. KOC & Creator Program
Help us build a community of people who genuinely use, enjoy and talk about our products.
You will:
· Identify and reach out to suitable KOCs, micro-influencers and content creators
· Coordinate collaborations, product installations, content briefs and posting schedules
· Work with creators to develop authentic content that showcases Viomi products and their benefits
· Follow up on content development and posting
· Track the performance of KOC and creator collaborations
· Help identify successful creators and content formats for future campaigns
4. Customer & ProductContent
Some of our best content comes from real customer experiences.
You will attend selected customer installations and product activities to:
· Capture the installation and customer experience through photos and videos
· Film product demonstrations, FAQs and educational content
· Capture customer feedback and testimonials where appropriate
· Turn real customer experiences into useful and engaging social media content
Who We’re Looking For
You could be a great fit if you:
· Love social media and understand platforms such as TikTok and Instagram
· Have a good eye for what makes content interesting and engaging
· Can independently conceptualise, shoot and edit short-form video content
· Are comfortable using tools such as CapCut, Canva, Adobe or similar content-creation tools
· Are willing to work both behind the camera and occasionally appear in content when needed
· Enjoy meeting people and are comfortable interacting with customers, promoters, creators and external partners
· Are organised and able to manage several activities at the same time
· Have good written and spoken English
· Are comfortable experimenting with AI and new digital tools
· Are proactive, resourceful and willing to learn
A Diploma or Degree in Marketing, Communications, Media, Business ora related field would be useful, but your creativity, attitude and portfolio matter more to us.
Fresh graduates are welcome to apply. Candidates with 1–3 years of relevant experience in content creation, social media, marketing, media or agency work are also encouraged to apply.
Knowledge of digital advertising, SEO or paid social media campaigns would be an advantage, but is not essential.
Show Us What You’ve Made
We care more about what you can create than having a fancy portfolio.
If you’ve created TikToks, Reels, videos, photography, school projects or content for your own social accounts, send us a few examples you’re proud of.
Personal projects count too.
Why Join Us?
Viomi is a growing consumer technology brand in Singapore. You’ll have the opportunity to join us at an exciting stage of our development and play a direct role in building the brand locally.
You’ll get hands-on exposure across social media, content creation, consumermarketing, events, roadshows and creator collaborations rather than being limited to one small area of marketing.
You’ll also have the opportunity to:
· Take ownership of content from ideato execution
· Experiment with new content formats and marketing ideas
· Work directly with customers, creators and the wider Viomi team
· See your work go live and measure its impact
· Build a broad marketing portfolio as the brand grows
Working Arrangements
This is a full-time position based in Singapore.
The role includes attending roadshows, consumer events and selected customer installations outside the office.
Occasional weekend work may be required for events and roadshows, with time off in lieu in accordance with company policy.
How to Apply
Please submit your CV together with 3–5 examples of content you’ve created.
These can be TikToks, Reels, videos, photographs, social media posts, school projects, freelance work or content from your own social media accounts.
We’re interested in seeing your ideas, creativity and what you can do.

Title: Marketing Executive
Description:
About Young Hungry Free
Young Hungry Free is a Singapore fashion label founded in 2012, known for edgy basics and wearable trends in sizes XXS to 3XL. A new named collection drops online every Monday at 8pm, and the #YHFAMILY community — members, Telegram subscribers and creators — is at the centre of how the brand grows. We ship from Singapore to customers across the region and beyond.
The role
You will tell the Young Hungry Free story every week. The core of the role is the weekly drop cycle: the content, copy, social publishing and creator seeding that bring each Monday collection to life. Around that, you will help deliver the brand's bigger moments — seasonal and collaboration campaigns, PR and events.
You will lead those bigger moments rather than support them, own media relations, and manage campaign budgets.
What you will do
1. Weekly content and social
Plan and run the content calendar around the Monday 8pm drop: teasers, launch-night content and follow-up.
Write copy for collection launches, product stories, social posts, EDMs and the website, in line with the brand's tone of voice and house style.
Schedule and publish across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and the #YHFAMILY Telegram channel, and manage community comments.
Brief designers, photographers and videographers.
Supply copy and assets for performance and CRM campaigns. The performance and marketing teams own targeting, flows and media buying.
2. Campaigns
Turn campaign strategy into narratives, key messages and visual direction for seasonal, launch and collaboration campaigns.
Coordinate campaign delivery across channels and teams, to agreed timelines.
Lead campaigns from brief to wrap reports.
3. PR and earned media
Maintain the media list, draft press releases and pitches, and manage press seeding.
Track coverage and report on earned media.
Own media relations, including building relationships with editors and handling enquiries.
4. Events and activations
Help plan and run pop-ups, launches and brand events, including vendor coordination and on-the-day delivery.
Lead events from concept to wrap, including vendors and budget.
5. Creators, KOLs and community
Run / Co-run the organic creator and ambassador programme end to end: shortlisting, outreach, product seeding against each drop, briefing and relationship management.
Build a library of user-generated content with written usage permissions.
Ensure all gifted and paid creator content carries the correct disclosure.
Work with the performance team on paid and affiliate creator partnerships, which they co-own.
6. Brand consistency
Apply the brand guidelines across every customer touchpoint, and flag inconsistencies before they go live.
7. Platform, Systems and Channel Management: Content Management Systems, Customer Relationship Management Systems, EDM Tools and Advertising Tools
Plan, execute and improve integrated campaign and marketing initiatives across our different CMS, CRM, EDM, Advertising tools and platforms.
8. Budget and reporting
Track campaign, seeding and event spend against budget, within approval limits set by the Head of Marketing.
Report monthly on content, social, creator and PR performance: what worked, what did not and what to change.
Work closely with performance marketing, CRM, product, operations and customer service.
Take on other duties within the marketing team as needed.
What we are looking for
Essential
Experience at the level you are applying for, ideally in fashion, lifestyle, e-commerce or an agency.
A portfolio showing copy you have written and social content you have produced or managed.
Strong English copywriting, with a sharp ear for tone.
Deep working knowledge of Instagram and TikTok — formats, trends, and what the analytics are telling you.
Experience working with creators or influencers.
A strong visual eye and the ability to give clear campaign, marketing and suggest creative direction together with the creative team.
The organisation to hit a weekly launch deadline, every week.
Comfort reading platform insights and basic web analytics, and turning them into decisions.

Title: Marketing Executive - Immediate
Description:
NLCS (Singapore) believes that each employee makes a significant contribution to our success and that contributions should not be limited by the assigned responsibilities.
Therefore, this position description is designed to outline primary duties, qualifications, and job scope, but not limit the employee, nor NLCS (Singapore), to only the work identified. It is the expectation of the school that each employee will offer his/her services wherever and whenever necessary to ensure the success of our organisation.
Our School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. The School expects all teaching staff, non‐teaching staff and volunteers to share and uphold this commitment.
DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
The Marketing Executive will take ownership of the day-to-day delivery of the School’s marketing activities across campaigns, content, digital, events, partnerships and communications.
Working within the School’s agreed marketing strategy, the role is expected to be proactive, bring forward ideas and opportunities, lead projects through to completion and ensure marketing activity is delivered accurately, consistently and on time.
The role requires someone who can think beyond execution, understand the purpose behind each initiative and recommend practical ways to strengthen the School’s visibility, engagement and admissions objectives.
Main Responsibilities:
1. Campaigns & Marketing Delivery
Lead the day-to-day delivery of agreed marketing campaigns and initiatives.
Proactively propose campaign ideas, themes, content opportunities and improvements.
Develop first drafts of campaign messaging, concepts and supporting content for review.
Own campaign timelines, actions, approvals and follow-ups through to completion.
2. Content, PR & Communications
Develop content for social media, emailers, website, PR, third-party deliverables and marketing materials.
Develop and maintain a regular pipeline of blogs, thought leadership articles, school stories and long-form website content aligned with marketing and admissions priorities.
Proactively identify student, staff, academic, enrichment and community stories.
Develop story angles and content ideas that strengthen the School’s positioning and reputation.
Gather information from academic and non-academic teams and turn it into engaging marketing content.
Support PR opportunities by preparing content, background information, imagery and other required materials.
Identify content opportunities that strengthen the School’s authority and discoverability across SEO, GEO and AEO.
Maintain a forward content pipeline aligned with School marketing and admissions priorities.
3. Digital Presence, Social Media & Website
Own and manage the monthly social media and digital content calendar.
Lead day-to-day social media publishing and content scheduling.
Identify and implement opportunities to improve reach, engagement and content performance.
Monitor comments, messages and online engagement, escalating sensitive matters where appropriate.
Keep website content, imagery, event information and downloadable materials accurate and current.
Identify areas of the website requiring updates or improvements and take them forward with the relevant teams.
Support the continuous development of the School’s digital presence through SEO, GEO and AEO, including website content, blogs, FAQs, landing pages and other relevant content.
Identify and recommend content and website improvements based on search behaviour, emerging queries and marketing priorities.
Work with relevant internal and external teams to ensure content is structured and optimised for traditional search engines and AI-led discovery platforms.
Monitor organic visibility, website engagement and content performance and recommend areas for improvement.
4. Events & Community Marketing
Own the marketing requirements for admissions events, Open Houses, education fairs, community activities and outreach initiatives.
Develop event promotion plans and ensure digital, creative, signage, collateral and content requirements are delivered on time.
Review and maintain the Marketing Events Calendar and plan marketing activity sufficiently in advance.
Support live content and social media coverage at key events.
Identify content opportunities from events for future marketing use.
5. Brand, Collateral & Multimedia
Ensure approved brand guidelines are consistently followed across marketing materials and touchpoints.
Lead the development and production of routine marketing and event collateral.
Review materials for accuracy, consistency and quality before production or publication.
Identify photography and videography requirements for campaigns and key School events.
Brief and manage routine requirements with photographers, videographers, designers and production suppliers as required.
Maintain an organised and current library of photography, video and marketing assets.
Ensure appropriate student photography, filming permissions and safeguarding requirements are followed.
6. Partnerships, Listings & Marketing Opportunities
Research and recommend relevant third-party platforms, editorial listings, directories, partnerships and marketing opportunities for annual engagement.
Identify opportunities that support SEO, GEO and AEO visibility, brand awareness and lead generation.
Maintain and regularly review School profiles across education portals, directories and external listings.
Support delivery of agreed marketing requirements for partnerships and external collaborations.
Ensure partner branding and marketing assets remain consistent with School guidelines.
Monitor agreed third-party deliverables and ensure required content and assets are supplied within deadlines.

Prepare quarterly marketing reports covering campaigns, social media, website activity, digital visibility and other agreed performance metrics, working with relevant team members to consolidate inputs.
Maintain and develop trackers and reports for management review, internal planning and marketing strategy alignment.
Maintain accurate marketing trackers, calendars and project records.
Obtain supplier quotations and manage routine production requirements within approved parameters.
Track supplier deliverables, timelines and quality, escalating issues where required.
Maintain records of marketing expenditure, purchase requests, invoices and associated documentation.
Maintain appropriate stock levels of marketing collateral, branded materials and event assets.

Build strong working relationships with Admissions, Academic Teams, Events, Partnerships and Business Development, Parent Engagement, Finance and other School departments.
Take ownership of agreed marketing requests and ensure they are followed through to completion.
Manage competing deadlines and escalate priorities where appropriate.

Title: Marketing Manager
Description:
BullionStar has no shortage of things worth marketing. We sell physical gold and silver, operate a market leading bullion centre and vaults across three countries, have an active and highly engaged customer base, and sit in an industry that is rarely short of something to talk about. What we need is someone to bring it all together.
As Marketing Manager, you will own the marketing plan and turn it into campaigns across social, email, content, PR, the website and our physical bullion centre. You will decide what we should be talking about, how we should talk about it, where it should appear, and how the different pieces come together. This is not a role where you will be handed a marketing plan to execute, you will help shape it with the Deputy CEO, and the wider team. What we need from you is the judgement to spot a good opportunity, know what to do with it, and turn it into marketing that works.
Who we are
BullionStar is Singapore’s leading precious metals dealer. We sell, buy back, store, and deliver physical gold, silver, and platinum to customers worldwide – from first-time buyers to institutional investors. We operate a full-service showroom in Singapore, a comprehensive e-commerce platform, and vault storage facilities across multiple jurisdictions.
We are independently owned, founder-led, and intentionally lean. There are no layers of corporate bureaucracy here. Decisions are made quickly, everyone is close to the customer, and every person in the business has a direct impact on what we deliver. We’ve built our reputation on trust, transparency, and doing things properly.
We’re looking for people who are drawn to that kind of environment – people who want ownership, not job titles, and who find energy in building something rather than maintaining something.
One thing to know about our audience: they are sceptics by temperament. They distrust banks, they distrust hype, and they will distrust us the moment we sound like an ad. The marketing that works here earns attention with substance.
What you will do
- Strategy. A real marketing plan: which audiences, what message, which channels, what calendar, and why. Shaped with the Deputy CEO, the wider team, and owned and executed by you.
- Campaigns. Product launches, limited time offers, seasonal pushes and competitions across digital, social, email and the store itself. The idea, the assets, the timing and the follow-through are yours.
- Social and community. With our creatives, drive what we do on X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and LinkedIn: the calendar, the formats and the growth. Show up where people already talk about gold and silver too: Reddit, forums and comment sections. Answer questions genuinely, understand what people care about, and bring those insights back into our marketing.
- Email. The programme end-to-end: calendar, segments, offers, copy, send, and the honest read on what it returned. Every send must earn the next one.
- Creative and content direction. Photography, video, graphics, ad creative and written content. You will not be behind the camera all day, but you will be the reason the work is good: the briefs, the direction, the feedback and the standard. You will also have real input into how bullionstar.com itself develops.
- Media relations. Be proactive with PR. Spot the opportunity, whether it is a journalist’s query, a news moment or a story worth pitching, and find the way to make it happen and land well.
- Analytics. We have an unusually deep warehouse of order and campaign data, plus analytics support. Know which campaigns moved product, which did not, and feed that into the next plan.
- The thread. Product, the shop floor, editorial, social, email, website: someone must make the post, the email, the site banner and the shop window feel like one campaign.
Who you are
- Campaigns directed, not just contributed to. Walk us through one from strategy to results: the audience, the idea, what you made, what you directed and what happened. More than once and across more than one channel.
- Excellent written and spoken English. This one is absolute. Plans that persuade, copy that sells without sounding like it, and the same standard out loud. Nothing else on this list can offset it. Your application is your first writing sample.
- E-commerce experience. You have marketed products that people buy online and understand the whole journey from first impression to landing page to checkout and repeat purchase. You think about the campaign and the buying experience as one thing and understand that getting attention is only useful if something happens afterwards.
- Social and email as crafts, not distribution channels. You understand how each platform works. Follower counts you inherited do not count; things you made that travelled do. You have also run an EDM programme yourself and can show what it returned.
- Understanding of brand and customer. Your creative judgement is grounded in who we are and who buys from us, not personal taste. You can explain the call to someone who disagrees.
- Genuinely inquisitive. You do not need to arrive knowing the difference between a kilobar and a collectible coin, but you should want to. Nobody hands you a syllabus here. You teach yourself the business, the industry, the products and the customers because you want to know, and it shows up in the work.
- You see the opportunity in the product. Gold and silver are unusual things to market. They are valuable, physical, visual and surrounded by history, markets, politics, manufacturing, collecting and some very opinionated customers. Then there are the vaults, the shop floor, the deliveries and the moments when the price moves and the shop suddenly fills up. You notice those things and instinctively start thinking about what we could do with them.
- You pay attention to the market. You know what our competitors are doing, what they are doing well and where they are getting it wrong. You look beyond bullion too, learning from the best ideas in e-commerce and other industries. You do not copy for the sake of it, but you are always watching, learning and thinking about what we could do better.
- Creative judgement. You have made enough yourself, whether video, image, layout or ad, to know quickly when something is not good enough and to explain why.
- Commercial instinct. You care about reach, engagement and brand, but you know they are not the result. Marketing here ultimately must attract customers, sell metal and grow the business. You naturally ask what something cost, what it returned and whether we should do it again.
- The whole digital picture. You understand SEO, paid media, attribution and conversion well enough to see how they fit together, even where specialists run the channel. You are comfortable enough with numbers to judge your own campaigns honestly.
- Media relations. You know how to spot a story worth pitching, deal with journalists and turn something happening in the business or the market into an opportunity.
- Based in Singapore. This is an on-site role at New Bridge Road. We work in the same room. And when we are busy, everyone gets stuck in the shop, the customers, the vault. An afternoon on the shop floor can teach you more than a month of dashboards.

This role sits at the intersection of talent, campaigns and performance. You will lead a team Athlete & Influencer Performance Executives across Australia and Singapore/Malaysia, signing and managing talent, building campaigns, negotiating deals and proving the return on every dollar invested.
Reporting to the Global Director of Marketing, you will play a pivotal role in building our new global marketing hub in Singapore and Malaysia.
Content is king, but distribution is the kingdom.
Success in this role means a high-performing roster, a campaign every week, and athlete and influencer partnerships that generate demand, customers and revenue.
Responsibilities:
- Drive Athlete & Influencer Performance: Plan and run 52 athlete- and influencer-led campaigns a year across North America, driving e-commerce revenue through discount codes, email acquisition and @OxyShred follower growth.
- Lead Campaigns & Launches: Own the talent layer of major brand campaigns, product launches and retail moments, with integrated plans across social, content, paid media, retail and e-commerce.
- Own TikTok Reach & Frequency: Set the strategy and brief for TikTok Reach & Frequency campaigns that drive awareness and retail velocity around launches.
- Scale Winning Content: Identify top-performing organic content fast, push it to Paid Media for amplification, and keep a steady pipeline of creative ready for paid.
- Build & Lead the Team: Hire 4 new executives in Singapore/Malaysia, coach the team against clear commercial KPIs, and run a weekly pipeline and performance cadence across both offices.
- Negotiate Talent Partnerships: Recruit athletes and influencers who fit our target consumer, and negotiate deals end to end, including fees, deliverables, exclusivity, usage rights and renewals.
- Manage the Roster for Return: Benchmark rates, track performance, cut or renegotiate underperforming partnerships, and move investment to the strongest performers.
- Report & Optimise: Report campaign and roster performance weekly to the Global Director of Marketing, using data to sharpen briefs, hooks, talent selection and creative.
About you:
- Proven experience leading athlete, influencer or creator marketing programs with clear commercial outcomes.
- Experience leading, hiring and performance-managing a team, ideally across multiple locations.
- Strong negotiator with experience in talent contracts, usage rights and exclusivity.
- Deep understanding of TikTok, Instagram and short-form content that drives both attention and sales.
- Commercially minded and comfortable owning revenue, ROI and budgets.
- Confident reading performance data and making fast decisions from it.
- Experience with paid social amplification and the North American market is highly desirable.
- Comfortable challenging talent, agencies and internal teams when performance isn’t good enough.
- Passionate about fitness, wellness and consumer brands.

Title: Marketing Manager - APAC
Description:
Who We Are
We’re not in the wing business. We’re in the flavor business. It’s been our mission to Serve the World Flavor since we first opened in 1994, and we’re just getting started. 1997 saw the opening of our first brand partner operated Wingstop location, and by 2002 we had served the world one billion wings. It’s flavor that defines us and has made Wingstop one of the fastest growing brands in the restaurant industry.
Above all else – our success is largely due to our people and our core values, or what we call The Wingstop Way of being entrepreneurial, service-minded, fun, and authentic. We believe having a strong people foundation centered on these collective values creates a crave-worthy culture and talented team, as well as ensures our brand is poised for accelerated growth. We all win together.
What We’ll Need
We are seeking a Marketing Manager - APAC to help drive brand growth, support our franchise partners, and execute best-in-class regional marketing initiatives across Asia Pacific. This role will partner closely with the Director, Marketing - APAC to implement regional marketing strategies, launch new market initiatives, and strengthen brand performance across existing and emerging markets.
The ideal candidate is passionate about brand building, thrives in a fast-paced international environment, and enjoys collaborating with cross-functional teams and franchise partners to deliver measurable business results.
- Partner with the Director, Marketing - APAC to execute regional marketing strategies that drive same-store sales, guest traffic, brand awareness, and restaurant growth.
- Support marketing launches across existing and emerging APAC markets, ensuring consistent execution of campaigns, promotions, and brand standards.
- Coordinate the development and execution of integrated 360° marketing campaigns across digital, social, media, PR, and in-store channels.
- Assist in building annual marketing calendars and field marketing plans aligned with regional business priorities.
- Support the planning and execution of Limited Time Offers (LTOs), menu innovation launches, and seasonal campaigns.
- Work closely with franchise partners to provide marketing guidance, review local marketing plans, and share best practices.
- Coordinate with creative, media, digital, and agency partners to ensure timely delivery of marketing initiatives.
- Monitor campaign performance and marketing effectiveness through analysis of sales, guest insights, media performance, and ROI.
- Gather and communicate consumer insights, competitive intelligence, and industry trends to support future marketing strategies.
- Partner with cross-functional teams including Operations, Supply Chain, Development, Finance, and Brand to successfully execute marketing initiatives.
- Assist with new restaurant openings by coordinating local marketing plans and launch activities.
- Support regional digital marketing initiatives including CRM, loyalty, delivery platforms, social media, and digital ordering.
- Manage marketing budgets for assigned projects while ensuring efficient use of resources.
- Help maintain marketing assets, promotional calendars, and project timelines across the region.
- Contribute to regional brand projects, creative development, pricing analysis, and marketing research as needed.
- Build collaborative relationships with franchise partners while serving as a trusted marketing resource.
- Identify opportunities to improve processes, marketing effectiveness, and franchise support.
What You’ll Need
- 5–8 years of marketing experience, preferably within QSR, retail, hospitality, or consumer brands.
- Experience supporting multi-unit or franchise businesses.
- Experience managing integrated marketing campaigns from planning through execution.
- Experience working across multiple countries or markets is preferred.
- A bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related field.
- Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
- A proactive mindset and willingness to take ownership.
- The ability to adapt quickly within a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Experience interpreting marketing performance metrics and consumer insights.
- Excellent communication and presentation skills.
- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
- The ability to influence stakeholders across cultures and functions.
Who You Are
No job is too small. You recognize that the real work happens in the restaurants, and everything we do should support their success. You stay humble, roll up your sleeves, and always look for ways to help. You learn from others and contribute wherever you can.
You care deeply about doing great work and driving results. You’re curious, ask questions, and seek out opportunities to improve. You don’t just point out problems—you bring solutions, ideas, and perspectives that move the team forward.
You take full responsibility for your work and see things through to completion. You aren’t afraid to fail because you know that failure is a part of learning and growth. You take action, move fast, and keep pushing forward.
You lead with empathy, respect, and emotional intelligence. You collaborate effectively, fostering a culture of trust and constructive feedback. You understand the importance of teamwork and ensure that your actions build others up rather than break them down.
You push yourself and others to be better. You embrace healthy conflict, knowing that great ideas and strong teams emerge from honest, constructive conversations. You believe that leaders create leaders and are committed to fostering a culture of growth, challenge, and continuous improvement.

- Business travel accident coverage

Description:
Additional Information
