Title: Assistant Director
Description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION
Montfort Care is a vibrant workplace with a supportive culture where collaboration and camaraderie thrive. Our teams are highly cooperative, and colleagues genuinely care for each other. We celebrate diversity and innovation, united by our three core values: Resonance, Ingenuity and Stronger Together.
Expect a dynamic and fast-paced environment, as we are in an exciting phase of growth. Success here requires adaptability, agility, and the ability to navigate complexity. Our people stay with us because they find a strong sense of purpose and community, enjoying the opportunity to make a tangible difference in people's lives.
We offer a flexible work environment that values the importance of personal and professional growth. With plenty of opportunities for continuous learning and development, Montfort Care is an ideal place for those who want to grow their careers while contributing to meaningful change.
Join us to be part of an amazing team that's dedicated to making a difference and having fun while doing that!
RESPONSIBILITIES
The Strategy & Growth team is an organisation-wide capability-building function for Montfort Care (MFC), partnering with leaders and teams to address the organisation's most complex and pressing challenges. It combines strategic thinking, transformation expertise and implementation to strengthen organisational capabilities and achieve sustainable impact.
The
Assistant Director
, Transformation leads organisation-wide transformation initiatives that improve service effectiveness, operational efficiency and client experience. Reporting to the Director, Strategy & Growth, the role has a strong focus on rethinking service delivery through digital means while ensuring that services remain accessible and inclusive for clients who may face barriers to digital adoption. The portfolio also includes non-digital aspects that enable digital service delivery, including service redesign, process improvement, operating model changes and new ways of working.
Working closely with the Director, Strategy & Growth, leadership, service leaders and corporate service functions, the Assistant Director identifies high-value digital transformation opportunities and leads initiatives from discovery and business case development through experimentation, implementation, adoption and benefits realisation. The role applies user-centred, agile and data-informed approaches to translate organisational and client needs into scalable solutions.
The
Assistant Director
, Transformation develops the internal capabilities required to sustain new ways of working. The role champions responsible experimentation, digital confidence and continuous improvement, ensuring that transformation strengthens outcomes for clients and employees without leaving digitally less-confident users behind.
This is a high-visibility role with frequent opportunities to engage and present to the Chief Executive Officer and leadership team. The
Assistant Director
must understand strategic intent, exercise sound judgement and translate broad direction into coherent priorities, practical action plans and measurable outcomes. The role offers an opportunity for a transformation practitioner to step into a wider organisational remit and make a significant contribution to Montfort Care's service and organisational outcomes.
Organisation Strategy Alignment and Transformation Planning
Partner with leadership, service leaders, employees and clients to define the future of social service delivery and identify the operating models, capabilities and transformation priorities required to realise it.
Define measurable outcomes and benefits for transformation initiatives, including improvements in client experience, service effectiveness, employee productivity, adoption, accessibility, efficiency and cost, and establish mechanisms to track benefits from baseline through implementation and scale-up.
Lead research, horizon scanning and analysis of client needs, sector developments, emerging technologies and new service delivery models. Translate findings into clear opportunity statements and evidence-based recommendations for leadership consideration.
Work with leadership to shape and prioritise a portfolio of digital and non-digital transformation initiatives based on strategic relevance, client and employee value, feasibility, inclusion, risk, resource requirements and expected benefits.
Facilitating annual/ multi-year strategic planning cycles. Lead secretariat function to organize MFC's annual work plan; this includes pre-retreat planning, conduct of retreats, and organising of cascade briefs to middle managers and front liners.
Transformation Project Management
Map out and track transformation project progress against MFC's strategic objectives to ensure alignment of transformation projects to broader organisational goals.
Establish governance structure for identified transformation projects based on organisation priorities; e.g. project organisation, project charter, timelines, resources, and accountability.
Engage stakeholders to build understanding of transformation objectives and drive ownership of transformation objectives by service pillars.
Diagnose broad or ambiguous symptoms, frame clear problem statements and identify root causes through data analysis, user research and process mapping. Conceptualise and implement fit-for-purpose responses, which may include service redesign, digital solutions, process improvement, operating model or organisation structure changes, capability development, and leadership or culture interventions.
Coach and guide Transformation team and Service Pillar Heads on transformation frameworks, methodologies, change management approaches and best practices. Support leadership in resolving organisation-wide structural, operational, or cultural barriers to transformation success.
Together with Service Pillar Heads, Transformation team, Communications team, drive change management strategies to enable success of transformation projects.
Track and manage transformation project progress and risks to ensure timely delivery of transformation milestones.
Design and deliver a tiered digital capability programme that can be scaled across more than 400 employees, covering foundational digital literacy, role-specific skills and advanced capabilities for digital champions. Develop playbooks, communities of practice, coaching and practical learning interventions that build a digital-first culture while supporting employees with different levels of confidence and readiness.
Experimentation and scaling
Lead research, experimentation and pilots for new ways of delivering services. Define hypotheses and success measures, test solutions with employees and clients, evaluate evidence and risks, and recommend whether initiatives should be stopped, refined or scaled.
Vendor Management
Build and manage partnerships with technology providers, social service agencies, public-sector bodies, research institutions and other ecosystem partners or vendors to co-develop and deliver transformation initiatives. Establish clear outcomes, governance, responsibilities and performance measures for joint projects.
Manage and track KPIs of vendors to ensure service delivered meet our contractual needs.
Funding Management
Research relevant grants and funding opportunities, and develop use cases and applications that support digital and broader transformation initiatives. Manage funding commitments, budgets, milestones, reporting and benefit measures to ensure compliance and intended outcomes.
Plan yearly departmental budget and be accountable for the expenditure of these funds in support of MFC organisational objectives.
People Management
Lead and develop strategy and transformation teams to drive delivery of organisational objectives.
Foster a culture of innovation in the team to meet social mission and objectives.
Risk and Compliance
Understand IPC (Institute of Public Character) and charity organisations compliance and regulatory requirements and ensure adherence.
Identify and manage transformation risks, including data protection, cybersecurity, accessibility, ethical use of technology, vendor dependency, service continuity and unintended exclusion of clients. Work with relevant corporate service functions and funders to ensure that initiatives meet applicable regulatory, security and governance requirements.
Others
Responsibilities listed above are not exhaustive. From time to time, additional duties or projects may be assigned based on organisational needs.
QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor's degree from a recognised institution of higher learning in business, information technology, information systems, engineering, social sciences, public policy, organisational development or a related discipline. An advanced degree in business administration, information technology or a related field is advantageous.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, Change management certifications (e.g. Prosci) is advantageous but not mandatory.
At least 7-10 years of progressive experience in management consulting, internal transformation, service design, digital transformation, innovation or major programme delivery, including demonstrated experience leading digital initiatives from problem de nition through implementation and adoption.
Prior experience in a major technology company, digital consultancy or technology-enabled organisation, with responsibility for delivering digital products or initiatives for internal or external users.
Experience in social sector, healthcare, or mission-driven organisations is advantageous. Candidates from other sectors with an interest in driving the change in the social service sector are encouraged to apply.
3-5 years of leading teams or major workstreams with a demonstrated ability to drive organisation-wide strategy and transformation projects. Hands-on experience in driving transformation planning, stakeholder engagement and governance.
Experience working with data, KPI, OKRs, dashboarding for reporting for leadership teams. Experience in driving process redesign, operating model/ organisation structure, skilling strategy, leadership and culture initiatives.
Demonstrated ability to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives, establish priorities based on organisational needs and delivery capacity, and build alignment across service, corporate and technology stakeholders.
Ability to lead concurrent initiatives using an agile, test-and-learn mindset while maintaining disciplined governance over scope, priorities, interdependencies, resources, risks and delivery commitments. The candidate must be able to adapt the approach when evidence or organisational needs change without allowing uncontrolled scope expansion.
Strong analytical ability & problem-solving skills to identify critical areas for action in a data-informed manner.
Executive presence and sound judgement to engage senior leadership, challenge assumptions constructively and in uence decisions, combined with the ability to explain complex transformation and digital concepts to frontline employees and non-technical stakeholders to build understanding and commitment.
Please note that your application will be sent to and reviewed by the direct employer - Montfort Care

Title: Assistant Director, Finance
Description:
About the Opportunity
Our client is an established organisation in Singapore with a sizeable and growing operational footprint. As part of its continued development, the organisation is looking to strengthen its Finance function and drive greater efficiency, standardisation and digitalisation across its finance operations.
This is a leadership role for an experienced finance professional who combines strong operational finance fundamentals with a track record in finance transformation. The successful candidate will oversee key finance operations while driving process improvements, automation and stronger controls across the function.
Key Responsibilities
Finance Operations & Governance
Oversee key finance operations including billing, Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, General Ledger and Fixed Assets.
Ensure accurate and timely financial processing, reconciliations and month-end activities.
Strengthen financial controls, policies and standard operating procedures to support good governance and compliance.
Oversee relevant funding and grant-related finance processes where applicable.
Support internal and external audits and ensure appropriate follow-up on audit and control matters.
Finance Transformation & Process Improvement
Lead finance transformation initiatives aimed at improving efficiency, scalability and controls across Finance.
Drive the review and redesign of finance processes, identifying opportunities for standardisation, simplification and automation.
Play a key role in ERP and finance system implementation or enhancement projects, working closely with internal stakeholders and external partners.
Champion the use of workflow automation, RPA and other digital tools to improve finance operations.
Develop appropriate operational metrics and reporting to improve visibility and performance across the function.
Leadership & Stakeholder Management
Lead, coach and develop finance managers and team members, building stronger capabilities within the function.
Partner with internal stakeholders to address operational issues and support organisation-wide initiatives.
Work closely with senior management and cross-functional teams on finance transformation, governance and process improvement matters.

Title: Assistant Director, Strategy, Public Sector Transformation, PSD
Description:
The Challenge
The Public Service operates in an increasingly complex environment shaped by changing citizen expectations, workforce shifts, technological disruption and greater interdependence across agencies. Public Sector Transformation (PST) seeks to ensure that the Singapore Public Service remains future-ready, effective and trusted by continually reimagining how the Public Service works, develops its workforce and organises itself.
The PST Cluster leads and coordinates Whole-of-Government transformation. Its role spans setting the vision and strategic direction for PST, catalysing deep organisational and business transformation, building the capabilities and ecosystem needed to sustain change, applying AI to the key challenges of today and mobilising leaders and officers around a shared transformation agenda.
As Assistant Director (Strategy), you will provide strategic and organisational leadership across key PST strategic portfolios, covering sensemaking, conceptualising, catalyst and mobilising workstreams. You will translate emerging priorities and senior leadership direction into coherent strategies, governance arrangements, programmes and resourcing approaches that enable transformation across the Public Service.
This is both a strategy and delivery role. You will work at the intersection of policy, organisational transformation, innovation, technology, workforce capability and public-sector governance, while leading teams to turn broad and often ambiguous ambitions into practical, coordinated action.
Key Responsibilities
As a Team Lead to a team of 3-5 officers, you will:
A. Set and steward the strategic direction for Public Sector Transformation
Lead the development and continual refinement of the overarching PST strategy, identifying the major shifts required for the Public Service to remain effective and future-ready.
Synthesise emerging operating-environment trends, ground sentiment, organisational data and agency experience to surface strategic priorities and areas requiring Whole-of-Government intervention.
Translate senior leadership direction into clear transformation outcomes, priorities, implementation pathways and narratives for agencies, leaders and officers.
Ensure PST priorities remain aligned with broader Whole-of-Government, Centre-of-Government and Public Service priorities.
Oversee the monitoring and reporting of PST progress, surfacing key achievements, implementation challenges and areas requiring leadership attention.
B. Lead cross-cutting and AI-enabled transformation
Shape and coordinate major cross-cutting transformation priorities requiring joint ownership across policy, technology, workforce and corporate-function stakeholders.
Provide strategic leadership for AI-enabled PST, ensuring technology adoption is connected to business and workflow redesign, organisational change, workforce implications and measurable outcomes.
Work with functional and mission leads to identify high-impact transformation opportunities, define the desired picture of success and establish coherent governance and tracking arrangements.
Develop proposals for the capabilities, funding, headcount and specialist support needed to implement transformation at scale.
C. Shape resourcing, governance and implementation arrangements
Design governance and operating arrangements that clarify accountability, enable timely decisions and provide progress assurance without imposing unnecessary process.
Develop and evaluate funding and manpower proposals for Whole-of-Government transformation initiatives, working with finance and policy partners to align transformation funding with strategic outcomes.
Establish portfolio-level measures, review mechanisms and reporting arrangements that support learning and course correction.
D. Mobilise and align Whole-of-Government partners
Build trusted relationships with Centre-of-Government partners, ministries, statutory boards, transformation offices and delivery agencies.
Convene stakeholders around shared outcomes, particularly where responsibilities and resources are distributed across organisations.
Develop engagement approaches across multiple levels, from senior leadership forums to working-level communities and agency visits.
E. Lead teams and manage an evolving portfolio
Review and assure the quality of key products, including strategies, submissions, briefs, programme designs and senior-leadership materials.
Build a collaborative, high-performing team culture that is comfortable with ambiguity, experimentation and constructive challenge.
Requirements
We are looking for someone who is curious about the future of government, passionate about AI and innovation, and excited to work with diverse stakeholders to shape meaningful transformation across the Public Service.
You enjoy solving complex problems, thrive in collaborative environments and are motivated by turning ideas into practical impact. Whether developing AI-enabled initiatives, building partnerships or supporting innovation programmes, you are driven by a desire to improve outcomes for citizens and public officers alike.
Key Competencies
1. Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgement
o You consider stakeholder needs as well as short- and long-term implications in proposing solutions.
o You make sound judgements about different policy options by synthesising various data points and using a good sense of realities on the ground.
o You anticipate and prepare for queries from stakeholders when operationalising solutions.
2. Serving with Heart, Commitment and Purpose
o You guide your team to demonstrate care and empathy in delivering services to citizens and stakeholders.
o You are a role model of, and ensure that your team upholds, the Public Service values in the course of their work.
o You are a role model of resilience and bouncing back from adversity.
o You orchestrate resources and monitor your team’s progress towards deliverables.
o You ensure that your team delivers with high standards and you take responsibility for their collective performance.
3. Working Effectively with External Stakeholders
o You reconcile different opinions and approaches to maintain a constructive partnership with stakeholders.
o You proactively identify opportunities for collaboration with stakeholders to advance a common good.
o You anticipate and manage critical stakeholder issues with patience, humility and timeliness.
4. Stewarding Systems for Today and Tomorrow
o You willingly remove outdated practices and actively explore digital technology and tools to simplify work processes.
o You implement good knowledge management practices to retain and transfer knowledge within your team.
o You enforce measures to safeguard data.
Functional Competencies
5. AI and Digital Transformation
o You understand AI, Generative AI and other digital technologies, and appreciate their potential applications within the public sector.
o You leverage AI and digital technologies, including Generative AI, to improve productivity, redesign workflows and enhance service delivery.
o You translate business needs into practical AI-enabled solutions by balancing user needs, technical feasibility and organisational priorities.
o You demonstrate an understanding of AI governance, data management and responsible AI practices, and apply these principles when designing and implementing AI-enabled initiatives.
o You keep abreast of emerging technologies and continuously identify opportunities to strengthen AI adoption across the Public Service.
Relevant Experience and Track Record
Relevant experience in several of the following areas would be advantageous:
Public-sector strategy or policy
Cross-agency or Centre-of-Government coordination
Organisational transformation or organisational development
Digital or AI-enabled transformation
Innovation and ecosystem development
Capability development
A strong track record of leading complex and ambiguous work, influencing senior stakeholders, developing teams and translating strategy into implementation would be essential. Candidates with at least 3 years of supervisory experience managing small teams in a collaborative environment will be viewed favourably.

Title: Assistant Manager / Manager, Corporate & Industry Partnerships
Description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION
NVPC is the national agency dedicated to growing a culture of volunteerism and philanthropy in Singapore. By engaging individuals, organisations, communities and leaders across the people, private and public sectors, we seek to create a more caring, inclusive, and compassionate society. Together, we envision Singapore as a City of Good, where everyone is able to give every day and everywhere (3Es), contributing their time, talent, treasure, ties and testimony (5Ts). Learn more at nvpc.org.sg.
RESPONSIBILITIES
This role sits in NVPC's Corporate and Industry Partnerships (CIP) department, which drives the Company of Good (COG) initiative — a national platform that supports and recognises companies in Singapore to integrate purpose and social impact into their core business strategies.
Today, there are over 1,000 recognised Companies of Good, helping businesses translate purpose into action across five key impact areas: People, Society, Governance, Environment, and Economic.
As the anchor for this work, NVPC's CIP department plays a pivotal role in shaping and strengthening Singapore's corporate purpose ecosystem — catalysing partnerships and collective impact, with the business community as a driving force for a stronger Singapore.
We are now seeking a purpose-driven and impact-led individual to help advance this national momentum — where both meaningful programme delivery and growing awareness of COG will increasingly become key levers for scaling impact.
In this role, you will support the design, execution and evaluation of programmes and platforms that encourage companies to give and volunteer more, as they embed purpose and impact into how they operate.
Your core work will centre on three key areas: (1) strengthening corporate capabilities in social impact, (2) building and growing the Company of Good community, and (3) scaling impact programmes.
This role works closely with colleagues across CIP to understand what companies are experiencing on the ground, and uses that insight to continuously refine our programmes — ensuring the overall Company of Good journey for firms remains relevant and valuable, not just individual initiatives in isolation.
Strengthen Corporate Capabilities in Social Impact
- Support the planning and delivery of our leadership development programmes — spanning different leadership audiences — to enable organisations to volunteer and/or donate better - as one reflection of corporates' purpose journeys
- Proactively cultivate new leads through targeted publicity and peer referrals
- Follow through (and improve) processes that will create powerful and valuable experiences for participants
Build and Grow the Community
- Support the design and facilitation of community-building and engagement efforts within the Company of Good ecosystem e.g. peer learning, networking events, and platforms for programme alumni to connect, share, and deepen their contributions
- Support the development and implementation of community engagement and growth strategies
Scale Impact Programmes
- Support the planning and delivery of NVPC's flagship corporate volunteering programme and ensure it remains relevant to corporates
- Cultivate potential leads and enable corporates to participate in our volunteering programme
- Respond to and fulfil requests from corporates seeking support in their corporate volunteering journey
- Gather insights and feedback from existing partners to identify opportunities to strengthen programme design, delivery and impact QUALIFICATIONS
- Bachelor's Degree in Business, Communications, Social Sciences, or a related discipline
- ACTA or WSQ Advanced Certificate in Learning and Performance (ACLP) qualification is advantageous
- Experience in managing multiple concurrent projects and working across different departments and teams
- Comfortable forging and growing corporate partnerships to deepen organisations' engagement with NVPC
- Ability to gather and synthesise input from colleagues and stakeholders to inform programme design and improvement, rather than working in a silo
- A collaborative mindset; experience in partnerships and stakeholder engagement is an advantage
- Ability to communicate clearly and concisely, both verbally and in writing
- Comfortable navigating ambiguity and uncertainty while keeping an eye on outcomes
- Exposure to ESG, sustainability, or social and community impact initiatives is an advantage Please note that your application will be sent to and reviewed by the direct employer - National Volunteer & Philanthropy Centre

Title: Assistant Manager, B2B & Physical Channel Growth
Description:
Position:
Assistant Manager, B2B & Physical Channel Growth
At Dr Mark Leong Team, we are more than a weight loss company- we are a community united by one mission: to support ladies above 40 to become fitter, stronger, healthier, and more confident as they age.
We understand that losing weight after 40 is different. Changes in metabolism, hormones, muscle mass, lifestyle, and nutrition can make it increasingly difficult to achieve results using the same methods that worked when we were younger.
That is why we focus on helping our community understand their body, nutrition, food choices, movement, and lifestyle - so that weight loss is not simply about seeing a smaller number on the weighing scale, but about building a stronger and healthier body for the years ahead.
We believe people deserve clarity, not guesswork.
Through education, practical nutrition strategies, community support, and technology, we help our members make better choices that can become part of their everyday lives.
Most importantly, we believe transformation is easier when you do not have to do it alone.
We are building a community where women can learn together, progress together, encourage one another, and celebrate every milestone - from losing weight and becoming fitter to gaining strength, confidence, and a better quality of life.
As the Dr Mark Leong community continues to grow across Asia and beyond, we are looking for passionate, energetic, andmission-driven individuals to join our team and help us create meaningful transformation - one woman, one family, and one community at a time.
We are looking for a commercially driven B2B & PhysicalChannel Growth team member whose primary responsibility is to build DML’s offline business into a profitable, repeatable and scalable revenue channel.
This is a business development and sales growth role, not an event coordination or administrative role.

Prospect and develop new B2B customers.
Identify corporate wellness, bulk purchase and corporate gifting opportunities.
Conduct meetings and presentations with prospective customers.
Prepare proposals and quotations.
Follow up opportunities through to conversion.
Develop existing customers into repeat accounts.
Identify opportunities to increase order size and product range.
Maintain an active B2B sales pipeline.
Achieve the monthly B2B revenue target.

Source opportunities at malls, hospitals, schools, offices, bazaars, wellness events and community locations.
Evaluate footfall, customer profile, rental costs and sales potential.
Negotiate with venue operators and organisers.
Develop a forward calendar of physical sales opportunities.
Set revenue and box targets before each activation.
Monitor sales performance and take action when targets are not being achieved.

Take ownership of the successful commercial execution of each activation.
Coordinate:
Venue and organiser requirements
Booth/display setup
Signage and promotional materials
Inventory and replenishment
Payment systems
Sampling and promotions
Manpower/ DF deployment
Logistics
Daily sales and inventory reporting

Develop additional offline channels for DML products.
Identify suitable:
Clinics
TCM centres
Gyms and fitness centres
Wellness centres
Health retailers
Corporate offices
Community businesses
Other relevant physical outlets

Develop recurring physical sales opportunities through organisations and communities.
Potential channels include:
Hospitals
Schools and universities
Corporates
Fitness communities
Yoga and wellness groups
Sports communities
Associations
Community organisations

Identify suitable DFs for pop-ups and roadshows.
Train DFs on physical selling.
Develop sales scripts and operating SOPs.
Provide product and promotional guidance.
Establish inventory and reporting processes.
Test different physical selling formats.
Identify successful models and replicate them.
Progressively hand suitable locations and activations to DFs.

Physical channels should generate more than immediate product sales.
Capture and qualify potential:
B2B customers
Corporate accounts
Affiliates
DFs
MLC customers
AI Summit prospects
Strategic partners
8. Account Management & Repeat Business
Build recurring revenue from existing customers and partners.
Maintain relationships with key accounts.
Follow up for replenishment and repeat orders.
Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities.
Develop recurring corporate programmes where appropriate.
Monitor customer performance and buying patterns.
Reactivate inactive B2B customers.
9. Sales Performance & Channel Optimisation
Track performance across all B2B and physical channels.
Measure:
Revenue
Boxes sold
Average transaction value
Direct costs
Profitability
Leads generated
Conversion
Repeat orders
Performance by location/channel

Sales and results driven - measures success by revenue, not activity. Generating at least S$30,000 monthly revenue through B2B sales, retail partnerships, pop-ups and roadshows.

Comfortable prospecting and approaching new businesses.
Strong at relationship building and follow-up.

Highly proactive and able to execute without constant direction.

Title: Assistant Vice President, Digital Workflow, Automation & AI
Description:
Assistant Vice President, Digital Workflow, Automation & AI
Global | Permanent or 12-month rotational assignment
About Citco
Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services with staff across 50 office locations worldwide. With more than $1.8 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional service to meet our clients’ needs.
For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com
About the Team & Business Line
Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.
Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.
The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:
Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.
Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.
Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.
The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.
Your Role
You will support the identification, build and deployment of automation and digital workflow solutions.
Map candidate processes in detail and quantify the manual effort involved.
Support the design of target workflows, including exception handling and controls.
Draft requirements and supporting documentation for review with IT and the Transformation Office.
Build and execute test scripts, run UAT cycles and track defects through to resolution.
Support deployment into the business, including user guidance and training material.
Track usage and benefit after go-live, and flag where a solution is not being used as intended.
Maintain project documentation, trackers and status reporting.
About You
You have 4+ years’ experience in private assets accounting or operations, with exposure to automation or process improvement work.
Solid technical knowledge of private assets processes and the manual steps within them.
Exposure to automation tooling, workflow design or testing, or a clear appetite to develop in that direction.
Comfortable challenging why a manual step exists and evidencing a better way.
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interrogate data and evidence a recommendation.
Attention to detail and a proven ability to manage several pieces of work at once.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel); exposure to reporting, workflow or automation tooling an advantage.
Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance or Economics; working towards a professional accounting designation an advantage.
What We Expect of the Strategic Operations Team
Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:
Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.
Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.
A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.
Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.
Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.
Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.
Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.
Our Benefits
Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.
We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.
Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com
About the Team & Business Line
Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.
Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.
The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:
Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.
Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.
Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.
The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.
Your Role
You will support the redesign and delivery of operating model and product change, with hands-on ownership of analysis, testing and implementation tasks.
Map current state processes, gather data and evidence where the friction and cost actually sit.
Support the design of target state processes, controls and handoffs.
Draft business requirements and supporting documentation for review with IT and the Transformation Office.
Build and execute test scripts, run UAT cycles and track defects through to resolution.
Document client-specific processes and requirements, and evidence where they differ from our standard model.
Prepare analysis and materials to support client pitches, POCs and solution design.
Support implementation of fund structures, new client setups, onboarding and transitions on our accounting platforms.
Maintain the reuse inventory — what was built, for whom, and who else could benefit.
Prepare training material and support Operations teams through go-live and into adoption.
Maintain project documentation, trackers and status reporting.
About You
You have 4+ years’ experience in private assets accounting or operations, at a fund administrator, fund manager or comparable environment.
Solid technical knowledge of private assets processes — general ledger, capital activity, fee calculations, financial statements and investor reporting.
Exposure to process improvement, system testing or project work, or a clear appetite to move in that direction.
Comfortable engaging both operational teams and technology partners.
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interrogate data and evidence a recommendation.
Attention to detail and a proven ability to manage several pieces of work at once.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel); exposure to reporting, workflow or automation tooling an advantage.
Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance or Economics; working towards a professional accounting designation an advantage.
What We Expect of the Strategic Operations Team
Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:
Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.
Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.
A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.
Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.
Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.
Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.
Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.
Our Benefits
Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.
We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.
Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

Title: Associate
Description:
TRINITY INTERNATIONAL
Tough projects. Exciting markets. Great people.
Trinity International is a boutique law firm with a unique focus on projects, finance, corporate and commercial transactions and international arbitration and dispute resolution in emerging markets. We think like entrepreneurs: we believe clients doing the most challenging deals in the most challenging markets deserve senior, hands-on lawyers who roll up their sleeves and get things done.
Our award-winning, senior-led team boasts vast experience in the power and renewables, resources, mining and infrastructure, industrial and agricultural sectors. With offices in Singapore, London, Paris and Washington, D.C., we are a boutique firm with a global vision.
The firm provides legal services in project finance, commercial and corporate transactions and international arbitration and dispute resolution in emerging markets across the Asia-Pacific, Africa and Latin America. These are tough, fast-moving and sometimes unpredictable markets, and that is exactly why we love working in them.
The firm’s clients include financial institutions, including development finance institutions, multilaterals, commercial banks and funds, major corporates, developers and sponsors of projects, equity investors, governments and other public sector stakeholders.
ROLE DESCRIPTION
We are looking for an Associate with energy, curiosity and a sense of adventure to join our growing Singapore team.
This is not a role for someone who wants to sit on one small piece of a very large deal. At Trinity you will be close to the action from day one: working directly with partners and clients, and helping to get landmark projects over the line in markets where the playbook is still being written.
The role covers the full life of energy and infrastructure projects: drafting, reviewing and negotiating project, finance and security documents, supporting M&A and joint venture transactions, carrying out due diligence and managing the interface with clients, local counsel and other advisers. You will work in a dynamic team with different partners, counsel and associates, often alongside colleagues in the firm's other offices.
Trinity does not believe in lawyers having a narrow focus or being pigeon-holed. As a result, although financing and energy M&A experience is key, the role will allow and encourage the successful candidate to experience other aspects of the firm’s practice, including project development, wider M&A/private equity and international arbitration. If you enjoy variety, you will fit right in.
Core focus will be on the power/energy and infrastructure sectors, but will also involve sectors including mining, oil & gas, petrochemicals, heavy industry, manufacturing and agribusiness.
Day-to-day tasks include drafting and reviewing contracts, conducting due diligence, managing client relationships, and advising clients on project and corporate finance and energy M&A matters. The role requires collaboration with international colleagues and handling cross-border transactions.
We are a growing firm and everyone has a stake in building it. All members of the team are encouraged to play a part in business development, and good ideas are welcome from anyone, whatever their seniority.
It is a hybrid role that requires no fewer than 3 days per week in the relevant office.
QUALIFICATIONS
Singapore or common law qualified (admitted in Singapore, UK, Australia, New Zealand or Canada), 3+ years PQE, preferably in a global law firm.
Experience in project finance, corporate finance, energy M&A and project development, with a particular focus on financing.
Proven ability to draft and negotiate finance and M&A transaction documents, conduct due diligence, and manage client relationships.
Strong knowledge of energy, infrastructure, resources, and industry sectors.
Excellent negotiation and communication skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team, with a willingness to collaborate across international offices.
Fluency in English; additional language skills are a plus.
Previous experience working in emerging markets, or a genuine appetite to do work in them.
ESSENTIAL QUALITIES
Entrepreneurial Spirit: Enjoy building things. See a tricky market or a complex deal as an opportunity, not an obstacle.
Team Player: Work in a team environment in a collaborative and positive manner. Be willing to help colleagues in busy times in particular.
Positive Outlook: Exhibit a friendly and enthusiastic demeanour that encourages a collaborative environment. Find solutions, not problems.
A Sense of Humour: We work hard on demanding matters and we like to enjoy it. We take our work seriously, but not ourselves.
Integrity and Professionalism: Demonstrate honesty and confidence, fostering trust and credibility with colleagues and clients.
Proactive Mindset: Take initiative to drive tasks and projects forward and address issues effectively, both personally and within the team.
Long term: We encourage candidates to take a long-term approach in interviewing with us and we provide a collaborative environment where a candidate can continue to grow professionally.
REMUNERATION
We have a pay scale similar to Silver Circle UK firms but will offer bespoke packages depending on the candidate’s experience, PQE, existing salary and profile.
We offer a bonus scheme that can be discussed in more detail, as well as a benefits package.
If you are looking for real responsibility on landmark deals in frontier markets, we would love to hear from you.

Title: Associate (Corporate Transactions)
Description:
About Ashurst Perkins Coie
Ashurst Perkins Coie is the global law firm for the future economy.
With more than 3,500 client-facing practitioners across 52 offices worldwide, we advise a broad range of clients, and have a distinct strength in technology, energy & infrastructure, and financial services - three sectors at the forefront of economic transformation.
Combining global scale, sector insight, and technological capability, Ashurst Perkins Coie helps clients unlock opportunity with market-leading experience in complex transactions, litigation, and regulatory matters.
We support clients through a shifting landscape where technology, and AI in particular, is both an accelerator and disruptor to their business opportunities and challenges and is reshaping how energy, data, and capital move across markets.
Our strengths have earned our lawyers recognition across the profession, and more importantly, the trust of our clients. Our people are our greatest asset, advising clients on complex, cross-border matters and collaborating seamlessly across markets and practices. We offer a global platform for career-defining work and an opportunity to help shape a firm with the culture and confidence to compete at the highest level.
For Ashurst Perkins Coie, innovation is our tradition. We have a long legacy of helping clients through moments of transformation with the insight to help them stay ahead.
To find out more please visit our website.
About The Team
We have a global team of Corporate partners and associates who are located across major commercial centres including in Australia, Asia, UK, Central Europe and the Middle East. This enables us to provide a true global, local and regional offering to our clients.
Our Singapore corporate transactions team regularly advises clients on cross-border mergers and acquisitions and joint ventures, as well as capital markets transactions. This includes advising on all aspects of public takeovers, schemes of arrangement, private equity buyouts, IPOs, secondary offerings, and due diligence and regulatory matters. We specialise in transactions in highly regulated industry sectors, in particular the energy and natural resources, financial services and insurance sectors, where we have strong sector experience and in-depth understanding of the key relevant commercial and regulatory issues facing our clients. For more information, please visit the practice group's page on our website.
About The Role
The Corporate Transactions team in Singapore advises a wide range of public and private clients on complex and high-profile matters cross-border M&As and investments, particularly in the region.
The team are now looking for an ambitious, driven and committed junior level practitioner to join this growing practice. This opportunity represents an outstanding opportunity for a team-player with strong technical skills and commercial acumen to join this well established and high regarded team.
Main tasks:
Drafting and reviewing of legal documents and agreements, including sale and purchase agreements, shareholder agreements, joint venture agreements and the like.
Familiarity with due diligence (both buy-side and sell-side)
Assisting in negotiations and related matters
Matter completion and post-closing work.
Business development and networking activities.
Contributing to department know-how.
About You
At least 1 to 3 years' legal experience gained within a top-tier firm;
Qualified in Singapore;
Strong experience in M&A transactions;
Keen sense of curiosity and adaptability to turn your hands at novel transactions and issues;
Excellent technical and drafting skills coupled with commercial nous;
Excellent verbal and written communication skills (including drafting) and excellent organisational skills.
Ability to work autonomously and effectively manage multiple and often competing priorities;
Build team morale and motivate team members, contributing to the creation of a positive work environment and to assist with training and development;
Lateral thinker to develop innovative solutions to issues that arise during transactions; and
A proactive, positive and energetic approach with a commitment to providing excellent service and, a desire to interact with the market and build client relationships.
Background checks
In order to comply with regulatory and client requirements, Ashurst Perkins Coie will undertake appropriate vetting of staff. When applicants accept a job offer, Ashurst Perkins Coie, alongside a specialist provider, will undertake professional verification and background checks. These checks are only undertaken with consent, and in accordance with our legal and regulatory obligations.

Title: Associate / Associate Director, FICC Trading (APAC)
Description:
Purpose
BNS Singapore acts as the regional trading hub, providing centralized, efficient client coverage and engagement for our flow business, DCM activities, private placements, financing, and credit- and rates- linked structured products. The primary role is to make markets for clients, and trade the firm’s repo, FX, STIR, rates and credit books in the region. The role will execute and hedge transactions to manage and mitigate risk associated with these customer transactions, along with managing risks associated with trading positions through a variety of hedging strategies to maximize the return to the business within approved risk appetite. At the same time, to engage with clients to foster and leverage Banking relationships.
The trader will contribute to the overall success of the FICC and GBM business regionally and globally ensuring specific individual goals, plans, and initiatives are executed / delivered in support of the team’s business strategies and objectives. Ensures all activities conducted are in compliance with governing regulations, internal policies, and procedures.
The role is based in Singapore.
Accountabilities
Meet and exceed client volumes and market share metrics.
Price fixed income cash securities from Scotiabank’s global product suite including but not limited to USD and CAD denominated instruments (Governments, SSAs and Corporates).
Help manage and hedge relevant interest rate derivatives trading risks (IRS, Xccy, and basis), as appropriate. Promote BNS interest rate products and identify and action cross-sell opportunities with clients
Help manage and hedge relevant FX spot, forwards, swaps, options and NDFs risks as appropriate in the region. Drive up trading volume during the process of expanding the FX business.
Help manage and hedge relevant short term interest rate risks and liaise with the global STIR desks to promote Bank’s products.
Assist with the structuring, marketing and pricing of various non-linear / exotic FICC structured solutions & FICC linked structured notes, during Asia time-zone, providing support to the client coverage teams (primarily APAC Fixed Income Sales).
Contribute to a client-focused culture throughout their team to deepen client relationships and leverage broader Bank relationships, systems, and knowledge.
Understand how the Bank’s risk appetite and risk culture should be considered in day-to-day activities and decisions.
Actively pursue effective and efficient operations of their respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank's Values, its Code of Conduct, and the Global Sales Principles, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions and conduct risk.
Champion a high-performance environment and contributes to an inclusive work environment.
Operate within approved risk limits and promptly escalate any actual or potential breaches
Dimensions
• This role requires successful completion of the National Futures Association’s Swaps Proficiency Requirement (SPR), prior to engaging in in-scope activity.
• Operate within designated trading limits
• Operates under general guidelines, specific code of conduct, and general bank policies
• Positive contribution to overall global business
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills
• Demonstrate ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and excel under pressure.
• Ability to work in Singapore.
• Self-motivated, with excellent judgement and discretion.
• The role requires a thorough understanding of liability management and extensive experience in the global fixed income and foreign exchange markets. Critical skillset includes hedging, price making, and risk management.
NOTE: Partial secondment to BNS Singapore Branch will be required to enable candidate to perform bookings in the name of BNS to comply with Singapore regulations governing Securities and Futures activities.
Education I Experience I Other Information (include only those that are specific to the role)
• MBA or undergraduate degree, with an established record of academic achievement.
• Minimum 3 years in Fixed Income markets primarily dealing Fixed Income (US, UK, Singapore)
• Current Singapore MAS (1B, 6A)
• Will have exposure to legal, risk, management, and regulatory issues both globally and in Asia Pacific; will be required to coordinate and connect with other global teams on a regular basis.
• Strong personal attributes, including enthusiasm, initiative, persistence, results driven, attention to detail, and setting high standards.
• Flexibility to meet demands inherent in a global business that operates 24 hours a day, over 5 days a week.
• Knowledge of Canadian fixed income markets an advantage
Working Conditions
1. Majority of time will be spent on the trading room floor.
2. High stress fast paced working environment with many deadlines.
3. Ability to multitask and deal with numerous competing demands
4. Moderate international travel, as required.
5. The transactions in which the position becomes directly involved have tight deadlines. Evening and weekend work can be regular, without prior notice, and could take place out of town. The position requires a very high degree of flexibility and cooperation, as well as occasionally accepting responsibilities outside of the defined accountabilities.

Title: Associate Director (Cost Planning/ MNC Consultancy)

Title: Associate Director of Quality
Description:
The Associate Director of Quality is a senior leadership role within the AMS Quality & Technical Team, responsible for the end-to-end quality framework across Vita Coco's Singapore operations. This role leads a multi-functional team spanning Brand Quality, Operations-facing Quality, and the Quality Laboratory, ensuring that quality standards are embedded across the full value chain — from supplier to consumer.
The role serves as the primary Quality interface between the Singapore site and global Quality leadership at US headquarters, translating corporate strategy into locally actionable plans while representing the realities of local operations in global forums. The Associate Director of Quality plays a critical role in driving a culture of quality, food safety, and continuous improvement across the organization.
Key accountabilities include:
Strategic Leadership & HQ Alignment
Serve as the primary Quality liaison between Singapore operations and global Quality leadership, ensuring corporate strategy is translated into locally actionable priorities.
Represent local operational realities and constraints in global Quality forums and contribute to the development and review of global Quality policies.
Champion a culture of quality and food safety across the Singapore Site & Manufacturing network, setting the standard for quality performance at all levels.
Proactively drive alignment across markets to standardize working methods and ensure consistency across the business.
Support all new product launches from a quality framework perspective, as required.
People & Team Leadership
Lead, develop and inspire a multi-functional Quality team spanning Brand Quality, Operations-facing Quality and the Quality Laboratory.
Set clear objectives, KPIs and development plans for direct and indirect reports.
Build team capability through coaching, training and structured development programs.
Manage team resourcing, workload prioritization and succession planning.
Foster collaboration and clear ownership across Corporate Quality, Operations Quality and Laboratory functions.
Corporate & Regulatory Quality
Supports the implementation of the QMS system once identified.
Ensure compliance with relevant local regulatory requirements (e.g. SFA) as well as international standards (FSSC 22000, BRC, ISO 22000, etc.).
Leads as needed various regulatory inspections and customer or third-party audits.
Manage document control, SOPs and quality records governance.
Drive CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) processes across quality incidents.
Oversee supplier and vendor quality assurance programs, including qualification and ongoing performance monitoring.
Create and maintain a framework supporting smart data analysis, including product integrity monitoring, shelf-life testing and other key data streams.
Operations & Factory-Facing Quality
Ensure robust quality controls are embedded throughout the manufacturing process, from raw material intake to finished goods.
Lead internal and external audit programs as needed.
Lead and support the supplier audit network, maintaining and developing audit capability across the supply base.
Partner closely with Operations, Supply Chain and R&D to resolve quality issues impacting production and supply chain continuity.
Monitor and analyze production quality data, driving root cause analysis for non-conformances.
Oversee new product and process qualifications from a quality standpoint.
Maintain strong relationships with the supply chain team, supplier network and internal stakeholders.
Laboratory Oversight
Provide senior oversight of the Quality Laboratory, ensuring it operates within a clear framework aligned with business and Quality objectives.
Act as the organizational buffer for the laboratory, ensuring incoming requests from across the business are appropriately filtered and prioritized before reaching the team.
Own senior-level cross-functional relationships on behalf of the lab, ensuring structured and well-managed engagement with key stakeholder functions.
Represent the laboratory at leadership level, advocating for the resources, investment and support needed for it to perform effectively.
Ensure the laboratory maintains its regulatory and accreditation standing, escalating quality risks with broader business implications as needed.
Consumer & Brand Protection
Oversee the consumer complaints management process, ensuring timely investigation and resolution.
Lead and coordinate product recall and withdrawal procedures if required.
Monitor quality performance metrics and trends to proactively identify and mitigate brand risk.
Partner with Marketing and Commercial teams to protect brand integrity and consumer trust.
Reporting, Data & Governance
Define and track Quality KPIs across Corporate, Operations and Laboratory functions.
Prepare and present regular Quality performance reports to local senior leadership and US HQ.
Ensure Quality risks and escalations are communicated proactively to relevant stakeholders.
Lead the local Quality Management Review process.
Maintain awareness of emerging food safety trends, regulatory changes and industry best practices relevant to Singapore and the broader region.
Qualifications & Skills
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Food Science, Food Technology, Microbiology, Chemistry or a related scientific discipline; Master’s degree would be beneficial.
Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in Quality within the food and beverage industry, with at least 2-4 years in a senior leadership role.
Strong written and communication skills.
Experience with low-acid aseptic Tetra Pak processing is required; experience with retorted cans and aseptic PET is a strong advantage.
Proven track record managing multi-functional Quality teams, including both corporate and operations-facing functions.
Strong working knowledge of food safety standards and frameworks (HACCP, FSSC 22000, BRC, ISO 22000).
Familiarity with laboratory operations and accreditation requirements (ISO/IEC 17025 advantageous).
Experience working within a multinational organization and interfacing with regional or global headquarters.
Solid understanding of local regulatory requirements (SFA and relevant Singapore food safety legislation).
Proficiency in Quality Management Systems (QMS) and data-driven decision making.
Willingness to travel internationally and to work extended hours during critical periods as needed.
Personal Characteristics
Natural leader who leads by example and earns trust at all levels of the organization.
Collaborative and relationship-driven, able to engage effectively with both technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong analytical mindset with sharp attention to detail, without losing sight of the bigger picture.
Pragmatic and calm under pressure, able to navigate ambiguity and manage competing priorities without compromising standards.
High degree of personal accountability and integrity.
Comfortable operating in a matrix environment, balancing local operational needs with global strategic direction.
Curious and growth-oriented, keeping pace with industry trends, emerging regulations and best practices.
Understands the dynamics of an entrepreneurial, high-growth business and brings the energy and results-orientation to thrive in it.

Vita Coco is headquartered in New York City with international offices Singapore and London.

Some careers have more impact than others.
If you’re looking for a career where you can make a real impression, join HSBC and discover how valued you’ll be. Whether you want a career that could take you to the top, or simply take you in an exciting new direction, HSBC offers opportunities, support and rewards that will take you further.
HSBC Corporate and Institutional Banking is a markets-led, financing-focused business that provides investment and financial solutions. Our sector-focused Banking relationship managers provide a single coverage point for multi-national clients. With our global capabilities and footprint, vast expertise, and local knowledge, our Global Network Banking teams connect clients to the products and services that meet their international financial needs.
We are currently seeking a high calibre professional to join our team as a
Associate Director, Account Management - Securities Services.
In the role you will:
Own client retention, sentiment and referenceability across the AO&M client base, working closely with Product Management, Service Delivery, Technology and Client Management teams to deliver consistently high service standards across SSv products and jurisdictions.
Develop and maintain detailed strategic client and account management plans aligned to broader SSv growth priorities, client objectives and Executive Committee (EXCO) planning, including clear actions, ownership, milestones and measurable outcomes.
Act as the client advocate across SSv, coordinating virtual and geographically dispersed teams to ensure a consistent, joined-up client experience and effective execution of the agreed client and HSBC agenda.
Lead proactive issue and service management across products and jurisdictions by directing the appropriate resources, ensuring timely resolution, transparent communication and effective escalation of material risks or concerns.
Identify and sponsor service improvement and transformation opportunities, using client feedback, data, automation, digitisation and new technology to enhance the account management proposition and prioritise change agendas across the business.
Establish and maintain robust client governance, including agreed service governance frameworks, senior stakeholder meetings, service reviews, management information and reporting, while ensuring adherence to internal controls and governance standards.
Support strategic growth, new business and cross-selling activity by partnering with Client Executives and Sales on client and prospect initiatives, leveraging HSBC’s broader product suite, SSv capabilities and proprietary network.
Own commercial outcomes for non CE covered clients, identifying incremental growth opportunities, supporting profitability and contribution to the Annual Operating Planning (AOP) process, and ensuring that commercial and contractual commitments are effectively managed.
To be successful you will need:
At least eight years’ relevant experience in client management, business implementation and change, business development, securities services or senior operational leadership, preferably within a complex financial services environment.
Strong client-facing, communication and presentation skills, with proven experience leading senior and executive-level meetings, influencing stakeholders and managing sensitive client discussions.
A demonstrable track record of managing, developing and retaining client relationships across securities services products, with the ability to contribute to and execute departmental strategy and deliver measurable client outcomes.
Strong commercial and contractual awareness, including experience managing client economics, profitability, contribution to AOP or strategic planning, business performance and growth opportunities.
Proven ability to operate collaboratively across a complex, global organisation, balancing the requirements of clients, internal stakeholders, risk and control functions, and multiple products and jurisdictions.
Strong understanding of the securities services industry, regulatory requirements, risk management and internal controls, including product and market risk, client management obligations and appropriate mitigation techniques. Demonstrated leadership, mentoring and team-working skills are also essential.

Title: AVP, Business Proposition, Protection, Global
Description:
Job Title
AVP, Business Proposition, Protection, Global
Job Description
The Role
The AVP, Business Proposition role plays an important role within the Protection business. To be successful in this role, the incumbent will be able to demonstrate long term and “out of the box” thinking to develop compelling solutions to market problems that will ultimately expand our proposition set and support us generating material volumes of highly valuable business in areas we currently do not operate.
This role would see strategic initiatives through end-to-end, working with others in the Global Client Solutions team and wider Protection teams. This role will also work closely with the Divisional Strategy team and will dotted line report into the VP, Strategy, Division, and will join Divisional Strategy meetings.
This role will be expected to collaborate closely with the Client Solutions market teams, and will be a conduit for global idea generation and sharing. Additionally, this role will also require a close working partnership with UnderwriteMe, ensuring where appropriate our UnderwriteMe differentiators are being leveraged in our propositions.
Responsibilities
New market/segments exploration:
Periodic initiation and review of new markets/segments working with relevant in-market Client Solutions Teams
Development of initial stage gates and fail fast criteria, working closely with relevant Protection teams, before eventually passing ownership to the most appropriate BAU market team once relevant stage gates are met
Product/Proposition development:
Leading global product / propositions which are typically large-scale cross market opportunities
Acting as a conduit for the function in Protection to leverage product work being performed in each market and ensure a global mindset is being adopted
From time to time developing ideas and material to support client workshops or pitches, to ensure that the best of our global business is being leveraged
Protection Strategy:
Facilitating periodic review of market strategies for Protection, which will require working closely with the Client Solutions teams in each of our markets and PMLCs
Supporting consistency of approach to strategy across the Line of Business and UMe where appropriate, including providing relevant tools and templates
Identifying opportunities to leverage projects across markets, including DISC initiatives
Divisional Strategy:
Working with the Divisional Strategy team on global or cross Line of Business initiatives
Attending relevant Divisional Strategy team meetings, including leveraging expertise across the business and ensuring consistency where appropriate
Together with the VP, Client Solutions, Protection, Global, providing Chief of Staff type support to the GPEC, including:
Supporting the development and review of strategic objectives
Supporting the reporting of strategic objectives and other initiatives, including in staff meetings and other forums
Working with PMLCs as appropriate to report on progress with strategic initiatives

Knowledge
Educated to at least degree level preferably with actuarial or other similar training

Ability and desire to communicate with business customers at all levels across the business and to work well within a team environment
Organised, conscientious, and deadline focused with an attention to detail
Ability to manage competing demands and deal with non-standard and unstructured requests, at short notice
Motivated to take ownership of work and to seek further responsibility

Proficiency extracting, manipulating, analysing and drawing conclusions from data.

The AVP, Business Proposition role is responsible for ensuring a strong risk culture exists within the global enablement team. The key risk management responsibilities include:
Demonstrating awareness and understanding of risk policies, key risks and associated controls;
Translating risk management principles and objectives into priorities, processes and activities that make sense to team members;
Fostering a culture of risk management in the team through training and performance management.
Taking a pro-active approach to identifying, fixing and learning from control failures.

Description:
ADDX is seeking a highly sales- and purpose-driven Client Account Manager who possesses a unique blend of expertise in financial markets, investment products, strategic thinking, and a strong client-focused and entrepreneurial mindset. As a Client Account Manager, you will play a pivotal role in working with our Head of Consumer Group to forging strong relationships with new and existing key accredited investors, and providing a strong feedback loop to enhance and improve our platform and digital client journey. This role will need to have the ability to manage a large portfolio of clients at scale, while having the ability to address more bespoke demands from our top-tier investors, as well as identifying strategic partnership opportunities.
Responsibilities:
1. Client Acquisition: Strong ability to acquire quality accredited investors who resonate with ADDX's proposition of investing in private markets and investment alternatives to strengthen and diversify their portfolio.
2. Client Relationship Management: Build and maintain strong relationships with top decile clients, serving as their primary point of contact. Understand their investment needs, objectives, and challenges to provide tailored solutions and meet their needs.
3. Strategic Business Development: Work closely with the Head of Consumer Group and team members to identify opportunities based on client feedback and experience across sales, partnerships, investment product and digital client journeys.
4. Client Support: Provide prompt and effective support to clients, addressing inquiries, resolving issues, and managing escalations.
5. Understand Market Trends: Understand industry trends, competitive landscape, and client-specific dynamics to proactively identify opportunities and mitigate risks.
6.Cross-functional Collaboration: Collaborate closely with internal teams, including sales, digital marketing, product, and operations, to align on client needs, ensure consistent messaging, and drive customer success. Share client feedback and insights regularly to inform product enhancements and service improvements.
7. Risk Management: Ensure compliance with financial regulatory and compliance standards when conducting regulated activities and managing client relationships.
8. Adherence to Financial Regulations and Standards: Attend mandatory training sessions and workshops conducted by LRC to ensure and enhance understanding and utilization of our products and services. Be aware of financial industry, best practices and trends.
Requirements:
1. Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration, Marketing, or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
