Title: Creative Producer, Senior Manager Asia
Description:
About Crunchyroll
Founded by fans, Crunchyroll delivers the art and culture of anime to a passionate community. We super-serve over 100 million anime and manga fans across 200+ countries and territories, and help them connect with the stories and characters they crave. Whether that experience is online or in-person, streaming video, theatrical, games, merchandise, events and more, it’s powered by the anime content we all love.
Join our team, and help us shape the future of anime!
About the Role
The Senior Manager, Creative producer — Asia (Ex IN) will lead the end-to-end operational delivery of regional campaigns across Asia excluding India, including Southeast Asia, Korea, Taiwan, and other priority markets. Based in Singapore, this role will ensure that campaigns move efficiently from brief to market through clear workflows, strong cross-functional coordination, disciplined production management, and reliable launch readiness.
You will work closely with Regional Marketing, Growth, Partnerships, Content, Communications & PR, Localization & Operations, Product, global creative teams, agencies, production partners, and distribution platforms. The role will manage campaign intake, prioritization, briefing, production, approvals, asset delivery, launch tracking, reporting, and post-campaign learning.
This is a senior individual-contributor role requiring strong project management, creative operations expertise, stakeholder influence, attention to detail, and the ability to manage complex multi-market campaigns across different time zones and cultures.
Role overview - Lead creative producer Across Asia (Ex IN)
Own campaign operations from intake and briefing through prioritization, resourcing, production, approvals, launch, and post-campaign closeout.
Translate regional marketing, content, growth, partnership, and communications priorities into clear creative briefs, scopes, workplans, timelines, owners, dependencies, and deliverables.
Establish campaign operating rhythms, status reporting, production trackers, decision forums, and escalation paths.
Maintain a consolidated view of campaign progress, asset status, approvals, risks, dependencies, resource constraints, and launch readiness.
Ensure campaigns are delivered on time, within agreed scope, and in line with brand, market, partner, legal, and channel requirements.
Manage Creative Production and Asset Delivery
Coordinate the development, adaptation, production, review, approval, and delivery of campaign assets across digital, social, content, partner, retail, event, platform, and owned channels.
Partner with creative leads to ensure briefs are complete, objectives are clear, audiences are defined, and deliverables are appropriately scoped.
Manage asset requirements, specifications, version control, usage rights, file delivery, trafficking, and distribution across markets and channels.
Coordinate creative revisions and approvals across Marketing, Creative, Content, Legal, Communications, Partners, and global teams.
Ensure final assets meet Crunchyroll brand standards, campaign objectives, partner specifications, local market requirements, and accessibility expectations.
Coordinate Localization and Market Adaptation
Manage the handoff of creative assets to Localization & Operations for translation, cultural adaptation, subtitling, dubbing, or other market requirements where applicable.
Track localized asset status, quality reviews, approvals, and final delivery across priority Asia (Ex IN) markets.
Ensure local adaptations preserve campaign intent, creative quality, brand consistency, and cultural relevance.
Identify localization dependencies and risks early and incorporate them into campaign plans and launch timelines.
Partner with regional market stakeholders to validate asset relevance and readiness.
Drive Cross-Functional Campaign Readiness
Coordinate with Regional Marketing, Growth, Partnerships, Content, Communications & PR, Localization & Operations, Product, Legal, Data, Finance, and Customer Experience.
Lead readiness reviews for content launches, seasonal campaigns, partner activations, brand initiatives, events, and market programs.
Track decisions, actions, dependencies, risks, and open issues through to resolution.
Ensure all campaign stakeholders understand their roles, deadlines, approval requirements, and launch responsibilities.
Escalate delivery risks and trade-offs in a timely, structured, and solutions-oriented way.
Manage Agencies and Production Partners
Coordinate internal creative teams, agencies, production companies, freelancers, localization vendors, media partners, and other external resources.
Establish clear scopes of work, production schedules, service levels, quality expectations, review cycles, and delivery requirements.
Monitor partner and vendor performance across quality, timeliness, responsiveness, capacity, and cost.
Support partner onboarding, briefing, evaluation, performance improvement, and closeout.
Build trusted relationships that improve creative efficiency, collaboration, and delivery quality.
Build Scalable Campaign Operations
Develop and maintain campaign operations playbooks, templates, workflows, checklists, dashboards, and reporting frameworks.
Improve briefing quality, production visibility, approval speed, asset reuse, localization handoffs, and launch execution.
Maintain organized campaign documentation, asset libraries, version control, rights information, and delivery records.
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and scale recurring campaign operations across the region.
Establish and track operational metrics such as on-time delivery, asset completeness, approval cycle time, issue aging, vendor performance, and launch quality.
Lead post-campaign reviews and translate learnings into improved processes, planning, and future campaign execution.
Experience and qualifications
8+ years of experience in campaign operations, creative operations, integrated marketing, production management, program management, or a related field.
Experience managing complex, multi-market campaigns across entertainment, media, streaming, technology, gaming, consumer platforms, or a related industry.
Strong understanding of creative briefing, production workflows, asset management, localization handoffs, approvals, trafficking, and launch readiness.
Demonstrated experience managing multiple campaigns, agencies, production partners, stakeholders, timelines, and dependencies simultaneously.
Experience building and improving creative operations processes, workflows, templates, trackers, dashboards, and quality-control frameworks.
Experience working with creative teams, marketing teams, localization vendors, media partners, agencies, and external production resources.
Strong project management, organization, prioritization, problem-solving, and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to balance creative quality, cultural relevance, brand consistency, launch deadlines, partner requirements, and operational constraints.
Experience working in a matrixed and globally distributed organization across different time zones, markets, cultures, and backgrounds.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide concise status updates and executive-level escalations.
High attention to detail and a strong commitment to quality, timeliness, and follow-through.
Willingness to travel across Asia and internationally as required.
Fluency in English is required; knowledge of relevant Asian languages is a significant plus.
Knowledge and passion for anime, entertainment, creative culture, and fan communities is a significant plus.
Why you will love working at Crunchyroll
In addition to getting to work with fun, passionate and inspired colleagues, you will also enjoy the following benefits and perks:
Receive a great compensation package including salary plus performance bonus earning potential, paid annually.
Flexible time off policies allowing you to take the time you need to be your whole self.
Generous medical, dental, vision, STD, LTD, and life insurance
Health Saving Account HSA program
Health care and dependent care FSA
401(k) plan, with employer match
Employer paid commuter benefit
Support program for new parents
Pet insurance and some of our offices are pet friendly!

Title: CRM & Loyalty Manager
Description:
About Us
Love, Bonito is Southeast Asia's leading womenswear brand, built with a mission to empower women to find confidence through style. Incorporated in 2010 in Singapore, we've since grown from a humble online startup into a multi-channel business with over 20 stores and counting across Asia and a thriving online presence.
For the next decade, we are looking to expand through new categories, markets, wholesale partnerships, and brand acquisitions. We are evolving into a next-generation regional consumer group — one that blends heart with performance, and creativity with technology.
At our core, we're a team of builders, dreamers, and doers who believe culture is more than words on a wall — it's how we show up every day. We move fast, stay curious, and take bold bets on ideas and people we believe in. Here, you'll find a community that challenges you to grow, trusts you to lead, and celebrates you for being you. Together, we're shaping the future of Asian brands — from right here in Southeast Asia, to the world.
Why join us?
At Love, Bonito, you'll do more than just a job — you'll help build a movement. We're creating an organization that's lean, bold, and full of heart — where every person has the space to make an impact. Here's what you can expect:
- Purpose with performance: We're building a world-class Asian brand that competes globally. We hold ourselves to high standards and operate with purpose, integrity, grit and excellence. Join us if you take customer service excellence seriously and are passionate about creating real impact!
- Growth that's real: We are known to be incredibly dynamic and fast-paced. You'll be expected to learn fast, stretch beyond your comfort zone, and work alongside people who challenge and support you in equal measure. Don't join us if you're looking for a comfortable, fully structured setup, but do join us if you're excited to build, shape, and make an impact together!
- Culture at our core: If you're looking for a no-corporate-BS environment, you'll fit right in. We lead with empathy, celebrate individuality, and believe that great work comes from trust, not titles. We believe in teamwork and effective collaboration - because when we run together, we go further. If this speaks to your values, come join us and be part of #TeamLB!
Join us as we redefine what it means to build an enduring global consumer group.
About The Role
We are looking for a CRM & Loyalty Manager to own how we talk to and reward our customers. Reporting directly to the CEO, you'll lead a lean team of three, and turn customer data into campaigns, rewards, and decisions that drive engagement, retention, and lifetime value.
Main Responsibilities
- CRM Communications
- Own the CRM communications strategy and calendar
- Build and manage campaigns to drive acquisition, retention, and LTV
- Drive segmentation, personalisation, and A/B testing to improve open, click, and conversion rates
- Mobile Engagement
- Own the mobile communications strategy and calendar
- Build and manage mobile campaigns to drive acquisition, retention, and LTV
- Drive segmentation, personalisation, and A/B testing to improve open, click, and conversion rates
- Loyalty Programme
- Own the loyalty programme strategy end to end — enrollment, tiering, rewards, and redemption
- Design and launch new perks, rewards, and experiences that increase engagement and repeat purchase
- Track programme performance (enrollment, redemption, incremental revenue) and iterate based on results
- Manage the loyalty platform vendor relationship and lead evaluations of new capabilities
- Customer Insights
- Analyse customer data — behaviour, purchase, and engagement — to generate insights that inform CRM, loyalty, and broader marketing decisions
- Build customer segmentation and journey mapping to sharpen targeting across channels
- Run surveys, focus groups, and voice-of-customer programmes to deepen the company's understanding of customer needs
- Partner cross-functionally to embed customer insights into product, merchandising, and marketing strategy
- Reporting & Budgeting
- Report CRM and loyalty performance against KPIs — acquisition, retention, engagement, and programme ROI
- Manage the team's budget, with full accountability for allocation across CRM and loyalty priorities
- Technology, Automation & AI
- Manage the CRM and push platforms, and maximize martech tools to strengthen automation and targeting
- Utilize technology and AI with the goal of improving efficiency whether across driving revenue optimization or automation
- Team & Stakeholder Management
- Lead and coach a team, owning goal-setting, performance management, and capability development
- Own CRM and loyalty KPIs — acquisition, retention, engagement, and programme ROI
- Represent CRM and loyalty priorities into broader marketing and leadership planning
- Manage vendor and agency relationships supporting CRM and loyalty execution
What Success Looks Like In 6 Months
- CRM communications run on a consistent, optimised calendar, with operational efficiency, with a measurable lift in engagement
- The loyalty programme has a clear roadmap
- Customer insights is feeding directly into marketing and business decisions
Main KPIs
- Revenues from email and mobile push notification channels
- Customer retention metrics
- Loyalty programme enrollment, redemption, and incremental revenue
- Mobile MAU
Requirements
Qualifications
- 7+ years of experience in a CRM role, preferably in retail or e-commerce
- Hands-on experience with CRM/marketing automation platforms (we use Braze)
- Experience in driving mobile engagement
- Experience managing a loyalty or membership programme
- Experience leading and developing a team
- Analytical and proficient in SQL
What Sets You Apart
- You're equal parts strategist and executor — as comfortable building the loyalty roadmap as you are debugging a campaign send
Who Will Not Be a Fit
- Anyone who wants to set strategy without owning execution
How We Work
- Clarity over complexity
- Fewer, bigger bets
- Hands-on, accountable leadership
- Open challenge, fast decisions

Title: Customer Success Manager
Description:
Who We Are
Overhaul is a supply chain integrity solutions company that allows shippers to connect disparate sources of data into the first fully transparent situational analysis engine designed for the logistics industry. Data that is transformed into critical insights can instantly trigger corrective actions, impacting everything from temperature control to handling requirements or package-level tracking, ensuring cargo arrives at its destination safely, undamaged, and on time. We are a dynamic, innovative, and fun team who is highly committed to our customers' experiences and our Mission and Vision.
The Role
As the Dedicated Customer Success Manager for Asia, you will be a regional owner and subject matter expert for one strategic global customer. This is a highly engaged role focused on knowing the customer's program in depth, staying ahead of performance and priorities, and ensuring that actions move from discussion to completion. You will build a strong working partnership with the customer, develop detailed knowledge of their logistics and security program in your region, and connect their needs to the right Overhaul teams and capabilities.
This role is dedicated to the customer's Asia program and is accountable for regional program health, stakeholder alignment, and execution while operating as part of a coordinated global Customer Success team led from the US.
Success requires curiosity, strong ownership, excellent organization, sound customer judgment, and the ability to connect day-to-day program detail with the customer's broader goals. You will be expected to be proactive, data-driven, and comfortable coordinating across functions, regions, and time zones.
Responsibilities
Regional Program Ownership and SME
Become the subject matter expert on the customer's supply chain, security program, operating model, workflows, use cases, stakeholders, and program requirements within Asia.
Develop a deep understanding of how the customer uses Overhaul across the region, including relevant product capabilities, configurations, monitoring processes, operational workflows, and escalation paths.
Build detailed lane-level knowledge of origins and destinations, transportation modes, carriers, hubs, airports or ports, handoffs, approved or expected routing, normal transit and dwell patterns, and relevant regional security risks.
Use that operational and security knowledge to identify recurring route or risk patterns and work with the customer and internal teams to optimize routing decisions, monitoring workflows, alert strategy, and escalation processes to reduce risk, delay, and unnecessary exceptions.
Stay ahead of the program by maintaining a clear view of priorities, open actions, risks, dependencies, changes, and upcoming needs - and drive customer and internal commitments through completion.
Customer Partnership and Governance
Serve as a primary Customer Success point of contact for the customer's Asia stakeholders and build trusted relationships across operational and leadership teams.
Lead regular customer cadences and program reviews with a clear point of view on program health, progress, risks, decisions, and next steps.
Proactively identify customer needs and challenges, translate them into clear internal actions, and keep the regional program aligned to the customer's business objectives.
Global Account Coordination
Operate as part of one global Customer Success team, partnering closely with the dedicated CSMs in the other regions and the US-based Global Customer Success Lead.
Share regional performance, route and security learnings, risks, customer feedback, and best practices so the customer receives a consistent global experience while legitimate regional differences are understood and managed.
Coordinate cross-region handoffs, dependencies, reporting, and follow-up so issues and initiatives continue moving across time zones and teams, escalating blockers to the Global Customer Success Lead when needed.
Performance and Continuous Improvement
Monitor key performance indicators, adoption, program activity, and service trends to assess account health and identify areas requiring attention.
Use data, shipment activity, event and incident trends, route performance, and customer feedback to identify patterns, gaps, and opportunities to improve program effectiveness, security outcomes, and customer operations.
Drive follow-through on root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement initiatives, and bring forward relevant Overhaul capabilities and best practices.
Cross-Functional Orchestration
Work closely with KAM/EAE, Sales, Operations, Support, Product, and other internal teams to ensure customer priorities are understood and advanced.
Own Customer Success coordination of regional escalations, ensuring the right teams are engaged, actions are clear, accountability is maintained, and customer communication is timely and accurate.
Partner with the commercial account team to identify opportunities to expand customer value, use cases, or adoption when aligned with the customer's needs.
What We Expect From You
Highly organized, proactive, and able to manage multiple priorities without losing sight of follow-through.
Strong ownership mindset with the ability to operate independently while working effectively as part of a global account team.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills with both operational teams and senior customer stakeholders.
Analytical mindset with the ability to use data to identify trends, frame problems, and drive decisions.
Ability to coordinate complex work across multiple internal teams and influence outcomes without direct authority.
Strong customer judgment and experience supporting complex customer programs.
Deep understanding of customer success best practices; experience in supply chain, logistics, transportation, cargo security, or technology-enabled operational programs is strongly preferred.
Comfort working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with a commitment to continuous improvement.
Fluency in English
Our Culture
We are guided by our core values of Diversity and Synergy, Creativity, Problem Solving, Authenticity and Receptivity, Trust, Encouragement, Teaching and Learning, Wellness and Integrity. These values help us recruit aligned talent to join our rapidly expanding team around the globe. It is important to us that each and every Overhauler is not only eager to challenge themselves and knows how to get work done, but is also an awesome addition to our company culture.
Equal Opportunity Employer
Overhaul is an equal opportunity employer. Our Overhaul Culture Code's top listed commitment is to "Diversity and Synergy." All aspects of employment will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law.

Threat Hunting

Atomic Testing & Security Validation

- Assist in determining attack scope, affected assets, root cause and attacker activities.

Description:
Overview
At Small Medium Enterprises and Channel (SME&C), we are leading a high-growth, AI-powered global sales team—one that is deeply connected to our partners and driven by customer success. By uniting our Small Medium Business, Corporate, Strategy, and Partner teams, we are unlocking the largest customer opportunity, backed by the industry’s most significant investments. Leveraging the power of AI and our extensive partner ecosystem, we are redefining how businesses of all sizes adopt technology to drive growth and innovation.
SME&C is more than a sales organization—it’s a culture of innovation, opportunity, and inclusivity. Here, you’ll be part of a diverse, high-performing, and customer-obsessed team where collaboration, connection, and continuous learning fuel everything we do.
If you thrive in a fast-paced, digital-first environment and are eager to make a meaningful impact, explore how SME&C can be the next step in your career. Together, we are shaping the future of business.

Responsibilities
The Digital Account Executive facilitates Microsoft to better serve our Medium Enterprise managed clients realize their potential and help them on their Digital Transformation journey. The Account Executive adds value by developing and maintaining strong customer relationships that include building relationships with executives at the Chief-level (CxO) as well as other Business and Technical Decision Makers within the customers’ organizations. The Digital Account Executive has to effectively leverage all the digital tools and processes available and orchestrate the other members of the team to address customer needs and requirements. Additionally, the Digital Account Executive engages with Partners to be able to find the best solution that will address the customer needs.
Efficiently orchestrate resources between different sales and specialized roles. Excel in key business processes such as territory management, pipeline management and overall business disciplines. Accountable for forecasting expected sales revenue.
Also the voice of the customer for Microsoft and share industry and competitive knowledge. This opportunity will allow you to accelerate your career growth, honing your sales and collaboration skills, and deepen cloud expertise.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Qualifications
Job Requirements
- Focuses on generating new pipeline by engaging with CXOs, ITDM and BDMs through territory planning, marketing signals and digital assets
- Central point maintaining strong customer relationships and advocates for customers within the organization/Microsoft.
- Surfaces customer organization structure to identify decision makers leveraging partners and v-teams.
- Engages with C-Suite executives. Focuses on customer satisfaction metrics. Takes ownership for issues and reaches out to customers to reinforce engagement.
- Ensures continuity of customer accounts and monitors customer satisfaction metrics by proactively establishing conditions of satisfaction at outset of engagement and managing escalation process
- Bachelor's Degree in Business Management, Information Technology, Marketing (or equivalent) or related field AND 6+ years sales and negotiation experience or related work experience OR 8+ years sales and negotiation experience OR equivalent experience
Account Management
- Thinks strategically about sales territory for accounts, setting standards and priorities, outlining where to and how to leverage specialized and technical resources and other roles, engaging internal and external decision makers on long-term business planning.
- Helps existing/new customers to cloud solutions via a cohesive plan across adds, consumption, , through upsell, co-sell motions, and renewal maximizing customer business outcomes and experience
- Understands and accelerates customer’s AI and cloud strategy.
- Builds enough pipeline to have a growing and sustainable business every single quarter.
Partnering
- Builds partner relationships to drive scale and revenue. Coaches and influences partners to consider different solution needs.
- Coordinates resources across teams to execute territory plans with partners. Leads teams on territory management best practices and techniques. Validates plans, drives accountability, and coaches teams to achieve or exceed plans. Drives strategic partner participation. Holds partners accountable to contribute to territory plan.
Maintain Product, Solution and Industry Expertise
- Proactively builds and maintains a strong knowledge of Microsoft's products, landscape, solutions, and strategy in the industry of assigned accounts, as well as of the business priorities; demonstrates a strong understanding of the customers' business strategy and the direction of the industry.
- Orchestrates specialized resources to engage with customers to provide strong solutions-based and technology-based engagement to help customers address their challenges and opportunities.

As Singapore’s longest established bank, we have been dedicated to enabling individuals and businesses to achieve their aspirations since 1932. How? By taking the time to truly understand people. Today, we’re on a journey of transformation. Leveraging technology and creativity to become a future-ready learning organisation. But for all that change, our strategic ambition is consistently clear and bold, which is to be Asia’s leading financial services partner for a sustainable future.

Help people grow their assets, business, and investments. Take your learning as far as you can. Or simply enjoy a vibrant, future-ready career.

Title: Digital Media Campaigns Analyst
Description:
Powering the agentic revolution in travel. Sabre is an AI-native technology leader, backed by one of the world’s largest travel data clouds. Built on an open, modular, cloud-native architecture, Sabre serves as the backbone for both established leaders and bold, new disruptors, guiding them to the next age of travel retailing through intelligent, connected, and personalized experiences. With AI at its core and operating at unparalleled scale, Sabre transforms insights into innovation, empowering airlines, hoteliers, agencies and other partners to retail, distribute and fulfill travel worldwide.
We are seeking a Media Campaigns Analyst to join our global Lodging, Ground and Media (LGM) team, where innovation knows no borders. The LGM team powers critical travel distribution and technology solutions that connect travel suppliers with buyers worldwide, creating seamless booking experiences and accelerating commercial growth across sectors. With an inclusive culture and flexible work environment, we work together with boldness, curiosity and commitment so we can all win together.
As a Media Campaigns Analyst, you will help deliver successful digital advertising campaigns across Sabre’s travel marketplace, including Sponsored Property and Display Advertising products. You will support campaigns from setup and optimization through performance reporting and billing reconciliation, using data to identify trends, investigate delivery issues and improve campaign effectiveness. You will work closely with Sales, Account Management, Product and Operations teams to deliver strong customer outcomes and maintain operational accuracy.
What you'll do
Manage digital advertising campaigns from setup and pacing through performance reporting and billing reconciliation.
Monitor campaign health using metrics including impressions, click-through rates (CTR), property participation, booking attribution, pacing and budget utilization.
Analyze performance trends, investigate delivery issues and recommend campaign optimizations.
Provide clear campaign reporting and actionable insights to internal teams and customers.
Partner across Sales, Account Management, Product and Operations to improve campaign performance and processes.
Identify opportunities to automate workflows and increase operational efficiency.
What you'll bring
Minimum 2 years of digital media experience, including campaign analysis and optimization.
Experience with digital advertising campaign management platforms or similar media tools; experience with Monetize is helpful but not required.
Strong analytical skills and attention to data accuracy.
Ability to interpret campaign performance and turn data into clear recommendations.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across teams, regions and time zones.
Ability to manage competing priorities and work independently.
Benefits that support you
We know support looks different for everyone. That is why Sabre offers benefits beyond medical and financial coverage, with programs designed to support your well-being, growth and life outside work:
Competitive pay and performance-based bonuses
Flexible work options
Comprehensive healthcare coverage
Generous PTO and holidays
Strong retirement planning support
Family-friendly benefits
Professional development opportunities

Title: Director
Description:
Job Overview
ULC Academy is seeking an experienced and commercially minded Director to oversee the overall management, business development and day-to-day operations of the Academy.
The successful candidate will work closely with the management team to develop and execute business strategies, improve operational efficiency, expand student enrolment and partnership channels, and ensure the sustainable growth of the Academy.
This position requires a hands-on leader who is comfortable managing both strategic planning and daily operational matters in a fast-paced education environment.
Key Responsibilities
Develop and implement the Academy's overall business and operational strategies.
Oversee daily operations and ensure effective coordination across academic, sales, marketing and administrative functions.
Establish annual and quarterly business targets and monitor performance against agreed objectives.
Lead business development initiatives to increase student enrolment and develop new revenue opportunities.
Identify and develop partnerships with companies, educational institutions, agencies and other external organisations.
Oversee the development and commercialisation of new education programmes and services.
Monitor sales performance, marketing activities, student acquisition and customer conversion.
Manage operational budgets, expenses and resource allocation to support sustainable business growth.
Recruit, manage and evaluate employees, including academic, sales and administrative staff.
Develop and improve internal policies, workflows and standard operating procedures.
Monitor service quality and student satisfaction and implement improvements where necessary.
Work with academic staff to ensure programmes are delivered effectively and meet the Academy's quality standards.
Ensure that the Academy's operations comply with applicable Singapore laws, regulations and internal policies.
Prepare regular management reports covering enrolment, revenue, operational performance and business development.
Represent the Academy in meetings, negotiations and discussions with business partners and other external stakeholders.
Perform other management duties reasonably required for the effective operation and development of the Academy.
Requirements
Diploma, Bachelor's Degree or equivalent professional qualification in Business Administration, Management, Education, Marketing or a related discipline.
At least 5 years of relevant working experience, preferably with experience in management, education, training, business development or service-related industries.
Demonstrated experience in managing business operations and leading teams.
Strong business development, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills.
Good understanding of sales, marketing and customer acquisition.
Ability to analyse business performance and translate data into practical action plans.
Strong organisational and problem-solving abilities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Able to work independently and take ownership of business and operational targets.
Comfortable working in a multicultural and international environment.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and common business productivity tools.
Preferred Qualifications
Previous experience in the education or private training sector in Singapore.
Experience managing an education centre, training centre or similar service-based business.
Experience developing B2B partnerships or corporate training programmes.
Experience managing international students and multicultural teams.
Familiarity with digital marketing, CRM systems and student acquisition processes will be an advantage.
What We Offer
Competitive monthly salary based on experience and qualifications.
Opportunity to take a senior leadership role in a growing education organisation.
Exposure to international students, corporate clients and education partners.
Opportunity to participate directly in the development of new programmes and business initiatives.
Career development opportunities based on performance and business growth.
About ULC Academy
Located in the heart of Orchard Road, ULC Academy is a premier language training institution dedicated to helping learners of all ages build real-world language confidence in a supportive, engaging environment.
We specialize in English programmes designed for both adults and young learners, offering a wide range of classes that cater to diverse goals and learning needs — from exam-focused preparation (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge English) to non-exam conversational courses for personal growth and professional development.
Whether you're preparing for university admission, looking to advance your career, or simply aiming to feel more confident in everyday conversations, our experienced team of educators is here to guide you every step of the way.
In addition to English, ULC Academy also offers Japanese, French, Spanish, and Chinese language programmes, taught by native or highly qualified instructors — all in a welcoming atmosphere right at the center of Singapore’s most vibrant shopping and business district.
Join our community of global learners and take the next step in your language journey with ULC Academy.

APAC

You will own the regional growth strategy for government partnerships, working closely with country teams and senior leadership to identify new opportunities, develop commercial strategies and build compelling business cases.

Title: Director of Housekeeping
Description:
Position Overview:
The Director of Housekeeping provides strategic and operational leadership for the Housekeeping Department, ensuring the highest standards of cleanliness, hygiene, presentation and upkeep are maintained across the entire Capella Singapore resort. The role holds overall accountability for the cleanliness of all guest rooms, suites, villas, Manors, Club Residences, public areas and back-of-house spaces, with cleanliness being the department's utmost priority. The Director leads the department in a proactive and strategically driven manner, anticipating operational needs and continuously identifying opportunities to enhance efficiency, quality and the guest experience. The role is responsible for establishing a strong culture of ownership, accountability, pride and continuous improvement, while ensuring that the Housekeeping team is supported, developed and well cared for. The Director manages departmental payroll, budgets, forecasting, productivity, staffing, supplies, linen, uniforms and equipment, ensuring resources are used responsibly without compromising standards. Through close collaboration with the Executive Committee and other departments, the Director ensures Housekeeping is fully aligned with the resort's operational, commercial and guest experience objectives. The role also leads quality assurance, training, talent development and succession planning to build a high-performing and sustainable team. Ultimately, the Director of Housekeeping acts as the guardian of the resort's cleanliness and presentation, ensuring every area consistently reflects the exceptional standards and attention to detail expected of Capella Singapore.
The Role:
Lead Housekeeping Operations
Lead and oversee all Housekeeping operations across the resort, including guest rooms, public areas, back-of-house areas, laundry, Long Stay Units, and linen management, ensuring the highest standards of cleanliness, presentation, operational efficiency, and consistency across all areas.
Ensure all guest rooms and public spaces meet established cleanliness and quality standards.
Conduct daily inspections of guest rooms, manors, long stay units, linen inventory, corridors, and public areas.
Implement and maintain housekeeping policies, procedures, and service standards to the highest level.
Coordinate with Front Office, In Room Dining, Engineering, Security, and other departments to ensure seamless operations.
Ensure prompt resolution of guest complaints and service recovery issues.
Monitor guest satisfaction scores and implement improvement initiatives.
Work proactively to enhance the overall guest experience.
Verify status on room reports, determine discrepant rooms, prioritize and update status of departing guest rooms.
Oversee linen, uniform, and housekeeping supply inventories.
Optimize daily housekeeping operations
Engage and maintain relationships with our current vendors and engage new vendors.
Manage replacement programs for linens, furnishings, and equipment.
Ensure that all Furniture, Fixtures and Equipment (FF&E) and Operating Supplies and Equipment (OS&E) are meticulously maintained, properly handled, and managed to the highest standards, preserving their quality, longevity, and presentation in line with Capella Singapore's luxury standards.
Ensure proper care and maintenance of housekeeping equipment.

Engage and drive a positive working relationship with all other departments.

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Join us to put AI to work for people.
Job Description
Location: APAC (Singapore based)
Reports to: GVP APAC Channels & Partnerships
We're looking for an experienced partnerships leader to own a portfolio of ServiceNow's most strategic APAC relationships — a mix of partnerships you build from zero and mature partnerships you manage and grow. You'll also own GSI Route-to-Market strategy for the region, acting as the main link between global GSI teams and the APAC field.
This Is a Builder-and-operator Role Spanning Two Distinct Halves
Build: spot white space, make the business case, negotiate terms, and stand-up new partnerships end to end.
Own GSI RTM for APAC: translate global partnership strategy and programs into regional execution, act as primary escalation point across APAC and global teams, run and represent APAC in partner QBRs and global forums, and land best practices into GSI Partner Managers' day-to-day work.
Responsibilities
- Identify partnership white space across APAC, build the business case, negotiate terms, and launch new partnerships end to end.
- Own a balanced portfolio of net-new and established partners, building joint business plans and measuring execution against shared targets.
- Partner with Marketing to develop joint campaigns and events, tracking pipeline contribution and performance.
- Own APAC GSI route-to-market strategy, connecting global GSI partnership priorities with regional sales and partnerships execution.
- Lead partner QBRs and represent APAC in global partnership forums, reporting partner health and pipeline contribution to regional and global leadership.
- Serve as the escalation point for portfolio priorities, coordinating resolution across APAC and global partnership teams.
- Coach GSI Partner Managers on GTM planning, demand generation, sales acceleration, industry solutions, and partner capacity-building.

- 8+ years in partnerships, alliances, or channel roles, including direct GSI experience with firms such as TCS, Accenture, Deloitte, EY, Infosys, KPMG, or similar.

About Stemgenic
Stemgenic is a Singapore-headquartered boutique executive search and career advisory firm specialising in leadership and business-critical functional roles across industrial and scientific sectors in APAC. As we continue to expand, we are looking for an entrepreneurial search leader to establish and grow our Mission Critical & Industrial Infrastructure practice across APAC. This is an opportunity for an established recruitment professional who wants to move beyond running a successful desk and take ownership of building a specialist business within a growing firm.
The Opportunity
You will take full ownership of the Mission Critical & Industrial Infrastructure practice, covering data centres, pharmaceutical and life sciences facilities, food and chemical plants, and other mission-critical and high-tech buildings across design, construction, commissioning and operations. You will shape its market strategy, build client partnerships, deliver executive search mandates and drive commercial performance. Initially, this will be a hands-on billing leadership role, with the opportunity to progressively build and lead a team as the business scales.
What You Will Do
Own the Mission Critical & Industrial Infrastructure desk across APAC and set its strategy, client focus and growth plan
Build and deepen trusted relationships with senior stakeholders and HR partners at developers, owner-operators, EPC and design firms, MEP contractors and critical equipment suppliers
Win and deliver retained and exclusive executive search mandates, from brief to offer
Drive revenue, placements and desk growth as a hands-on individual contributor
Grow the practice over time by hiring and developing consultants to build a team around the desk
Represent Stemgenic in the sector through networking, industry events and thought leadership
What We Are Looking For

Title: Director, Commercial Excellence APAC
Description:
Driven by the passion to improve quality of people’s lives, WSA continues to grow as market leader in the hearing aid industry. With our commitment to increase penetration in an underserved hearing care market, we want to accelerate our business transformation in order to reach more people, more effectively.
This pivotal role is central to setting the agenda and standard for commercial excellence across APAC. As Director, Commercial Excellence APAC, you will own the design and rollout of WSA's Commercial Excellence program, embedding the Smart Lean methodology into how every country team operates. Reporting to the Regional President, APAC, you will drive commercial excellence in the region — building the program in partnership with global teams, training markets in it, and ensuring it becomes the operating rhythm of every country's commercial approached.
What you will do
Partner with global teams to build and shape WSA's Commercial Excellence program for APAC, ensuring it reflects both global standards and regional commercial realities.
Own the integration and rollout of the Smart Lean methodology into commercial excellence, embedding it as a core operating discipline across the region.
Train and upskill the region in WSA's commercial excellence agenda, maintaining a consistently high standard across all APAC markets.
Champion commercial excellence at the country level, working closely with country commercial teams to ensure the program sits at the center of their day-to-day ways of working.
What you bring
Experience
5+ years of commercial experience, complemented by a minimum of 5 years leading project and change management initiatives, with formal change management qualification.
Smart Lean trained and experienced, with a track record of embedding the methodology into real commercial operations.
Strong interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to bring diverse country teams along through complex transformation.
Experienced working across multiple countries or multinational contexts, able to adapt a regional agenda to fit varied market realities.
Performance and personal competencies
A results-driven high performer with a strong “can-do” attitude
Willing to drive organizational change
Drive, determination and high standards. Resilience, high energy and a ‘can-do’ attitude
Results orientated, accountable, and leads by example, raising standards
Influential, make an impact, drive the teams and act as role model
A people-oriented person who is always looking for solutions and bringing quality and efficiency improvements.
Who we are
At WSA, we provide innovative hearing aids and hearing health services.
Together with our 12,000 colleagues in 130 countries, we invite you to help unlock human potential by bringing back hearing for millions of people around the world.
With us, you will become part of a truly global company where we care for one another, welcome diversity and celebrate our successes.
Sounds wonderful? We can't wait to hear from you.
WSA is an equal-opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive employee experience for all. Regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, medical condition, ancestry, disability, military or veteran status we firmly believe that our work is at its best when everyone feels free to be their most authentic self.
WSAudiology is formed in 2019, through the merger of Sivantos and Widex, WS Audiology combines over 140 years of experience in pioneering the use of technology to help people with hearing loss hear the sounds that make life wonderful. We are active in over 125 markets and employ 11,000 people worldwide. Our broad portfolio of hearing-related products and services generates annual revenues of around EUR 2 billion.
As advanced as hearing care is today, we are dedicated to making it even better. Our people have a passion for innovation and are committed to applying it to help make a wonderful sound part of everyone’s life.
There is nothing more rewarding to us than seeing someone regain the miracle of hearing and watching them thrive. As a leader in our industry, we have already helped improve the lives of millions of people, but there is more to be done.
WSAudiology Singapore employs more than 1,300 people across a variety of functions. Here, we host numerous global functions such as Manufacturing & Supply Chain, Quality, IT, Legal, and HR. We also develop and manufacture state-of-the-art behind-the-ear hearing aid devices for our global markets.

www.wsa.com

The Sellers & Fintech Partnerships team is responsible for identifying, structuring, closing and managing strategic partnerships, alliances and commercial deals. The fintech partnerships team works closely with Visa’s Product and Solutions teams (functions and services) to identify and pursue a new client base of Issuing & Acquiring platforms and various service providers and ecosystem participants in the payments industry across Asia Pacific.
What a Director, Fintech Partnerships Does At Visa
The Director, Fintech Partnerships is responsible for driving end-to-end partnership growth across the Singapore fintech ecosystem, from opportunity identification and business development through solution design, commercial structuring and commercialization.
This role requires a recognized fintech and payments specialist with deep market knowledge, strong industry connections and a proven ability to create new business opportunities. The successful candidate will be responsible for developing strategic partnerships that accelerate adoption of Visa's capabilities while delivering mutual growth for Visa and its partners.
Given the rapid evolution of digital money movement, the candidate should be well versed in stablecoins, tokenized payments, and the broader digital asset ecosystem. They should possess a strong understanding of the regulatory landscape, emerging business models, and the role stablecoins can play in cross-border payments, treasury, settlement, and programmable commerce. The individual will be expected to identify, develop and commercialize partnerships with stablecoin issuers, digital asset platforms, wallets, infrastructure providers and other ecosystem participants that align with Visa's strategic priorities.
While the primary market focus is Singapore, the role may support selected opportunities across Asia Pacific where ecosystem relationships, partnerships or growth opportunities align with Visa's strategic priorities.

Strategic Account Management and Business Development Ecosystem Growth:
- Own and manage key fintech and digital asset client relationships, ensuring strategic alignment with regional and global priorities while identifying opportunities to deepen partnerships and accelerate business growth
- Identify, develop and execute high-impact partnerships across fintechs, digital banks, payment service providers, embedded finance platforms and emerging ecosystem participants.
- Build strong business development and hunting capabilities to identify new opportunities and emerging business models.
- Leverage industry relationships and ecosystem intelligence to identify opportunities before they become mainstream market initiatives.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with founders, investors, accelerators and ecosystem influencers
Solutioning & Partnership Development
- Work closely with partners to understand customer needs, business models, customer journeys and growth objectives.
- Translate strategic opportunities into scalable payment and commerce solutions leveraging Visa's capabilities.
- Act as a solution integrator by bringing together internal products, services and partners to address client needs.
- Advise internal stakeholders on emerging fintech trends, technologies and ecosystem developments.
Commercialization & Deal Execution
- Lead complex partnership opportunities from origination through negotiation, contracting, launch and revenue realization.
- Build business cases, commercial models and partnership strategies that drive measurable business outcomes.

Title: Director, Investments - Asset Management
Description:
Position Overview:
Clifford Capital Asset Management (“CCAM”) is a new line of business that was established in December 2024. CCAM is regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (the “MAS”) and holds a Capital Market Service License to conduct fund management activities for accredited and institutional investors. CCAM will focus on launching mandates as well as collective investment schemes. CCAM products are expected to invest in range of credit instruments including but not limited to senior credit, subordinated debt/high yield as well as hybrid instruments representing debt financing.
Primary Responsibilities:
Work closely with origination, corporate coverage and investor coverage teams to source, assess and execute infrastructure credit investment opportunities across CCAM-managed pools of capital
Lead credit due diligence, investment analysis, financial modelling, structuring assessment and risk evaluation for primary and secondary market opportunities
Build and maintain relationships with banks, sponsors, intermediaries, investors and other market participants to strengthen CCAM’s market presence and access to investment opportunities
Prepare and present investment recommendations, credit papers and portfolio updates to CCAM’s Investment Committee, senior management and relevant governance forums
Drive the internal credit application and approval process, coordinating inputs from origination, risk, legal, operations and other relevant stakeholders
Undertake upfront and ongoing relative value analysis, portfolio monitoring, asset performance review and portfolio management activities across relevant mandates and funds
Support investor marketing, fundraising and due diligence processes by providing investment insights, portfolio information and market perspectives as required
Act as deal captain for selected transactions, providing end-to-end transaction leadership and, over time, supervising and mentoring junior investment team members
Professional Experience / Qualifications:
At least 10 years of relevant experience in infrastructure credit, private credit, project finance, leveraged finance, structured finance, asset management or a related investment role within a financial institution or investment platform
Strong academic background, with demonstrated investment judgement and experience in credit analysis, investment structuring, financial modelling and investment committee processes
Strong understanding of infrastructure, private credit and APAC markets; experience across global infrastructure debt markets or cross-border transactions would be advantageous
Proven ability to manage multiple transactions and portfolio priorities independently, with strong execution discipline, commercial judgement and attention to detail
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the maturity and credibility to engage senior management, investment committees, investors, counterparties and external advisers
Business-level Japanese language skills are advantageous for engaging with Japanese investors and counterparties
Headquartered in Singapore and established in 2012, Clifford Capital is an infrastructure credit financing platform for real assets globally across the debt capital structure. The Group is increasingly pivoting towards areas such as clean energy, energy transition, social and digital infrastructure, electrification, and maritime decarbonisation to address the challenges posed by environmental, social and governance issues globally, and in particular within the Asia Pacific region. Its ambition is to deliver innovative financing solutions that positively influence sustainability and deliver commercial returns for its shareholders.
Clifford Capital aims to build a globally competitive alternative asset management and financing platform closely aligned to Singapore’s objectives of creating a centre of excellence in financial markets focused on sustainability and green finance.
Clifford Capital’s shareholders comprise Temasek Holdings, Prudential Assurance Company Singapore, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Standard Chartered Bank, DBS Bank, John Hancock Life Insurance Company (Manulife), and the Asian Development Bank.

Job Summary
The purpose of this role is to act as the primary point of contact within the Second Line Operational, Technology and Cyber Risk (OTCR) function for the Corporate and Investment Banking business (the Business), covering all non‑financial risk matters across operational processes, technology platforms, information security and cyber resilience.
The role provides independent oversight, challenge and assurance to ensure that the Business identifies, assesses, manages and escalates Operational, Technology and Cyber risks in line with the Group’s Enterprise Risk Management Framework (ERMF) and the OTCR Risk Type Framework, and that material risks and control weaknesses are transparently governed.
Key Responsibilities
This role includes responsibility for monitoring, reviewing and challenging the Business’s adherence to its obligations under the Operational, Technology and Cyber Risk frameworks, ensuring that:
• Material risks across operations, systems, technology resilience, cyber security and data are appropriately identified and assessed;
• Controls are designed, implemented and operating effectively; and
• Breaches, incidents and weaknesses are escalated in line with appetite, policy and governance requirements.
This is delivered through close collaboration with other Second Line risk teams, including Technology Risk, Information & Cyber Security (ICS), Third Party Risk and relevant Centres of Excellence, as well as enterprise‑wide SMEs.
The role holder is expected to demonstrate deep subject matter expertise in one or more OTCR domains, including:
• Operational and process risk within Corporate and Investment Banking;
• Technology risk, system stability, resilience and change delivery;
• Information and Cyber Security risk, including data protection and control frameworks.
• The role holder must understand the interdependencies between operational processes, technology platforms and cyber vulnerabilities, and how weaknesses in one domain can amplify risk in another.
• Coverage includes all Second Line responsibilities within the Group’s Enterprise Risk Management Framework (‘ERMF’). This includes oversight, review and challenge of all risk decision making within the Business.
From a regulatory perspective, the role requires a strong understanding of global supervisory expectations relating to operational resilience, technology risk and cyber security, including banks’ obligations to demonstrate robust identification, monitoring and control of risks arising from end‑to‑end processes, critical systems and digital infrastructure
• The role holder is expected to understand how these requirements are embedded within the OTCR Risk Type Framework, and how they interact with other Risk Type Frameworks under the ERMF.
• The Second Line OTCR function is responsible for independent oversight and challenge, ensuring that risks are appropriately identified, assessed, controlled and managed within risk appetite, and that material issues are escalated, tracked and remediated. The role holder is accountable for leading the delivery of Second Line OTCR responsibilities for the CIB business, including continuous improvement of risk transparency, control effectiveness and governance outcomes.
Business
• Demonstrate deep understanding of the Business strategic priorities to effectively advise and challenge decisions across all relevant Risk Types. Demonstrated experience/SME in an equivalent 1st line/2nd line role managing one or more areas of the Business particularly Operations is a strong plus.
• Review and recommend resolutions to risk-related escalations from the Business, keeping in mind Operational, Technology and Cyber Risk Appetite thresholds, policies, and procedures.
• Work with OTCR Policy team to clarify / interpret any policy-related matters or queries from the Business.
• Identify internal / external insights and emerging risks that can impact the Business.
• Attend relevant Business Risk committees representing Risk in advising, challenging and providing Risk insights to business stakeholders.
The role-holder is also responsible for taking a lead in ensuring that the Business adheres to agreed Operational, Technology and Cyber Risk Appetite, including supporting the Business in defining its Operational, Technology and Cyber Risk strategy in conjunction with Group Internal Audit. This includes the challenging of the Business strategy and Corporate Plan and seeking to embed awareness and engagement with all Operational, Technology and Cyber Risk sub-types across the Business.
This will be achieved through partnership, challenge and control as follows:

Title: Director, Partnerships, Greater China (Singapore)
Description:
About The Role
About the role
Shopify has no office in mainland China, Hong Kong, or Taiwan. This role is what we have instead.
Chinese merchants are building some of the fastest growing direct-to-consumer brands in the world, and they are building them for customers outside China. Greater China export is a top global priority, with product, infrastructure, and go-to-market investment landing behind it now. None of it reaches merchants without partners, and no partner in this market commits to a platform they have not met in person.
You are the face of Shopify partnerships in Greater China. In market, in the room, at the dinner, on the stage. You build the relationships that turn into merchants, and you find the opportunities nobody has written down yet.
You build on an ecosystem of more than a thousand active agencies, system integrators, developers, and technology partners, alongside the domestic commerce platforms that hundreds of thousands of Chinese merchants already sell on. Uniquely across Asia Pacific, technology partners here outnumber agencies, which changes what the ecosystem can do and how you build it. You own it end to end, and you are accountable for what it produces: merchants launched, merchants that survive and grow, and a partner base that gets measurably better at Shopify every quarter.
The work is genuinely unfinished. Partner capability is uneven, merchant success after launch is low, and the operating model is still being built. You will be making calls with incomplete data, in a market that moves faster than most, on one of the biggest openings Shopify has.
What you'll own
- Agency and SI partnerships across mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, including the managed partner portfolio and the team that runs it.
- Technology partnerships, including export-focused partners and the global platform relationships that matter most here.
- The import motion, currently run centrally and transitioning to you.
- Platform and joint venture relationships, including the domestic commerce platforms that are our most scalable route into the merchant long tail.
- A growing in-market team, including a Partner Solutions Engineer and a Partner Marketing Manager, both new roles.
What you'll do
Be Shopify in this market
- Be in market constantly. Partner offices, factory floors, merchant warehouses, industry events, dinners. Deals here get made in person, by people who keep showing up.
- Build a personal network at the top of the ecosystem: agency founders, platform executives, trade association leaders, and the category leaders in the export verticals that matter. Be the call they take.
- Create opportunities that are not on anyone's plan. Invent the pilot, the coalition, the program, the event. Test it with a handful of partners in weeks and scale what works.
- Move at the speed of the market. A good idea executed this month beats a better idea next quarter.
- Carry Shopify's story publicly: stage, press, WeChat, industry forums, partner communities. Be the reason a Chinese founder has heard of us.
Own the Greater China partner strategy
- Set the partner strategy for mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan: which partners we recruit, which we invest in, which we scale, and which we let go. Reason from first principles rather than the orthodox answer, and defend those calls with evidence.
- Build the partner base against where merchant demand is actually going: cross-border D2C, brand building in Western markets, and enterprise migration off local and legacy platforms.
Drive launches, merchant success, and partner capability
- Own the volume and the quality of partner-led merchant launches. Chinese agency partners already launch hundreds of stores every quarter. Far too few of those merchants go on to succeed.
- Hold partners accountable for what happens after launch, not just at it: traffic, conversion, and merchant survival. This is the number that matters most in this market.
- Own partner-sourced pipeline and the commercial relationship with the Greater China sales, solutions engineering, and marketing teams, and lift partner-led merchants into higher value plans.
- Most Chinese sellers compete on price and product rather than brand, and lack the fundamentals of Western direct-to-consumer commerce. Build the enablement model that makes partners genuinely good at teaching this, in market and in language, and take them from selling Shopify to architecting and delivering on it.
- Localize Shopify product launches and roadmap changes so partners can act on them in weeks rather than quarters.
Build a scaled motion into the long tail
- The long tail of Chinese export merchants is the largest opportunity here and the most expensive to serve directly. Design the motion that reaches it: partner-delivered, platform-delivered, and product-delivered rather than headcount-delivered.
- Own the relationships with domestic commerce platforms that can acquire and train merchants at scale on our behalf, including train-the-trainer models that use their existing sales and operations teams. Prove the unit economics before we scale, and kill what does not work.
Build and lead the team
- Lead and grow a distributed, in-market team with clear ownership, high standards, and a high pace. Onboard new roles as they land, absorb the responsibilities currently held centrally, and build the team through addition and subtraction.
- Coach the craft yourself. You will be in partner meetings, on deal reviews, and in the detail, not managing from a dashboard.
- Be the credible internal voice for Greater China with Shopify's global partnerships, product, and commercial leadership. Surface problems early, with a solution attached.
Multiply the market's impact with AI
- Merchant willingness to pay for professional services here is very low. AI is the most credible way to serve a long tail that will not pay for people, so push AI adoption into the partner ecosystem and into the tooling partners put in front of merchants.
- Use AI across your own work and your team's. Aim for what was not possible before, not marginal time savings, and own the output whether AI generated it or not.
What success looks like
Within your first six months, you will have:
- Built a named relationship map across the top agencies, technology partners, platforms, and industry bodies in the region, with you personally connected at decision-maker level across most of it.
- At least two opportunities in flight that were not on the plan when you joined, sourced from your own network and time in market.
- Published a clear Greater China partner strategy across agencies, technology partners, import, and platform relationships, with a named portfolio, explicit investment choices, and the metrics you own.
- Improved the quality of partner-led launches, with evidence that merchants launched by partners are surviving and growing, and delivered against partner-sourced pipeline targets.
- Stood up at least one scaled long-tail motion with real merchant volume and unit economics you can defend.
- Onboarded the new in-market roles, absorbed the responsibilities transitioning to you, and become the person the Greater China commercial, product, and marketing teams call when they need a door opened.
What you'll bring
- An existing, activatable network across the Greater China partner landscape: agencies and system integrators, technology partners, domestic commerce platforms, potential joint venture partners, and industry and trade associations. You should be able to open doors in your first weeks, not your first year.
- Evidence you create opportunities rather than manage them. You have built something from nothing: a market, a business, a category, a partner motion. You can point at deals that exist only because you made them exist.
- Presence and persuasion. You can hold a room, host a table of founders, and be the person they want to work with. Here the relationship comes before the contract.
- Relentless energy, and the follow-through to convert it.
- Ten or more years in partnerships, channel, alliances, or ecosystem roles with significant time in Greater China, or an unconventional path that produced the same network and the same results.
- Native Mandarin language proficiencies to liaise with clients in the Greater China Region and professional English. You can hold a technical discussion with a partner CTO in one and a commercial forecast review with global leadership in the other.
- Deep knowledge of the Chinese export ecommerce ecosystem, and enough credibility on brand building and Western direct-to-consumer fundamentals to be taken seriously by a merchant who has only ever competed on price.
- A record of owning a business outcome through partners, not just relationships, with the discipline to forecast it and hit it, and experience building a leveraged motion where reach grew faster than headcount.
- Experience leading distributed teams across markets and time zones, and comfort with ambiguity: incomplete data, evolving tooling, and a strategy being written as you go.
- Technical fluency with software platforms and integrations, enough to hold a credible conversation with a partner about what they are building.
- Demonstrated use of AI in your day-to-day craft, with examples of how it changed your scale, speed, or quality of decisions, and strong written communication. Much of your influence at Shopify is exercised in writing, to people you have never met.
Nice to have
- Experience in commerce, ecommerce, or SaaS, particularly cross-border.
- Cantonese, in addition to Mandarin and English.
- Experience standing up a partner motion in a market without a local Shopify presence.
How you work
- You would rather be in a partner's office than an internal meeting.
- You are unorthodox. You find the angle nobody else saw, and you test it before anyone gives you permission.
- You ruthlessly prioritize. Mission critical work gets resourced and everything else stops, and your team knows the difference.
- You ship weekly, not quarterly.
- You take extreme ownership. You dive deep into the details of your team's work and you own its mistakes.
- You invite challenge, including your own ideas, and you let the best idea win. You resolve conflict rather than route around it.
- You put Shopify first, ahead of the org, the team, and yourself.
How this role is structured
This is a build-phase role inside a dedicated, in-market China team. Ecosystem aim and strategy for the market is set by Shopify's VP of Product for China. You own partner strategy and execution against that aim, and you report to the Director of Partnerships for Asia Pacific.
You are the most senior Shopify partnerships leader in Greater China and you carry that externally. The title exists to open doors. Use it.
As the in-market team is staffed through the coming year, the longer term reporting structure will be confirmed. Expect to help shape it rather than inherit it. If a settled org chart is what you need to do your best work, this is not the right role.
Location and travel
Based in Singapore, working standard Greater China business hours with flexibility for teams in Singapore, Australia, and North America.
Expect to be on the road at least half your time across mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, plus occasional regional and global travel. This is not a role you can run from a desk in Singapore.
About Shopify
Opportunity is not evenly distributed. Shopify puts independence within reach for anyone with a dream to start a business. We propel entrepreneurs and enterprises to scale the heights of their potential. Since 2006, we’ve grown to over 8,300 employees and generated over $1 trillion in sales for millions of merchants in 175 countries.
This is life-defining work that directly impacts people’s lives as much as it transforms your own. This is putting the power of the few in the hands of the many, is a future with more voices rather than fewer, and is creating more choices instead of an elite option.
About You
Moving at our pace brings a lot of change, complexity, and ambiguity—and a little bit of chaos. Shopifolk thrive on that and are comfortable being uncomfortable. That means Shopify is not the right place for everyone.
Before you apply, consider if you can:
- Care deeply about what you do and about making commerce better for everyone
- Excel by seeking professional and personal hypergrowth
- Keep up with an unrelenting pace (the week, not the quarter)
- Be resilient and resourceful in face of ambiguity and thrive on (rather than endure) change
- Bring critical thought and opinion
- Put AI agents and tools to work on the tasks they're built for, and focus on the work only humans can do
- Embrace differences and disagreement to get shit done and move forward
- Work digital-first for your daily work

Title: Director, Restaurant & Bars Partnerships - Asia Pacific
Description:
Operating at the intersection of Development, Brand and Operations, this role is responsible for sourcing, structuring and executing strategic restaurant and bar partnerships across Hilton’s Asia Pacific (APAC) portfolio and pipeline. The Director of Restaurant & Bar Partnerships will secure high-impact collaborations with leading restaurant groups, brands and chefs to enhance guest experience, strengthen brand positioning and drive owner returns.
This is a newly created, entrepreneurial role requiring a commercially driven leader with strong industry credibility, deep networks and the ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy across a complex, multi-market environment. The position plays a critical role in supporting Hilton’s growth ambitions by enabling compelling F&B propositions that drive deal competitiveness, enhance asset value and elevate brand differentiation across the region.
This role will sit within APAC Brand team and report directly into Vice President, F&B Brand Operations - APAC. The APAC Brand function is responsible for ensuring that Hilton’s global brands are an attractive investment value proposition for owners and that they deliver experiences which attract, excite, and inspire guests in the APAC region.
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT
Your role is important, and below are some of the fundamental job duties that make your work unique.
1. Strategy & Pipeline Development
- Develop and execute the APAC Restaurant & Bars Partnership strategy aligned with global and regional growth priorities
- Identify opportunities across existing hotels and pipeline assets to introduce branded, leased or partner-led F&B concepts
- Build and manage a robust pipeline of partnership opportunities across key gateway cities and high-growth markets
2. Sourcing & Partnerships
- Source leading restaurant groups, brands, chefs and investors for existing properties and new hotel developments, including franchise, lease and chef-led models
- Maintain deep market insight into restaurant, consumer and operator trends across benchmark cities such as Singapore, Shanghai, Tokyo, New York, Los Angeles, Dubai and London
3. Deal Structuring & Execution
- Lead commercial negotiations and structure partnership models, including leases, operating agreements, franchise arrangements and chef-led partnerships
- Drive transactions from origination through to execution in collaboration with Development, Legal, Operations and Finance
- Navigate complex deal structures and proactively resolve issues to ensure timely and efficient execution
4. Commercial & Financial Performance
- Partner with Finance and Feasibility teams to evaluate ROI, P&L contribution and value creation of partnership models
- Ensure partnerships deliver strong commercial outcomes aligned with owner expectations and brand positioning
- Support risk mitigation, including exit strategies where required
5. Stakeholder Management
- Serve as Hilton’s primary interface with external restaurant and bar partners across the region
- Collaborate with Development, Brand and Operations to review, select and implement restaurant and bar partners across markets, brands and locations
6. Governance & Tracking
- Track and manage all restaurant and bar partnership projects across APAC
- Maintain oversight of contractual agreements and partner performance
- Ensure consistent reporting and communication across internal stakeholders
Success Measures
- Number and quality of strategic F&B partnerships signed annually
- Incremental revenue and profitability contribution to owners and Hilton
- Adoption of partnership models across pipeline and existing portfolio
- Speed and efficiency of deal sourcing and execution
- Strength and depth of external partner network
- Guest satisfaction and repeat partnership engagement
WHY YOU’LL BE A GREAT FIT
You have these minimum qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
- 10+ years of experience in hospitality, preferably within hotels, including at least 5 years in restaurant franchising, leasing or partnership structures
- Proven track record of sourcing and executing commercial deals with restaurant groups, brands, chefs and operators
- Experience structuring lease, franchise, operating and chef-led agreements
- Strong regional exposure and relevant experience across APAC
- Strong commercial acumen with a sound understanding of F&B and real estate economics
- Advanced negotiation skills with the ability to structure complex, high-value transactions
- Highly credible externally, with established industry relationships
- Strategic thinker with the ability to translate market trends into scalable opportunities
- Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills across senior levels
- Self-starter with the ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, multi-market environment
- Willingness to travel across APAC (~50%)
It would be useful if you have:
- Proficiency in Asian language to support APAC region

At Crocs, Inc., every career offers a chance to make a real impact. No two journeys look the same. And that's exactly how we like it.
