Title: EVENT OPERATIONS MANAGER
Description:
Job Description & Requirements
Job Overview
We are seeking an experienced and detail-oriented
Event Operations Manager
to oversee the end-to-end operational planning, logistics, and on-site execution of live events, productions, and entertainment experiences. This role leads operational workflows from concept to post-event teardown, ensuring high production standards, strict budget control, venue compliance, and seamless guest experiences.
Key Responsibilities
Operations & Production Management:
Lead end-to-end operational planning and on-site execution for corporate, public, and live entertainment events.
Vendor & Contractor Coordination:
Source, negotiate with, and supervise vendors for audio-visual (AV), staging, lighting, logistics, ticketing, catering, and security.
Permits & Regulatory Compliance:
Secure necessary venue approvals, police permits, SCDF fire safety clearances, and public entertainment licenses in accordance with Singapore statutory requirements.
Risk Assessment & Safety:
Develop and implement crowd management plans, emergency response protocols, and Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) guidelines for bump-in, event duration, and teardown.
Budget & Resource Planning:
Manage operational budgets, monitor run rates, allocate internal/external resources efficiently, and minimize operational wastage.
Team Supervision:
Lead, train, and deploy full-time production crews, part-time event staff, and freelance technicians to ensure seamless coordination on show days.
Post-Event Review:
Manage inventory returns, venue handover inspections, vendor reconciliation, and operational post-mortem reports.
Requirements & Qualifications
Diploma or Degree in Event Management, Operations Management, Hospitality, or a related field.
Minimum 3–5 years of hands-on event operations or live entertainment production experience.
Proven track record managing large-scale event logistics, venue setup/strike, and technical production teams.
Strong familiarity with local venue regulations, statutory licensing, and WSH compliance in Singapore.
Excellent negotiation, conflict resolution, and crisis management skills under tight deadlines.
Willingness to work irregular hours, including evenings, weekends, and public holidays, based on event schedules.

The Singapore Mint was established in 1968 to mint circulation coins for the newly-independent nation. Over the years, The Singapore Mint has evolved from a basic minting facility to a fully integrated business operation, comprising programme concept, product design, marketing, sales and distribution with after sales service. Focusing on quality system and standards, The Singapore Mint is a certified ISO 9001 and 14001 organisation. Today, it has grown to become one of the leading innovative mints in the industry, capable of producing coins and medallions of the highest quality.
Leveraging on technology, The Singapore Mint has developed hybrid techniques to create high security and innovative features on circulation and commemorative coins and collectables. Fusing advanced minting technologies with authentic crafting methods, The Singapore Mint is one of the few mints in the world that still maintains a team of highly skilled craftsmen, adding intricate elements that can only be meticulously achieved by the human touch.
As a testament of its high quality crafting techniques, The Singapore Mint has won multiple international awards and its rising stature has garnered much interest internationally. The mint has been appointed by issuing authorities around the world for the production of their coins.
Other than producing coins and medallions, The Singapore Mint has also expanded to provide quality currency-related gifts and collectibles, lifestyle products and services to both local and international markets. We continue to pledge our unwavering commitment to our customers, business associates and partners to offer the best in quality, value and service.
The Singapore Mint (Singapore Precision Industries Pte Ltd) is a fully owned subsidiary of Sembcorp Industries.

Lead and manage catering staff, providing training and guidance as needed.
Foster a positive and collaborative environment on-site

Work closely with culinary, operations, and sales teams to ensure effective cross-departmental collaboration.

This role sits at the heart of our events business — bringing to life memorable experiences across some of Singapore's most iconic F&B brands. Whether it's an intimate dinner at Jiak Kim House, a craft beer celebration at Brewerkz, or a vibrant fiesta at Café Iguana, you'll be the person who makes it happen.
We're looking for a self-driven, personable go-getter who loves building relationships, closing deals, and growing a business. This is a pure sales role — ideal for fresh graduates or individuals with up to a year of experience who are ready to kickstart a career in F&B events and business development. Our Brands
Brewerkz
– Singapore's longest-running craft brewery, with six thriving restaurants and a proud Made with Passion brand
Café Iguana
– serving modern Mexican food and a pioneer in Singapore's Mexican dining scene since 2000
Jiak Kim House

Responsibilities
This role will report directly to Head of Marketing and work closely with outlet teams, the central marketing team, and external vendors. Your main responsibilities include:
Promote, sell, and secure group bookings and event enquiries
Manage inbound leads, prepare proposals and quotations, handle follow-ups, and confirm event bookings
Conduct site visits and present venue offerings professionally
Coordinate with operations teams to ensure smooth sales handover and execution
Liaise with third-party vendors when required to meet client expectations (e.g. florists, AV, décor)
Build and maintain a healthy sales pipeline; track leads and conversions
Maintain accurate sales records and provide reports with insights and recommendations
Identify upselling opportunities and stay aware of market trends and competitor offerings
Drive new business through cold outreach, on-site networking, and proactive client engagement
Deliver excellent pre-sale service that leaves clients excited to come back
Support company initiatives and new projects as and when required

Fresh graduates or candidates with up to 1 year of experience in sales, events, hospitality, or customer-facing roles are welcome
Outgoing and confident communicator with strong interpersonal skills

Title: Events Executive (Govt and Corporate)
Description:
ABOUT THE ROLE
This is a role for someone who decides what needs to happen and drives it to delivery, without needing to be reminded twice. Progression is earned through outcomes, not time served. This is an entry point, not a fast-track.
At PurpleForest, successful events are delivered by people who take ownership, solve problems and care about outcomes. As an Events Executive, you will work closely with managers and project teams while owning your outcomes end-to-end.
The role spans client management and business development, giving you a broad view of how projects are won, delivered and closed.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Own Defined Project Outcomes: Take accountability for scoped outcomes, delivering them accurately, professionally and on time, not just completing assigned activities.
Earn Client Confidence: Understand client needs, communicate proactively and follow through on commitments to build trust and future opportunities.
Drive Projects Forward: Maintain momentum by aligning timelines, vendors and requirements, anticipating dependencies and resolving matters without repeated reminders.
Solve Problems Proactively: Anticipate risks and implement practical solutions within your scope before they affect the client, project or team.
Contribute to Business Growth: Spot areas to add client value, help develop proposals and quotations, and follow-up with suitable opportunities.
Deliver and Close Well: Own delivery outcomes from planning through execution and closure, aligning operational details and commitments to the required standard.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
Relevant Experience: 2–3 years of experience in events, project management, account servicing or a client-facing role, including clear examples of independently moving work forward and delivering agreed outcomes.
Ownership & Initiative: A track record of taking responsibility for outcomes and following through without needing repeated direction, even under shifting priorities.
Communication & Commercial Awareness: A confident communicator who moves proposals and opportunities forward without being asked twice.
Team Accountability and Adaptability: Collaborate effectively while remaining personally accountable for your outcomes, raising issues early and maintaining quality and follow-through when priorities or requirements change.
WHAT WE OFFER
Base Salary: SGD $3,500 – SGD $4,000
Meaningful Ownership:Your name is attached to real projects and real client relationships, not just tasks assigned by others.
Diverse Project Exposure:Work across a wide range of events, industries and client types, from government agencies to private-sector organisations.
Commercial Exposure:See how an agency wins and prices work, beyond just delivering it.
Performance-Linked Growth: Recognition, broader scope and increased responsibility follow demonstrated ownership and reliable performance over time, not tenure, effort or requests for advancement. Some team members progress quickly; others do not, based entirely on what they deliver.
Collaborative Team Environment: Work alongside experienced managers in a team where initiative, personal accountability, reliable follow-through and shared results are expected.
HOW TO APPLY
Interested applicants are invited to send a copy of their resume, together with a brief cover note, to jobs@purpleforest.com.sg.
Share your previous experience about an incident when you fixed something nobody asked you to fix before it turned out to be a larger issue.
Please include your full name, contact number, email address, nationality, education qualifications, employment history, reasons for leaving your last job, earliest available start date, and expected salary.

Reports To: The Council & Secretariat
Location: Singapore

Job Overview
Landscape Industry Association (Singapore) is seeking an organised, proactive Executive Coordinator to manage and drive the association's educational programs and events operations. In this role, you will manage day-to-day operations in our Association—working closely with the Executive Council and Committees to develop and deliver impactful workshops, educational courses, and industry programs.
The ideal candidate excels at balancing cross-functional communication, managing timelines with committee members, and delivering reliable, efficient administrative and logistical execution.
Key Responsibilities
1.End-to-End Training & events management/coordination
Facilitate the complete project lifecycle for training programs/events—from initial course scoping and curriculum scheduling to execution and final closeout.
· Ensure all course dependencies (e.g. accreditation/CEU submissions, trainer onboarding, venue bookings) are completed on time.
Conduct post-training evaluations, compile feedback analysis, and present findings to the Committee to continuously refine course quality.
Coordinate events organised by LIAS in conjunction with council and existing secretariat team
2.Committee Liaison & Stakeholder Engagement
Act as the primary liaison for Committee members, gathering, managing, and prioritising all incoming requests.
Foster team collaboration and idea-sharing among Committee members
Coordinate communications and facilitate information flow between the association, government agencies, and industry partners to ensure timely responses to joint initiatives and industry inquiries.
Build and maintain positive working relationships with trainers, industry regulators, government agencies and venue partners.
· Organise, facilitate, and document Committee meetings, preparing agendas, tracking action items, and circulating meeting minutes.
3.Timeline Tracking, Risk Management & Issue Resolution
Develop and maintain the full-year training calendar for operational tracking and resource planning
Proactively identify potential project risks (e.g., low registration numbers, trainer availability shifts) and implement contingency plans.
Resolve operational issues and participant inquiries professionally and promptly.
4.Project Documentation & SOP Management
Maintain a centralised, secure archive of course materials, participant databases, attendance records, and certification records.
Maintain and update Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) including association documentations.

Education: Diploma or Degree in Business Administration, Education/Training Management, Project Management, or a related field.
Experience: 2–4 years of experience in project coordination, event management, or administrative operations—preferably within an industry association, non-profit, or professional membership body.

Strong project planning skills

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.

Results driven, and thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth work environment.

Capacity to conceptualize as well as operationalize commercial strategies.

Superior organizational awareness.

Title: Executive Vice President, Operating Model & Product
Description:
Executive Vice President, Operating Model & Product
Global | Permanent
About Citco
Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services with staff across 50 office locations worldwide. With more than $1.8 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional service to meet our clients’ needs.
For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com
About the Team & Business Line
Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.
Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.
The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:
Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.
Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.
Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.
The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.
Your Role
You will own how our service should run and what we commit to clients, with accountability for the design and adoption of the Private Assets operating model.
Set the direction for the Private Assets operating model — defining how services should run end to end, and building the case for change with senior stakeholders.
Lead the Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions focus area, balancing long-term transformation priorities with near-term business and client demand.
Act as the senior Operations voice in client pitches, POCs and strategic direction setting, ensuring what we sell is something we can genuinely run.
Own the marquee solution reuse agenda — identifying where a solution built for one client can be applied across the wider book, and driving that rollout.
Partner at senior level with Operations, Tactical Operations, Marquee Client teams, the Transformation Office and IT to align change activity and remove duplication.
Govern the transformation portfolio, including prioritisation, resourcing, budget, risk, dependencies and executive reporting.
Establish plans for new client setup, transitions and complex implementations, coordinating across Operations, Financial Statements, Tax and Investor Relations.
Build and develop the team, including the rotational model, and actively participate in recruitment.
Maintain alignment with Tactical Operations and Marquee Operations, routing work to the right group and handing back anything better delivered tactically.
Represent Strategic Operations at Private Assets and CFS leadership forums.
About You
You have 12–15 years’ experience in fund administration, alternative asset management or a related financial services environment, predominantly in private assets.
A demonstrable record of delivering large-scale operating model or product re-engineering initiatives, with change that was genuinely adopted by the business.
Deep knowledge of private assets operating models, fund structures and the end-to-end service model.
Strong executive stakeholder management, with credibility in front of clients and senior leadership.
Commercial judgement — able to assess what we can genuinely deliver and price, and to hold that line in a client conversation.
Portfolio and programme governance experience, with proven ability to manage competing priorities across multiple focus areas.
Strong leadership skills and supervisory experience of other professionals, including rotational colleagues joining from the business.
Skilled in business planning, budgeting and stakeholder negotiation.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and SharePoint).
Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics or a related field; professional accounting designation a plus.
What We Expect of the Strategic Operations Team
Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:
Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.
Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.
A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.
Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.
Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.
Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.
Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.

Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.

Description:

Leong Jia Wei

jiawei@placement.com.sg

About the Division
The Retail Distribution Division is responsible for the growth of multiple channels including Bancassurance, Intermediaries, Direct channels, and Partnerships. It is also responsible for delivering service excellence for all UOI customers and increasing market awareness of UOI to achieve consumer trust and recognition.
Job Purpose
The Bancassurance Executive is responsible for ensuring smooth operational processes for bancassurance partnerships. This role focuses on coordinating with bank partners, managing documentation, and supporting compliance and service delivery. Key responsibilities include sales and commission reporting and tracking, conducting regular cadences with bank stakeholders, executing and tracking initiatives, and identifying new opportunities. The Executive will work closely with internal teams and bank stakeholders to resolve operational issues, track performance, and maintain strong partner relationships.
Key Responsibilities
1. Partner Coordination
Serve as the main point of contact for operational affairs with banking partners and hold regular updates to assess performance and projects. Arrange meetings, draft agendas, log outcomes, and monitor agreed tasks. Guarantee a minimum of 95% of planned catch-ups take place on schedule and action points are resolved within the specified periods.
2. Sales & Commission Reporting
Compile, manage, and verify precise summaries regarding sales results, commission payments, and operational data. Carry out reconciliation and variance analysis. Achieve 100%accuracy in reports and ensure submission within 3 working days of month-end.
3. Initiative Execution
Assist in the rollout and monitoring of projects designed to boost bancassurance results and client satisfaction. Track schedules, report on milestones, and flag delays or potential risks ahead of time. Ensure 90% of initiatives are delivered within agreed timelines and KPIs.
4. Opportunity Identification
Partner with stakeholders to discover fresh business avenues and operational upgrades. Review market trends and offer suggestions for development. Present at least one actionable opportunity per quarter
5. Compliance & Audit
Ensure adherence to regulatory and internal audit requirements. Prepare audit documentation, assist in compliance reviews, and implement corrective actions where necessary. Achieve zero non-compliance findings in audits and complete corrective actions within agreed timeline.
6. Cross-functional Collaboration
Work with underwriting, claims, and operations teams to ensure smooth policy issuance and servicing. Coordinate with multiple teams for issue resolution and process improvements. Resolve 95% of escalated issues within SLA timelines.
Requirements
Diploma or Degree in Business, Finance, or related field.
1–2 years in bancassurance, insurance operations, or financial services support (preferably with exposure to partner coordination).
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP) and reporting tools. Familiar with CRM systems and bancassurance processes.
Ability to interpret sales and commission data, identify variances, and provide actionable insights.
Strong interpersonal skills to liaise with bank stakeholders and internal teams effectively.
Understanding of regulatory requirements and audit processes in insurance.
Detail-oriented, organized, able to manage multiple priorities, and proactive in problem-solving.

Title: Executive, Client Experience (Catapult)
Description:
About Us
CapitaLand Group (CapitaLand) is one of Asia’s largest diversified real estate groups. Headquartered in Singapore, CapitaLand’s portfolio focuses on real estate investment management and real estate development, and spans across 270 cities in 45 countries.
Job Description
Catapult by CapitaLand is Singapore's premier executive education and leadership development campus. More than a venue, Catapult brings together corporates, learning providers, industry partners and business leaders through executive programmes, leadership offsites, conferences, corporate events and networking experiences. Located within Rochester Commons, Catapult provides a purpose-built environment designed to support collaboration, innovation, learning and business transformation.
We are looking for a hands-on and service-oriented executive to support clients in delivering successful meetings, conferences, executive programmes and corporate events at Catapult.
The Role
The Executive, Client Experience (Catapult), plays an important role in ensuring a seamless experience for clients, participants and guests from pre-event planning through on-site support and post-event follow-up.
Reporting to the Director, Sales & Business Development, the successful candidate will work closely with clients, vendors and internal stakeholders to coordinate venue requirements, operational arrangements and service delivery, ensuring clients have the support they need to execute successful events at Catapult.
This is a highly operational and execution-focused role suited for someone who enjoys engaging clients, managing multiple projects concurrently, solving issues proactively and delivering exceptional service experiences. The successful candidate will contribute directly to client satisfaction, repeat business and Catapult's reputation as a premier destination for executive learning and corporate engagement.
Key Responsibilities
1. Client Experience & Event Support
Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned clients following booking confirmation.
Coordinate client requirements and event needs from planning through completion.
Conduct venue walkthroughs, planning meetings and pre-event briefings with clients.
Provide guidance on venue capabilities, facilities, processes and available service offerings.
Ensure client requirements are accurately documented and communicated to relevant stakeholders.
Build positive client relationships and deliver a high standard of customer service throughout the client journey.
Anticipate client needs and proactively address issues to ensure a seamless experience.
As events may be scheduled outside normal business hours, the role requires flexibility to support evening, weekend and public holiday event operations when required.
2. Venue & Operational Coordination
Coordinate venue preparations and operational arrangements to support client events.
Liaise with internal teams and service partners on room setup, catering, AV requirements, access arrangements, signage and logistics.
Prepare event orders, operational briefs, schedules and run sheets.
Ensure event spaces and facilities are ready and aligned with client requirements.
Monitor event-day operations and coordinate prompt resolution of operational issues.
Provide onsite support to clients and serve as the key liaison throughout their event.
Ensure service delivery standards are consistently maintained across all events and programmes.
3. Participant & Guest Experience
Coordinate guest arrivals, reception services and VIP support arrangements.
Ensure participants and guests experience a welcoming and professional environment.
Attend to enquiries, requests and feedback promptly and professionally.
Support the collection of client and participant feedback following programmes and events.
Identify opportunities to enhance the overall client and guest experience.
4. Stakeholder & Vendor Coordination
Work closely with Sales & Business Development and Marketing & Partnerships teams to ensure smooth delivery of client engagements.
Coordinate with external vendors, service providers and contractors to fulfil event requirements.
Monitor vendor performance and escalate service issues where necessary.
Support procurement, purchase requisitions and administrative processes where required.
Maintain strong working relationships with key stakeholders and service partners.
5. Administration & Reporting
Maintain event schedules, client records and operational trackers.
Prepare event documentation, reports and post-event summaries where required.
Track client feedback, service recovery actions and improvement opportunities.
Support invoicing, billing coordination and administrative follow-up activities.
Ensure records and databases are updated accurately and in a timely manner.
Support continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency and client satisfaction.
Requirements
Diploma or Bachelor's degree in Hospitality, Events Management, Business, Communications or a related discipline.
1-3 years of experience in client service, hospitality, events, customer success or related roles.
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications
Experience with CRM, event management or venue booking systems would be advantageous.
Strong organisational and coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple activities concurrently.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
Strong attention to detail and ability to work in a fast-paced environment.

Title: Executive, Fundraising & Partnerships
Description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION
Founded in 1978 as Singapore's first family service centre, Allkin Singapore is a community-centric social service agency that believes everyone has the potential to create positive change, regardless of age, race, or background.
Through our service offerings, strategic partnerships, and community initiatives, we unlock opportunities for vulnerable individuals and families to overcome life's challenges, build a brighter future, and inspire others to do the same.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Allkin Singapore is a social service organisation that believes in the power of community to drive change. We work alongside partners and residents to strengthen families, build social connections, and foster a culture of care and contribution.
As Executive, Fundraising & Partnerships, you will play a key role in supporting fundraising initiatives and strategic partnerships that help sustain and grow our impact. Working closely with the Senior Executive, you will contribute to donor engagement, partnership development, fundraising campaigns, impact reporting, and stakeholder stewardship. This role is ideal for a resourceful and organised individual who is passionate about building meaningful partnerships and advancing positive social outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
Fundraising & Donor Development
Research and identify prospective donors, corporate partners, foundations, grantmakers, and funding opportunities.
Support donor outreach, cultivation, and engagement activities.
Develop grant applications, partnership proposals, sponsorship decks, donor presentations, and fundraising collateral.
Work with programme teams to gather programme information, funding needs, budgets, impact data, and beneficiary stories.
Maintain and track the fundraising pipeline, including donor engagement status and follow-up actions.
Donor & Partner Engagement
Support the stewardship and engagement of donors, corporate partners, foundations, and key stakeholders.
Coordinate donor meetings, site visits, appreciation activities, and partnership engagements.
Manage donor communications, acknowledgements, and recognition requirements.
Ensure timely fulfilment of partnership and sponsorship commitments.
Build and maintain positive, long-term relationships with donors and partners.
Impact Reporting & Accountability
Compile programme outcomes, impact data, and beneficiary stories for donor reporting.
Prepare donor impact reports, partnership updates, and stewardship materials.
Track reporting timelines, funding utilisation, and donor requirements.
Support data collection and impact tracking to demonstrate the outcomes of donor and partner support.
Fundraising Campaigns & Events
Support the planning and execution of fundraising campaigns, events, and community fundraising initiatives.
Coordinate internal teams, partners, vendors, and service providers to ensure successful event delivery.
Work with the communications team to develop fundraising content and campaign materials.
Assist with post-campaign reporting, evaluation, and donor follow-up activities.
Operations & Administration
Maintain accurate donor, donation, and partnership records within relevant systems.
Support fundraising reporting, budget tracking, invoice processing, and reconciliation activities.
Monitor fundraising performance and prepare regular management updates.
Ensure proper documentation and compliance with governance, audit, and reporting requirements.
Manage fundraising and partnership enquiries through shared mailboxes and communication channels.
QUALIFICATIONS
Diploma or Degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Social Sciences, or a related field.
At least 3 years of relevant experience in fundraising, partnerships, marketing, stakeholder engagement, or a related function.
Prior experience in the social service or non-profit sector is preferred but not essential.
Skills and Competencies:
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build and maintain relationships with diverse stakeholders.
Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
Experience in donor management, event coordination, CRM systems (e.g. Salesforce), and digital marketing will be an advantage.
Personal Attributes
Passionate about community impact and committed to advancing Allkin Singapore's mission through meaningful partnerships and fundraising initiatives.
Proactive, resourceful, detail-oriented, and able to work independently.
Professional integrity with a collaborative, customer-centric approach and commitment to excellence.

Title: Executive, Product, Pricing and Planning
Description:
[What the role is]
To support the development of commercially viable products, value-led experiences and pricing frameworks that strengthen Sentosa’s visitor proposition and drive incremental revenue for SDC and its Island Partners.
The role is responsible for building a continuous pipeline of new products, bundles and photo-worthy micro-experiences across Sentosa, working closely with Island Partners and internal stakeholders to curate fresh, authentic and commercially accretive offerings. This includes identifying new product opportunities, supporting experience design, developing pricing recommendations, and ensuring pricing governance, price parity and revenue controls are properly maintained across sales channels.
[What you will be working on]
Product Development & Experience Curation
- Identify and develop new products, bundles and curated experiences that enhance Sentosa's destination appeal and commercial performance.
- Collaborate with Island Partners to co-create innovative, value-driven visitor experiences and ancillary revenue opportunities.
- Analyse market trends, visitor insights and competitor offerings to identify product innovation opportunities.
- Translate business needs into feasible product concepts and coordinate cross-functional teams to support product development, launch and optimisation.
Pricing Strategy & Revenue Governance
- Support the development and implementation of pricing strategies for products, partner offerings, bundles and campaigns.
- Conduct pricing analysis, benchmarking and financial modelling to optimise revenue and competitiveness.
- Ensure pricing governance, approval processes and price parity across all sales channels.
- Review promotional pricing and discounts to ensure alignment with commercial objectives and pricing policies.
Commercialisation & Partner Management
- Partner with the Business Partnerships team and Island Partners to develop and commercialise new products and experiences.
- Support commercial discussions on pricing, packaging, revenue-sharing and operational requirements.
- Coordinate partner onboarding and product launches across Sentosa's sales and distribution channels.
- Serve as the key liaison between partners and internal stakeholders to ensure smooth execution of initiatives.
Performance Monitoring & Optimisation
- Monitor product, campaign and partner performance against revenue, sales and visitor engagement targets.
- Prepare performance reports, pricing analyses and business recommendations for management.
- Identify opportunities to optimise product offerings, pricing strategies and commercial outcomes.
Administration & Operational Support
- Manage operational and financial administration, including purchase orders, invoices, payments and accruals.
- Maintain pricing, product and governance documentation in compliance with internal policies.
- Coordinate with Finance, Procurement, Legal and other stakeholders on vendor onboarding, contracting and payment processes.
- Support continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency and governance.
[What we are looking for]
- Degree in Business, Marketing, Hospitality, Tourism, Economics, Finance or a related discipline.
- Minimum 2 to 3 years of relevant experience in product development, pricing, revenue management, commercial planning, business development, partnerships or sales.
- Strong commercial acumen, with the ability to assess product viability, pricing impact and revenue opportunities.
- Good analytical and numerical skills, with experience in pricing analysis, benchmarking, reporting or performance tracking.
- Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively with internal teams and external partners.
- Good project coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams from concept development to implementation.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare proposals, presentations and management updates.
- Meticulous and structured, with attention to detail in pricing, product information, commercial terms and governance processes.
- Resourceful, proactive and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with evolving business needs.
- Proficient in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
- Experience in tourism, attractions, hospitality, travel, e-commerce, retail, lifestyle, events or related industries will be an advantage.
- Experience in pricing, revenue management, product packaging or partnership-led product development will be an added advantage.

Title: Executive/Assistant Manager, Partnerships
Description:
Responsibilities
We are looking for a commercially minded Senior Executive / Assistant Manager to lead partnerships and partnership marketing across our hotel and serviced residence portfolio. This role is responsible for identifying and growing partnerships that drive room night production, and for bringing them to life through campaigns, collateral and communications.
You will work closely with the Director, Loyalty and CRM, and with cluster, property, marketing and revenue teams, with clear accountability for monitoring, tracking and reporting partnership results.
Partnership Development & Management
Identify, develop and manage partnerships with banks, travel, lifestyle, F&B, retail and other relevant brands, prioritising groupwide partnerships with strong potential to drive room night production in addition to brand visibility.
Develop compelling partnership propositions, benefits and experiences that add value to our guests, moving beyond discount-led offers.
Manage partnerships end-to-end, from opportunity identification and proposal development through to negotiation, activation and performance review.
Develop joint campaigns and activations with partners, ensuring all agreed deliverables are executed effectively.
Work with cluster and property teams so that property-level partnerships complement groupwide partnerships and build brand awareness for each cluster.
Build strong relationships with external partners and with internal commercial, marketing, cluster and property stakeholders.
Customer Engagement & Partnership Marketing
Develop and execute customer-facing campaigns and marketing initiatives to build awareness, participation and engagement with partnership offers.
Develop campaign concepts, messaging and copy across seasonal, promotional and partner initiatives.
Own campaign briefs and work with designers, agencies and internal teams to develop creative assets, collateral and communications.
Ensure consistent brand expression and guest experience across digital, social, website, hotel and other relevant touchpoints.
Manage the partnership marketing calendar and coordinate campaigns from concept through to launch.
Monitoring, Tracking & Reporting
Manage the administration of partnership programmes with both internal and external stakeholders e.g submission of reports to partners for billing
Maintain the Partnership Master List covering all contracted partners, including active partnerships, contract periods, offers, deliverables and production.
Track room nights and revenue achieved by each partnership against agreed targets, and report on a regular cadence.
Monitor campaign and partnership performance, flag underperformance early, and recommend whether to renew, renegotiate or exit.
Prepare performance updates and recommendations for the Director, Loyalty and CRM and senior management.
Maintain partnership agreements and supporting documents.
Requirements
3–5 years' experience in partnerships, marketing, brand, loyalty, hospitality, lifestyle or retail.
Good understanding of branding, including aligning partner brands with Far East Hospitality in customer-facing communications.
Strong partnership and relationship management skills, with the ability to negotiate commercial terms.
Strong hands-on experience in campaign development and execution, including creative concepts, copy and marketing collateral.
Comfortable working with multiple stakeholders, including external partners, cluster and property teams.
Commercially minded and results-driven, with a focus on commercial elements
Organised and detail-oriented, able to track, analyse and report performance, and to manage multiple initiatives from idea to execution.
Experience in hospitality, travel, lifestyle or loyalty programmes is an advantage.

About the team The Extreme Risk Operations (ERO) team assesses and acts on livestream extreme risk content, combining fast intervention with continuous detection improvement to reduce serious harm at scale. We are the first point of interruption and transfer for credible, specific and imminent live stream escalations to the Emergency Response Team and Child Safety Teams for assessment, acting as the first line of defense when dealing with extreme risk on TikTok. Responsibilities 1. ERO responsibilities - You will bring operational excellence to a team that handles a large volume of Livestream Escalations and evaluates risk, threats, and user safety in time-critical escalations. - You will provide support to escalations related to sensitive materials and subject matter. - Execute instant decision-making while analyzing a variety of factors that include imminent, dangerous, sensitivities, and graphic content and coordinate with a number of internal partners to ensure user's safety. - You will clearly respond to process and policy questions from internal parties. - You will be working with a cross-functional team, driving improvements to policies and processes within the ERO team. - You are willing and able to maturely work with sensitive issues that include child exploitation, a variety of religious and political views, violence, and adult content. - You will participate in frequent refreshers and new training in order to adhere to relevant SOPs and policies 2. Live Risk Assessment and Escalation: - You will review videos, posts, comments, user profiles, and live-streaming content according to the policies, workflows, and targets, which may include graphic, violent, explicit, political, profane, and otherwise disturbing content - You will investigate and resolve complex issues regarding content in accordance with SLAs and metrics - You will add accurate metadata/tags to content items, identify and escalate potential risks to relevant teams - This position is part of a team that provides 24/7 support and requires working scheduled shifts, which may include holidays
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications - You must have fluency in English as you will be working with cases that require language skills (verbal and written) - You have at least 1 year of experience or relevant educational background - Excellent verbal and written communication skills and ability to adapt communication styles to suit different stakeholders, like cross-functional teams - Experience in reviewing or being exposed to sensitive content and a deep understanding of removal workflow calibrations and escalations management. Preferred Qualifications: - You have experience communicating with cross-functional teams - You have experience working independently with judgment - You are proactive towards complying with procedures, policies, and objectives set in place and taking a disciplined approach when undertaking tasks. - Proven ability to make important decisions independently and multi-task, responding quickly to changing situations in complex environments without compromising quality - You have the ability to perform duties objectively, devoid of inherent biases or personal beliefs. - Demonstrate good analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills - Willing to work over weekends and holidays on a rotation basis. Willing to start between the hours of 1000 and 1200 daily on a rotational basis - EMEA. (for APAC this will read 0600 and 1000). AMS will be start time between 0900 and 1100. Description:
Company Overview
Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.
Company Operating Rhythm
At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.
Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.
Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.
Team Overview
Deepgram recently opened its APAC headquarters in Singapore, and the region is one of our fastest-moving markets. You’ll build the APAC marketing function from zero, partnering closely with the APAC GM and regional sales leadership to shape and execute the regional plan. As part of the global Events & Field Marketing team, you’ll get the playbooks, brand assets, budget framework and coaching to help you move fast.
Your job is to make Deepgram visible and credible across the region through technical community and partner motions, and to turn that presence into pipeline. As the senior marketer in region, you're also marketing's local point of contact: you'll work with our APAC PR agency and partner with global Brand, Web, and Product Marketing to keep regional messaging local and consistent.
Key Goals
- Ship an APAC field and events plan and budget, agreed with regional sales leadership, with reserve held for in-quarter opportunities
- Launch a recurring technical community program out of Singapore, India, and Australia, with steady attendance from developers, builders and customers
- Stand up repeatable joint field programs with cloud, technology, and channel partners, each with shared pipeline goals and tracking
- Grow program-sourced and program-influenced pipeline and new logos across APAC
- Localize global "event-in-a-box" kits for priority markets and follow up with every lead fast
- Put a live APAC customer proof library (stories, case studies, references) into active use by sales aligned to global Marketing Team.
- Work with global Brand Team to properly represent APAC on the website: a regional landing page, local customer logos, case studies, proof points, product news and team presence.
- Deliver executive roundtables, customer dinners, and sponsorships, on time and on budget, reporting spend, attendance, and pipeline against plan
Minimum Skills, Knowledge & Capabilities
- Plans and runs field and event programs end to end, from small executive dinners to large sponsorships, on time and on budget
- Builds community technical audiences choose to attend: hands-on content, credible speakers, and real builders in the room
- Designs partner marketing motions (joint programs, co-marketing, co-sell) with shared goals and measurable pipeline
- Partners with sales to tie every program in the quarterly plan to pipeline
- Adapts global playbooks to local markets across language, culture, format, and buyer expectations, and knows the APAC vendor landscape
- Operates AI-native: designs Human+AI workflows for planning, logistics, follow-up, and reporting, and builds systems that eliminate recurring event work instead of redoing it each time
- Works self-directed as the first in region, across time zones with a US-based team; travels across the region regularly (roughly 30-40%)
Preferred Qualifications (nice-to-have, not required)
- Typically ~3–6 years in field or event marketing covering APAC, or equivalent demonstrated experience
- Background in B2B SaaS, developer-focused, or AI/infrastructure marketing
- Co-marketing experience with technical partners
- Experience working with PR agencies or supporting regional communications
- Professional proficiency in an additional regional language (e.g., Bahasa, Mandarin)
Our Values
- Be You: bring your whole self and a different perspective; diverse viewpoints make our products better.
- Be Curious: challenge the status quo, keep learning, and ask 'how might we?' instead of accepting limits.
- Grow Together: push each other to do great work, treat feedback as a gift, and leave the drama out.
- Do the Right Thing: act with integrity and candor, assume best intent, choose ethics over expediency.
- Think Smart. Act Fast.: weigh the high-leverage options, decide, and move; no analysis paralysis.
- Put the Customer First: listen with empathy, understand their goals, and let their success drive ours.
We know the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting great candidates — so please don't hesitate to apply. We'd love to hear from you.

Title: Finance Manager, Sales Compensation (Strategic Center of Excellence)
Description:
About the Role:
Grade Level (for internal use):
11
The Role:
The Finance Manager, Sales Compensation (Strategic Center of Excellence) will serve as a strategic and governance advisor, bringing executive presence, strong policy expertise, and a deep understanding of sales compensation strategy. This role will guide the organization through complex business changes while designing legally sound, scalable sales compensation policies.
In addition to core compensation governance, the Finance Manager will oversee all SPIFF and supplemental incentive programs, including KPI collection, validation, and calculation processes to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with business objectives. By applying expertise in sales behavior, incentive design, and SFDC infrastructure, this role will develop effective dispute resolution processes, create engaging training resources, and translate complex compensation methodologies into clear, actionable, and commercially relevant guidance for sales leaders.
Responsibilities and Impact:
This role is the cornerstone of governance, audit compliance, and strategic enablement for our sales compensation operations. By serving as the authoritative voice on policy architecture, managing complex integrations, and ensuring exactness in KPI and SPIFF calculations, the Finance Manager ensures our incentive strategies are seamlessly translated into operational reality, driving both compliance and highly motivated sales behaviors across the organization.
Establish clear, legally robust, and unambiguous global sales compensation policies. Define global approval matrices and uphold governance standards in partnership with senior Sales, People Partner, and Finance stakeholders.
Lead the assessment, mapping, and integration of incentive plans and personnel structures during corporate transactions and restructurings. Ensure compensation continuity, policy alignment, and operational readiness during periods of organizational change.
Manage the end-to-end collection, validation, and calculation of all sales compensation KPIs, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and alignment with plan requirements.
Oversee and execute calculations for all SPIFFs and custom supplemental incentives, ensuring accuracy, data integrity, and alignment with commercial milestones.
Analyze and present performance trends, risks, exceptions, and opportunities for process or incentive optimization to senior leadership.
Manage escalated compensation disputes and define comprehensive dispute-resolution SLAs and policies. Ensure issues are resolved accurately, consistently, and with a customer-centric approach to supporting sales representatives and leaders.
Evaluate custom supplemental incentives and provide advisory support to commercial and finance stakeholders. Ensure incentive structures are clear, measurable, operationally executable, and aligned with intended sales behaviors.
Draft step-by-step Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and governance workflows. Project manage multi-phased initiatives, including the integration of custom incentives, to ensure deliverables remain on track, well-documented, and operationally sustainable.
Build interactive training libraries for sales representatives and ensure seamless rollout, adoption, and tracking of required compliance and compensation training.
What We're Looking For:
Basic Required Qualifications:
7+ years of relevant experience in sales compensation, finance governance, audit, sales operations, or corporate incentive strategy.
Governance & Audit Expertise: Strong background in governance, policy design, internal controls, audit trails, and risk mitigation across complex corporate compensation structures.
Policy Architecture & Structural Design: Expert-level capability in writing clear, legally robust, and unambiguous sales compensation policies and terms and conditions.
KPI, SPIFF & Incentive Calculations: Hands-on proficiency in collecting, validating, and calculating sales compensation KPIs, SPIFFs, and complex supplemental incentives with high precision.
Organizational Integration: Proven track record evaluating, mapping, and integrating incentive plans and personnel structures during corporate transactions, spinoffs, and restructurings.
Executive Presence & Negotiation: Ability to uphold governance standards, defend approval matrices, and negotiate policy changes with senior Sales, People Partners, and Finance executives.
Translational Communication: Strong ability to translate complex mathematical compensation rules into simple, commercial, and motivating terms for sales representatives and leaders.
Salesforce/SFDC Proficiency: Strategic and operational understanding of Salesforce workflows, case queues, routing rules, and dashboard reporting.
Technical Writing & Digital Enablement: Expert skill in drafting detailed SOPs, governance workflows, and training materials, and build interactive training libraries and support scalable rollout.
Customer-Centric Problem Solving & Precision: Detail-oriented approach to audit compliance, matrix tracking, dispute resolution, and query management, with a supportive and customer-centric mindset.

Title: Financial Partnerships Lead - Market Expansion Lead, Singapore/Hong Kong/Malaysia
Description:
About the Xendit
Xendit is an enterprise payments platform powering complex financial operations across Southeast Asia and global markets. We provide a unified API layer combining payment processing, global payouts, localized FX, identity compliance, and fraud protection. As a trusted financial partner backed by top-tier global investors, Xendit processes high-throughput transaction flows for leading global platforms including Meta, Traveloka, ByteDance, Wise, and Grab, building resilient payment infrastructure to drive regional commerce forward
About the Job
Xendit is going from a Southeast Asian payments provider to a global one. Nothing in that sentence happens without rails. Every market we want to sell in has to exist before it can be sold in — an entity, a licence or a licensed partner, bank accounts, and live rails — and every market we already sell in only earns what its partner economics allow
This role owns both halves, at roughly equal weight
Market expansion. You will help decide which markets we enter, build the case that gets them funded, choose whether we build, buy, or partner for the licence, and then run the entry end to end until the market is licensed, funded, connected, and handed over to a country commercial lead. You will do it as a repeatable playbook rather than a one-off project, so the second market is faster than the first and the fifth is faster than the second
Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong. You will own Xendit’s financial partner portfolio in those three markets — the banks, wallets, card schemes, FX providers and domestic rails we run on. You own the relationships, the commercials, the performance, and the cost of every rail in your markets
Responsibilities
Market expansion
- Market intelligence. Screen and rank candidate markets on market size, regulatory openness, payment rails, competitive density, and merchant demand. Maintain a live pipeline and a decision-ready entry book per market
- Business case and investment decision. Build the cost-to-launch and cost-to-operate model, the revenue and margin projection, and the breakeven view. Take the go/no-go paper to leadership and defend it
- Licensing strategy. Recommend build, buy, or partner per market. Select the licence type, shape the regulator engagement approach, and hold a coherent licensing roadmap across markets rather than a footprint we did not design
- Foundational set-up. Drive entity incorporation, the licence application end to end, bank account opening, and scheme and rail access — executing with Corporate Secretarial, Legal, Compliance, and Treasury
- Programme management. One timeline, one budget, one risk register per market. Convene the functions, hold them to dates, and escalate early and specifically when a gate is at risk
- The playbook. Turn each entry into reusable artefacts — stage gates, application pack templates, a common business case model, a bank account approach, a handover checklist — and own the country-specific deviations
- Handover. Support the hire of the country commercial lead, operationalise the licence with Compliance, and hand over against a defined readiness bar. Until every item on that bar is true, the market is still yours
Financial partnerships in Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong
- Partner portfolio strategy. Decide which partners we run which rails and corridors on, where we need redundancy, and what the partner roadmap is for each of the three markets
- Commercials. Negotiate pricing, rebates, revenue share, and FX spreads. Use volume across markets as leverage rather than negotiating each market from scratch. Own the contract lifecycle with Legal
- Cost of rails. Own COGS in your markets. Find the margin, model it, and work with Product and Treasury to move routing and volume to where the economics are better
- Partner performance. Set and enforce SLAs, run QBRs, chase root causes when a rail underperforms, and manage escalations with the partner rather than around them
- Regulatory posture with partners. Keep partner flows appropriate to our licences in each market, make sure agreements carry the right AML and KYC responsibilities, and give Compliance and the country teams a clear view of each partner’s regulatory role
- Being the accountable owner. Every partnership has one accountable owner. For these markets, it is you. Other teams can talk to partners directly for execution and compliance; nothing material happens without you
- Unblocking commercial deals. Support sales cycles that turn on a partner capability we do not yet have, and bring the market and merchant insight back into the global partner strategy
The Questions You Will Answer
- Which markets should Xendit enter next, in what order, and which ones should we decline?
- What will it actually cost and how long will it actually take to be able to process a first transaction there?
- Do we build our own licence, acquire one, or launch on a partner’s — and what does that trade in cost, speed, control, and margin?
- What has to be true before we commit commercially or hire in a market?
- Where is the margin in Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong, and what has to change to get it?
- Which rails in these markets are a single point of failure, and what is the backup?
- What did the last entry teach us that makes the next one cheaper and faster?
- Is this market genuinely ready to run itself, or are we handing over a problem?
Minimum Qualifications
- 3+ years of experience running a complex cross-functional programme to a committed date — not only designing the plan, but landing it. Backgrounds that travel well here include top-tier management consulting, corporate development or strategy at a high-growth technology or financial services company, and programme leadership at a payments, banking, or fintech business
- Experience running a complex cross-functional programme to a committed date — not only designing the plan, but landing it. Backgrounds that travel well here include top-tier management consulting, corporate development or strategy at a high-growth technology or financial services company, and partnership or programme leadership at a payments, banking, or fintech business
- A track record of negotiating and running commercial relationships with banks, card schemes, wallets, or payment providers. You have held a number and moved it
- Working knowledge of payment regulation, banking, and payment infrastructure. You do not need to be a lawyer. You do need to hold a credible conversation with a regulator, a global bank, and our own Compliance team on the same day
- Strong commercial and financial judgment: you can build the model, stress the assumptions, and say plainly when a market does not clear the bar
- Exceptional written communication. Much of the output of this role is a paper that a CEO, a board, or a regulator reads without you in the room
- A genuine global operator who translates across cultures and domains. Relationship building and regulator engagement in developed markets do not work the way they do in Southeast Asia, and this role has to work in both. Familiarity with the Malaysian, Singaporean, or Hong Kong payments landscape is a clear advantage
- A strong team player. On the expansion half this role has no line authority over the functions it depends on and has to earn its way through them
- Comfort with ambiguity and with owning an outcome that is largely dependent on other people’s work
- A bachelor’s degree in an analytically rigorous discipline
You Will Thrive Here If You
- Are more interested in the market going live than in the plan being elegant
- Sequence properly: you establish whether we can be licensed, at what cost and by when, before anyone commits
- Bring functions in at the start as inputs rather than at the end as approvers, and hold them to dates without turning it into a fight
- Are willing to recommend a no-go on a market leadership is excited about, with the analysis to support it
- Build things that outlast you: templates, models, and playbooks the next person inherits.
- Are energised by a fast pace, high accountability, and direct feedback
Working Model
- Based in Singapore or Hong Kong
- We expect team members in the office four days per week to support close collaboration and fast decisions
- Travel of approximately 20–30%, to target markets, regulators, banks, and partners, weighted to the entries in flight
Why This Role?
- Most people who work on market entry do one market, once, inside a function. Here you own the whole sequence — the screen, the case, the licence, the accounts, the rails, the handover — and then you own it again in the next market, with the advantage of having built the playbook. It is one of the few roles where the scope of what you own is genuinely limited only by how fast you can make the machine work
- If you want a defined lane inside an established process, this is not the role. If you want to build the capability that decides where a payments company can operate, we would like to hear from you

Title: Fitness Sales Executive Singapore - NOCCO | Barebells | Vitamin Well
Description:
Vitamin Well Group develops premium functional drinks, snacks and protein products designed for modern, everyday life and on-the-go consumption. Our portfolio includes Barebells, NOCCO and Vitamin Well. With over 750 employees and revenue of more than SEK 10 billion, we are present in over 50 markets, with our headquarters in Stockholm and local teams and partners around the world. Our growth is driven by a focus on building strong brands, creating products with uncompromising taste and clear functionality, and consistently raising the bar across our categories.
Vitamin Well Group in Asia Pacific
In Asia Pacific, we grow through strong distributor partnerships and high-impact consumer activations. The region represents a strategic growth priority, driven by ambitious expansion plans and a clear expectation of in-market execution. From our APAC Hub in Singapore, we operate with our brands NOCCO, Vitamin Well and Barebells across fitness and retail channels – and see significant further potential for expansion.
To accelerate growth and strengthen our commercial presence, we are now looking for a dedicated Field Sales & Activation Executive.
About the role
This is a commercially driven, field-based role focused on accelerating distribution, sales and brand execution across Singapore.
You will be responsible for growing our presence across gyms, fitness partners, retail and other relevant local accounts. The majority of your time will be spent in the market – visiting customers, identifying and winning new accounts, strengthening existing relationships and ensuring consistent brand execution at point of sale.
Sales is at the core of the role, but your responsibility goes beyond winning the account. You will also plan and execute local activations, sampling, events and demos, and ensure our brands are visible, available and strongly represented at customer sites. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys combining commercial ownership with getting things done in the market.
The position is employed by our local distribution partner in Singapore and fully dedicated to Vitamin Well Group. You will work closely with the local distributor team in day-to-day operations, while reporting to the Sales Manager APAC, Distributor Markets. The role is based in Singapore and is primarily field-based across the market.
In short your responsibilities will be:
Deliver on monthly volume, distribution and other commercial targets through well-planned routes and purposeful customer visits.
Manage and grow existing accounts through regular follow-ups, strong relationships, smart prioritisation and upselling and cross-selling opportunities.
Proactively prospect, approach and win new accounts to expand the presence of NOCCO, Barebells and Vitamin Well across Singapore.
Secure regular orders and strong execution at customer sites, including product availability, visibility, pricing and display standards.
Plan and execute sampling, activations, events and demos, including coordinating sampling teams and taking ownership of agreed larger activations from planning through execution and follow-up.
Own the field execution of our branded fridge placements, from identifying suitable sites and coordinating placements to following up on stock, product range, visibility and performance.
Work closely with the distributor and Vitamin Well Group teams, staying on top of customer needs, competitor activity and market trends and turning insights from the field into action.
What you can expect
A market-facing role where your work has a direct impact on our growth in Singapore.
The opportunity to work across both sales and activation, from identifying commercial opportunities to seeing them come to life in the market.
Close collaboration with regional teams, with visibility across the wider organisation.
An opportunity to combine an interest in fitness, community and active lifestyles with a driven, field-based commercial career.
Who are you
You are a commercially driven sales professional who enjoys being out in the market, meeting customers and turning opportunities into business. You are comfortable approaching new customers, building relationships and asking for the sale, while understanding that strong results come from consistent follow-up and execution.
You thrive in a hands-on environment and take ownership of your customers and priorities. You are proactive, structured and comfortable working independently, while also enjoying the practical side of building brands in the market – from customer execution to activations and events.
You have a genuine interest in sports, fitness and active lifestyles and understand the communities our brands are part of. You are also a team player who shares insights and contributes to the wider team's success.
Essential skills to succeed
Relevant experience in field sales, account management or new business development, including experience winning new accounts.
Demonstrated experience managing and growing customer accounts.
Comfortable working independently in a field-based role and taking ownership of day-to-day execution.
Fluent in English.
Strong local knowledge of Singapore.
Experience within the fitness industry or familiarity with the local fitness community is highly valued.
Legal right to work in Singapore, as visa sponsorship is not available for this role.
How to Apply
Application deadline: October 31st 2026
We review applications on an ongoing basis and may fill the position before the application deadline. We appreciate LinkedIn, but to get a full picture of your experience, we ask you to also include a CV.
Life at Vitamin Well Group
At Vitamin Well Group, we believe that a great workplace fuels great products. With over 750 employees worldwide, our people play an important role in how we build brands, develop products and grow the business. Our values – innovation, courage, drive and responsibility – shape how we work together and how we do business.
Across functions and markets, our teams are hands-on in building our brands, developing our products and making them available to consumers around the world. We embrace an office-first principle because we believe our best ideas emerge when people come together, share ideas, build relationships and take ownership.
Promoting active lifestyles is part of our culture. Employees can take part in run clubs, group workouts, races and sporting events that suit different interests and fitness levels. As we continue to grow, we aim to make a positive impact by reducing our environmental footprint, promoting active and healthy lifestyles, and acting responsibly across our value chain.
As part of the recruitment process, we may ask you to conduct a personality test as well as a test that measures logical ability. The purpose of the tests is to evaluate candidates as objective as possible and identify the best possible match for the role. The tests are based on solid research and are taken through our partner.

Manager

data centres

.
You will work closely with team members to support our data centre clients on public policy, regulation, politics, and commercial strategy. There may also be opportunities to work with Flint’s other tech sector clients.
Data centre operators face a challenging policy and regulatory environment across Asia-Pacific. AI and cloud-based demand is driving rapid growth and investment, but delivering a return on this capital is becoming more complicated. In parts of the region, concerns over data centres’ impact on communities, on infrastructure, and on the environment are leading to policy change that impacts on how operators build and operate data centres. We are helping investors and operators of data centres to build understanding of the benefits they bring and to make the case to governments for policy frameworks that enable the growth of the sector.
You will have scope to engage with clients at the most senior levels. The role will provide an unparalleled opportunity to research and analyse the complex policy and political challenges our clients face and develop options and approaches to address those challenges, backing up recommendations with wider strategic and political analysis.
Flint provides an excellent professional and educational environment for people to accelerate their personal and career development. There will be space to engage in discussion and debates on substantive policy and political challenges, as well as significant scope for progression through the company.
You will join a rapidly growing team, with the opportunity to take ownership of tasks and contribute to the company’s growth in the region.
