Description:
About the Team
GitLab's APJ Ecosystem team builds and scales the partner (channel, alliance, and hyperscaler) motion across the region. ASEAN is a strategic market for GitLab, and this hire is central to strengthening our partner ecosystem there — deepening a smaller number of high-value partnerships rather than spreading thin across many transactional ones.
About the Role
Based in Singapore, our Ecosystem Sales Manager (ESM)- ASEAN, is a senior, market-facing role responsible for building and scaling GitLab's partner business in ASEAN countries across the full breadth of the ecosystem: hyperscalers, large ASEAN-centric system integrators (SIs), and born-in-the-cloud / AI-native partners. We are looking for someone with the range and seniority to credibly own strategic partner relationships across all of these partner types, and to help grow our business through these partners.
This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who has already built a career scaling partner-sourced and influenced revenue in ASEAN, someone who knows the hyperscaler ecosystem (AWS & GCP), has deep, credible relationships with ASEAN's major SIs, and understands how to engage newer-generation cloud-native and AI partners as they become an increasingly important part of the go-to-market.

Develop deep, strategic (not transactional) relationships with a focused set of priority partners — joint business plans, QBRs, and named executive sponsorship.

Own hyperscaler relationship management and Marketplace motion with AWS and/OR GCP.

Build and grow relationships with major ASEAN SIs and market-making channel/born-in-the-cloud partners and emerging AI-native partners.

We work to drive impactful development that is: i) inclusive of everyone, including women and young people; ii) resilient to shocks, including against climate and biodiversity crises, pandemics and fragility; and iii) sustainable, through growth and job creation, human development, fiscal and debt management, food security and access to clean air, water and affordable energy.
The EAP Infrastructure Department is responsible for project lending and policy advisory work in the energy; transport; urban, land, and resilience, and related climate action and private capital mobilization space for the EAP Region. The department presently comprises an energy and extractives unit, a transport unit, and two urban units.
The energy unit [IEAE1] manages a diverse program of projects, analytic and advisory work. The principal themes underlying the lending and advisory engagements include access to modern energy services; transitioning to a clean energy mix away from coal; climate resilient energy infrastructure; regional energy connectivity, integration and trade; governance reforms and financial strengthening of state-owned enterprises/utilities; and reforming sector regulations to improve the environment for efficient private finance solutions
Duties and accountabilities:
The Senior Energy Specialist will bring a strong track record of leading high-level policy dialogue, advancing regional power integration, and mobilizing private capital for power-sector projects. The successful candidate will combine deep knowledge of policy, regulation, and institutional reform with hands-on experience in project finance, transaction structuring, risk allocation, and private-sector participation. The candidate will also have strong operational experience in project design, implementation, and supervision, including regional and cross-border initiatives. Key responsibilities include:
• Conceptualize and lead investment operations that leverage private capital for energy projects, including ASEAN Power Grid (APG) interconnections and related transmission infrastructure, and/or energy sector operations. Responsibilities include early-stage concept development, project structuring, financial and economic analysis, institutional arrangements, and risk assessment.
• Lead high-level policy dialogue with governments, ASEAN institutions, regulators, utilities, and private-sector stakeholders on cross-border electricity trade, power-market development, investment frameworks, and an enabling environment for private capital mobilization in Southeast Asia.
• Supervise an active portfolio of national and regional lending operations, including Investment Project Financing (IPF) and Program-for-Results (PforR), and apply a strong understanding of guarantees and other risk-mitigation instruments relevant to electricity projects.
• Engage bilateral and multilateral partners, regional organizations, and financing institutions to coordinate support and mobilize resources for APG priorities and other regional energy activities.
• Lead sector analysis and advisory activities on regional power trade, transmission planning, market design, regulatory and institutional frameworks, and the financial and technical performance of power-sector entities.
• Prepare regional, country, and sector briefings, background reports, case studies, and portfolio reviews, energy connectivity, and private financing, ensuring outputs are timely, technically sound, and aligned with program messaging.
• Identify knowledge gaps and develop innovative financing, guarantee, and risk-allocation approaches for energy projects, including cross-border interconnections and associated infrastructure.
• Organize knowledge exchanges and contribute to publications and communications that share operational lessons on cross-border power trade, and private capital mobilization.
• Participate actively in EAP Energy Practice-wide knowledge sharing and contribute to regional and global communities of practice on energy finance and power-system integration.
Selection Criteria
• Master's degree or higher required, in economics, finance, engineering, or a closely related discipline. A combination of financial training with economics and/or engineering is an advantage.
• Minimum of 10 years of relevant professional experience in the energy sector, with a strong track record in project preparation, implementation, and supervision. Experience in project finance, regional power integration or cross-border electricity trade, and multilateral development bank operations is highly desirable.
• Demonstrated experience with a range of IBRD, IFC, or MIGA financing instruments, including guarantees and other risk-mitigation approaches, is a significant advantage.
• Experience in Southeast Asia and familiarity with ASEAN energy cooperation, the ASEAN Power Grid, and the region's electricity-sector context is an advantage.
Technical Skills and Professional Competencies

• Deep knowledge of energy-sector topics, including power-sector engineering, financing, regional power markets, transmission planning, and related regulatory, commercial, and institutional frameworks.

• Strong communication and stakeholder-engagement skills, with proven writing and editing ability and the capacity to convey complex technical and financial issues clearly to diverse audiences.
• Self-driven and proactive, with the ability to work with a sense of urgency and manage competing demands under tight deadlines.
• Positive, solutions-oriented approach to problem-solving and client engagement.
• Intellectual curiosity and openness to innovation in development approaches.
• International mobility without restrictions and willingness to undertake frequent travel within Southeast Asia and the wider East Asia and Pacific region.
• Professional proficiency in English required.

Description:
Career in the Hospital
Join our incredible team at the National University Hospital (NUH), where we believe that a hospital is more than just a workplace. Every day, we witness the remarkable impact that our healthcare professionals can have on individuals, families, and entire communities.
At NUH, we are driven by a shared purpose – to lend a helping hand to those in need, to be a source of support and healing, and to empower patients to live their best lives.
We are looking for passionate and committed individuals to join us as we transform lives and create a lasting impact in the lives of our patients. The impact you make at NUH will be profound, regardless of the role you take up in the hospital.
About NUH
The National University Hospital (NUH) is Singapore’s leading university hospital, with a proud heritage dating back to 1905 with the establishment of what’s now the NUS Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine. Our strong ties with the medical school have shaped us into a unique institution, allowing us to seamlessly integrate clinical care with teaching and research. As a university hospital, we go beyond the realm of providing tertiary medical care. We are a hub of knowledge and innovation, attracting healthcare professionals who are passionate about pushing boundaries and making significant contributions to the field.
About Department and Purpose of the Position
The Senior Executive / Assistant Manager (EPIC Specialist) provides functional and application support for the NGEMR EPIC Beacon module, with a focus on oncology workflows. The role supports system configuration, maintenance, enhancement, and user engagement to ensure safe, effective, and compliant use of the EMR system.
Key Responsibilities
Coordinate with NCIS stakeholders and GMIO on system change requests, enhancements, and workplans
Support daily operations of the NGEMR EPIC Beacon module through system analysis, configuration, testing, maintenance, and troubleshooting
Gather, document, and validate user requirements in collaboration with clinical and operational users
Translate documented requirements to enterprise IT partners (e.g. Synapxe) clearly and accurately
Configure and maintain oncology treatment plans, protocols, and related clinical build content in accordance with approved workflows
Support system testing activities, including preparation of test scripts, test data, and coordination of user acceptance testing
Provide at-the-elbow or on-site support during system go-live and post-implementation stabilization periods
Participate in on-call or after-hours support rotas when required, in accordance with operational schedules
Adhere to institutional governance, information security, and change management policies
Support assigned projects and initiatives led by GMIO or NCIS, as directed by supervisors
Represent the team in workgroups or committees when assigned
Participate in cross-training and continuous learning to expand system and domain knowledge
Contribute positively as a team member and support collaborative working relationships
Key Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Pharmacy, Nursing, Health Informatics, Biomedical Science, Information Systems, Computer Science, or related healthcare / IT disciplines
2 to 3 years of relevant clinical, healthcare operations, informatics, or EMR-related experience
Strong understanding of clinical workflows, preferably oncology-related
Strong analytical, documentation, and problem-solving skills
Effective verbal and written communication skills
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications
EPIC certification (e.g. Beacon or other clinical modules) is preferred
Experience supporting EMR build, configuration, or system implementation projects would be an advantage
Exposure to healthcare IT governance, change management, and information security practices would be an advantage

About the Role!
As our Senior Executive / Associate Manager, Partnerships, you will work closely with the Head of Partnerships to develop and manage strategic alliances that fuel FOMO Pay's business growth, product innovation, and global market expansion. In this dynamic role, you will help shape the future of finance by nurturing vital existing relationships and proactively onboarding new partners who align with our visionary goals. - Demonstrated success in independently managing complex commercial discussions, partner onboarding, and cross-functional project delivery.
- Highly comfortable coordinating with Product and Technology teams on API or system integrations from a strategic business perspective.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and written/verbal communication skills, coupled with meticulous attention to detail.

Job Title: Senior Executive, Dean's Office (Office for Students), 2 years' contract

Employee Category: Executive & Administrative
Posting Start Date: 25/09/2026

Job Description
Established in 1905 to educate and train medical professionals for Singapore, the NUS Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine is recognised as one of Asia's leading medical educational and research institutions. We are committed to cultivating the next generation of healthcare professionals who will embody the highest clinical standards, addressing tomorrow's medical challenges with competence, compassion, and creativity.
Why Join Us
This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the future of Singapore's doctors; from selecting tomorrow's medical students through the admissions process, to supporting professionalism throughout their journey at NUS Medicine. You'll work closely with senior faculty, collaborate with the team to organise key projects and events, and contribute to initiatives that make a lasting impact on the student experience.
Key Responsibilities
Work with the team to plan and execute the annual NUS Medicine admissions exercise, including interviews, applicant engagement, admissions operations, and providing secretariat support to the Admissions Committee.
Coordinate admissions outreach and engagement activities, including Open House, talks, webinars and applicant events, to promote NUS Medicine and support prospective students throughout the admissions journey.
Contribute to process improvements, digital initiatives and data analysis to enhance the admissions experience and operational efficiency.
Collaborate with faculty, clinicians, student leaders and external stakeholders to deliver high-quality programmes and events.
Support the planning and execution of projects, events, vendor coordination, committee work and new initiatives.
Support the Professionalism & Student Conduct Committee (PSCC) by coordinating committee meetings, case management and follow-up, while maintaining the highest standards of confidentiality and professionalism.
Contribute to strategic initiatives that strengthen the student experience and shape the future of medical education.
Admissions interviews and major outreach events peak during the admissions cycle (January to May), which includes approximately 10–12 weekends of work annually and overtime during peak periods.
Time-off arrangements will be provided in accordance with NUS policies.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in any discipline.
Strong event management skills.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Detail-oriented with excellent organisational skills.
Ability to work collaboratively with faculty, students, internal and external stakeholders.
Prior experience in admissions, event planning or project management is preferred but not required. Fresh graduates are welcome to apply.

Title: Senior Executive, Market Development & Partnerships
Description:
Mandai Wildlife Group is the steward of Mandai Wildlife Reserve, a unique wildlife and nature destination in Singapore that is home to world-renown wildlife parks which connect visitors to the fascinating world of wildlife. The Group is driving an exciting rejuvenation plan at Mandai Wildlife Reserve, adjacent to Singapore’s Central Catchment Nature Reserve, that will integrate five wildlife parks with distinctive nature-based experiences, green public spaces and an eco-friendly resort.
Job Duties And Responsibilities
- Develop and manage strategic partnerships with community organisations, corporates, government agencies, associations and other key stakeholders to create mutually beneficial opportunities and strengthen market presence.
- Identify and develop new partnership opportunities by understanding community needs, market trends and partner objectives, translating these into relevant collaborations and initiatives.
- Build and nurture strong partner relationships, acting as a key liaison to understand partner needs, facilitate collaboration and deliver a positive partner experience.
- Manage partnerships across the end-to-end lifecycle, including opportunity development, proposals, negotiations, contracting, activation, performance tracking and relationship management.
- Draft partnership propositions and commercial proposals, working with internal stakeholders across marketing, operations, product and events to deliver partnership and community engagement initiatives.
- Develop and execute community engagement and partner activation initiatives to broaden audience reach, encourage participation and strengthen the company’s connection with local communities.

- Support GlobalTix vendor management and liaison, including coordinating system or operational issues, following up on resolutions, managing reports and ensuring timely communication between internal stakeholders, GlobalTix and relevant partners.
- Maintain accurate partnership and business development records, reports and databases, ensuring timely follow-ups and effective tracking of partner activities and opportunities.
- Represent the company in external stakeholder engagements and support events, activations and ad-hoc projects that contribute to business growth, community engagement and strategic partnership development
Job Requirements
- Minimum Diploma in Hospitality Management, Events, Business Administration/Management, Sales & Marketing or a related discipline.
- Minimum 2 years of experience in business development, partnerships, stakeholder management, community engagement, events or a related field.
- Experience in developing and managing relationships with corporates, community organisations, government agencies, associations or other external stakeholders will be an advantage.
- Strong ability to build and maintain a network of business and community contacts and develop relationships into meaningful partnerships.
- Commercially minded, with the ability to identify opportunities, develop partnership propositions and negotiate mutually beneficial arrangements.
- Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage stakeholders across different levels and organisations.
- Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills.
- Strategic and critical thinker with strong problem-solving skills and the ability to identify opportunities, risks and potential roadblocks proactively.
- Proactive, collaborative and adaptable team player with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
- Comfortable working across multiple stakeholders and managing projects from development through to execution.
- Willingness to support partner activations, events and engagements outside of regular working hours, including weekends and public holidays where required.

Title: Senior Executive, Venue Event Services
Description:
In this role, you will be responsible for the successful end-to-end delivery of events hosted within the venue, including conferences, corporate events, and client functions. This role focuses on upselling opportunities, operational planning, on-site execution, and stakeholder coordination, ensuring all events are delivered safely, efficiently, and to the required quality standards in accordance with venue policies and regulatory requirements.
- Manage the full event lifecycle within the venue, from initial planning and coordination through to on-site execution and post-event wrap-up.
- Translate client and organiser requirements into operationally sound, venue-compliant event plans, while identifying opportunities to upsell venue services where appropriate.
- Develop and manage event timelines, operational schedules, and on-site deployment plans.
- Act as the primary point of contact for venue-related matters across all event phases, including build-up, live event days, and teardown.
- Coordinate closely with internal teams (Operations, Facilities, Sales, etc.) to ensure aligned and timely event delivery.
- Liaise with event organisers, contractors, and service providers to ensure all works comply with venue rules, safety standards, and approved timelines.
- Identify opportunities to enhance event delivery through additional venue services, in collaboration with relevant internal teams.
- Ensure all events comply with venue policies, safety regulations, and relevant statutory requirements, implementing necessary controls and approvals as required.
- Proactively manage and resolve operational issues, conflicts, and on-site incidents, including escalation and crisis management where required.
- Maintain accurate event documentation and records, including operational notes, feedback where applicable.
- Any ad hoc duties as assigned by Reporting Officer from time to time.
Requirements
- Diploma or Degree in Events, Hospitality, Business, Marketing or related discipline advantageous.
- Minimum 1 to 2 years of experience in a venue-based event, operations or hospitality environment.
- Demonstrated experience supporting events from planning through on-site execution and post-event follow-up.
- Strong understanding of venue operations, on-site event execution, and safety considerations.
- Customer-oriented mindset, focused on delivering positive experiences while upholding venue standards.
- Proven ability to work effectively with multiple internal departments and external stakeholders.
- Ability to multi-task and manage multiple priorities across concurrent events and timelines.
- Strong planning, organisational, and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple events concurrently.
- High level of attention to detail and sound operational judgment.
- Resourceful, proactive, and calm under pressure in a live event environment.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, PowerPoint, Excel).
- Willingness to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends, based on event requirements.

Title: Senior Executive/Assistant Manager, Advocacy & Partnerships (Major Gift)
Description:
About the Role
This role is suited for are relationship-oriented fundraising professional who enjoys connecting with people, understanding donor motivations and translating meaningful conversations into long-term partnerships.
You will support HCA's major gifts programme by managing donor relationships, preparing tailored proposals and reports, coordinating donor engagement activities, conducting prospect research and working with colleagues across the organisation to develop funding opportunities.
While this role includes fundraising administration where required, its primary focus is building and stewarding relationships that inspire philanthropic giving.
Key Responsibilities
Major Gifts & Donor Relationship Management
Build and maintain meaningful relationships with individual donors, families, philanthropists, corporate partners and foundations.
Support the cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of major gift donors across the donor lifecycle.
Manage an assigned portfolio of donors and prospects appropriate to experience and organisational needs.
Conduct regular donor meetings, presentations and engagement sessions.
Prepare personalised stewardship plans and follow-up actions.
Coordinate donor visits, programme tours and engagement opportunities.
Ensure timely acknowledgement and recognition of donor support.
Prospect Research & Pipeline Development
Identify prospective major donors through research and networking opportunities.
Prepare donor profiles, briefing papers and meeting notes.
Maintain an accurate fundraising pipeline and relationship records.
Monitor donor interactions and recommend appropriate next steps.
Work with internal stakeholders to identify new funding opportunities.
Proposal Development & Institutional Fundraising
Prepare tailored funding proposals, concept papers and donor presentations.
Support grant applications and institutional fundraising opportunities.
Coordinate donor reports, impact updates and funding reports.
Work with programme and clinical colleagues to gather information required for proposals and donor reporting.
Assist in developing compelling cases for support aligned with HCA's funding priorities.
Stewardship & Donor Engagement
Develop meaningful stewardship experiences that strengthen donor relationships.
Coordinate donor appreciation events, recognition activities and engagement opportunities.
Ensure donors receive timely updates on the impact of their support.
Work with the communications team on donor stories and engagement materials where appropriate.
Partnerships & Fundraising Initiatives
Support corporate partnership discussions and community fundraising initiatives.
Represent HCA Hospice at networking events, meetings and fundraising activities where appropriate.
Support fundraising campaigns and special projects led by the Advocacy & Partnerships Department.
Collaborate with colleagues across HCA to identify opportunities for donor engagement.
Department Support
Prepare reports, presentations and fundraising updates.
Maintain accurate donor records using HCA's donor management system.
Support departmental planning, budgeting and fundraising administration where required.
Contribute to continuous improvement of fundraising processes and donor experience.
Undertake other duties reasonably related to the role that support the department's fundraising and engagement objectives.
Who We're Looking For
We're looking for someone who enjoys building relationships, is naturally curious about people and is motivated by creating meaningful partnerships that make a lasting difference.
Qualifications
Degree in Business, Communications, Marketing, Social Sciences, Non profit Management or a related discipline.
Experience
Approximately three to six years of relevant experience for Senior Executive level, or five or more years for Assistant Manager level, depending on experience and demonstrated competencies.
Experience in fundraising, philanthropy, donor relations, business development, account management, partnership management, relationship management or a similar c slient-facing role would be advantageous.
Experience in the charity, healthcare or social service sector is welcome but not essential.
Skills
Excellent interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
Strong written communication skills, with the ability to prepare donor proposals, reports and correspondence.
Strong presentation and meeting facilitation skills.
Ability to manage multiple donor relationships and priorities.
Good organisational and project management skills.
Comfortable using Microsoft Office and Teams
Comfortable learning and working with donor management systems or CRM platforms.
High level of professionalism, discretion and integrity.
Attributes for Success
You may be a good fit if you are:
A confident and authentic relationship builder.
Curious and proactive in identifying opportunities.
Comfortable engaging senior stakeholders and donors.
An excellent listener with empathy and professionalism.
Organised and able to follow through on commitments.
Collaborative and willing to work across teams.
Adaptable and comfortable balancing strategic thinking with hands-on execution.
Motivated by meaningful work and creating social impact.
Occasional evening or weekend work may be required to support donor engagement activities and fundraising events.
What You Can Expect
As part of HCA Hospice's Advocacy & Partnerships team, you will contribute to building meaningful philanthropic partnerships that enable compassionate care for patients and families.
The role offers broad exposure to:
Major gifts fundraising
Individual giving
Corporate and foundation partnerships
Institutional fundraising
Donor stewardship
Proposal development
Fundraising strategy and pipeline management
Stakeholder engagement within Singapore's charity and healthcare sector
Working alongside colleagues across fundraising, communications, finance, operations and clinical services, you will have the opportunity to develop practical experience across the full donor journey while contributing to HCA Hospice's mission.

Degree in Business, Communications, Marketing, Social Sciences, Non profit Management or a related discipline.
Experience

Title: Senior Lead, Partnership
Description:
Job Description
Job ID: MJ000375
About Traveloka
Traveloka is Southeast Asia's leading travel and lifestyle super-app. We connect tens of millions of travellers across the region with flights, hotels, experiences, financial services, and more — all from a single platform. Since our founding in 2012, we have expanded to eleven markets, processed billions of dollars in transactions, and built one of the most recognised consumer brands in the region.
We move fast because the region demands it. Southeast Asia is young, mobile-first, and growing faster than almost anywhere else on earth. We are not transplanting a Western playbook — we are writing a new one, from scratch, for a market that does not look like anywhere else — and we are calling for people who want to be part of that.
About The Team
Payments is the platform every Traveloka transaction runs through — and the commercial side is where that platform turns into lasting partnerships with the institutions that make regional payments work. You will shape how millions of travellers across Southeast Asia pay: the cards, wallets, bank rails, and pay-later options that fit each of our markets, no two of which behave the same way. This is product and partnership work where the agreement you negotiate and the experience you ship are the same problem.
You will build and steward relationships with banks, networks, and fintech players — understanding their priorities as closely as our own — and translate that collaboration into payment products people actually choose at checkout. You think in unit economics and conversion rates as fluently as in partner roadmaps and mutual value. If you want to build durable, win-win partnerships around a system the whole company depends on, this is where you do it.
About The Job
As a Senior Lead on the Payment team, you are the deepest individual-contributor authority on a complex set of payment partnerships spanning markets and partner types. You influence payment strategy well beyond your own remit, without managing a team.
- Own the health of a broad payment partnership portfolio across multiple markets and segments as an expert IC, shaping terms, incentives, and partner mix collaboratively for the relationships you own
- Shape Traveloka's payment cost and partnership approach alongside product and finance leadership
- Steward our most critical relationships — leading negotiations with major banks, schemes, and fintechs toward agreements that work for both sides
- Build the analytical and negotiation standards the wider team works to, raising the bar through expertise rather than headcount
- Influence enterprise decisions on payment methods, pricing, and partner mix using rigorous, jointly-grounded analysis
- Drive operational excellence in partnership execution so payments launch faster, perform better, and cost less to run
- Represent Traveloka as a senior payments voice with partners, regulators, and the industry — building trust as much as driving terms

- Bachelor's degree in a relevant field; an MBA or relevant Master's is a plus
- At least 10 years of experience in payments, fintech, or strategic partnerships, with a track record as a senior advisor or subject-matter expert who combines deep payment product knowledge with structuring complex, multi-stakeholder agreements
- A strong track record of owning large payment partnership portfolios and the cost and value impact behind them
- Ability to shape approach across markets and align product and finance behind it through influence, not authority
- Ability to set the analytical and negotiation standard others follow, deepening capability through your expertise
- Skill negotiating and building consensus at the most senior levels, both internally and with major partners
- Rigorous reasoning about payment economics, using data and AI to inform joint decisions at scale
- Autonomy and sound judgment in ambiguous, fast-moving markets, with no team to manage
- Clarity and authority communicating in English; regional language ability is a strong plus
- Personal experience building and managing a payments partnership portfolio across several Southeast Asian markets
- Experience structuring landmark, mutually-beneficial partnerships with tier-one banks, card networks, or wallet platforms
- A track record of shaping enterprise payment-cost or monetisation strategy through collaborative partner engagement, with measurable impact

Title: Senior Manager, Business Development & Partnerships Manager
Description:
Job Description
We are seeking a Business Development Manager to drive the origination and commercialisation of Keppel's future subsea cable systems. Together with the Technical Team, you will own the market intelligence that helps shape route selection, build the partnerships and consortiums that make joint builds possible, landing parties, co-investors and anchor customers that underpin each project's business case. Lead the sales of the FPs through the negotiations of IRU and O&M agreement with target customers.
This is a relationship-driven, commercially sharp role for someone who knows the global subsea ecosystem — hyperscalers, carriers, landing parties and supporting engagements with suppliers, investors and lenders.
1: Market intelligence, insights and origination
- Own Keppel's market view of the global and regional subsea cable landscape: capacity supply and demand, route economics, pricing trends (IRU, lease and spectrum), and competitor system announcements — producing regular insight reports and demand forecasts that inform investment decisions and underwriting assumptions.
- Track emerging trends shaping future demand — AI and hyperscale data centre growth, cloud region expansion, edge connectivity, cable resilience and route diversity requirements, and new technologies
- Originate and qualify new system opportunities: route feasibility (with technical teams), addressable demand, competitive positioning leading to development of business case
- Represent Keppel at key industry forums and convert conference presence into pipeline.
2: Strategic Partnerships & Customer Engagements
- Identify, originate and secure strategic partners, co-investors and anchor customers for new cable systems, including hyperscalers, Global Carriers, etc
- Lead the structuring and negotiation of all commercial arrangements — from consortium and investment agreements (MOUs, JBAs, LPAs, Fibre Pair allocations, governance frameworks) through to customer contracts (IRUs, capacity and spectrum agreements, leases and O&M arrangements) — from term sheet to execution.
- Manage all partnership relationships (together with Technical Teams) across the full lifecycle — through development, construction and into service — aligning stakeholders on route selection, system design, commercial structure, supplier strategy, budget and schedule, and capturing upgrade, renewal and expansion opportunities.
- Assist with regulatory, licensing and market entry initiatives, including building of business cases, securing landing parties, backhaul arrangements and necessary government and industry stakeholder support.
- Develop and execute go-to-market, pricing and commercialisation strategies for each system, ensuring alignment with investment cases, underwriting assumptions and long-term revenue objectives.
- Identify adjacent revenue opportunities across the Keppel ecosystem — including data centre interconnection, marine services and integrated connectivity solutions — and work closely with various corporate functions and external advisers to develop bankable transaction structures.
3: Investment Case & Commercial
- Own the investment approval papers, ensuring underwriting assumptions are robust, defensible and aligned with fund co-investor requirements.
- Working with Keppel's Fund Management & Investment & Commercial Project manager to build the investment case and underwriting model for new subsea cable projects
- Develop and maintain the full project financial model: capex and opex build-up, capacity sales assumptions (IRUs, leases, spectrum), revenue phasing, returns analysis (IRR, MOIC, payback) and sensitivity/scenario testing.
Join our vibrant and inclusive workforce to shape a better future for all!

- Direct experience negotiating JBA, IRU, capacity, spectrum and/or O&M agreements.

- Experience working alongside investment/fund management teams or with co-investment structures.

Title: Senior Manager, Business Development - Rest of Asia (Taiwan & Hong Kong Operators / China CE Partnerships)
Description:
Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.
In building and scaling our business across the Rest of Asia, we've established partnerships with leading mobile, broadband, and PayTV operators in Taiwan and Hong Kong (e.g. CHT Group, Taiwan Mobile, PCCW/CSL), as well as with the largest Mainland China consumer electronics manufacturers (e.g. Hisense, TCL, Xiaomi, Oppo) that ship smart TVs and mobile devices across the region and globally.
These partnerships help deliver Netflix in a consumer-friendly way - from bundling Netflix into a mobile or broadband plan, to prominent, durable placement on smart TVs and mobile devices - and have been essential to accelerating our global growth.
Chinese CE OEMs in particular are now among the largest and fastest-growing players in the global TV ecosystem, making them ever more strategic partners for Netflix.
We're looking for a Senior Manager, Business Development to grow our commercial partnerships with Taiwan/Hong Kong operators and Mainland China CE/mobile partners - building the strategic roadmap for these relationships, support structuring and commercial alignments in deals, and working closely with cross-functional teams to ensure successful launch and ongoing performance of these partnerships.
The role will report to the Director, Business Development - Rest of Asia, and will be based in Taipei or Singapore.
Responsibilities
- You will forge and manage commercial partnerships with mobile, broadband, and PayTV operators in Taiwan and Hong Kong, building new bundles and promotions and deepening existing relationships to streamline Netflix membership and viewing in an efficient manner.
- You will lead commercial relationships with Mainland China consumer electronics and mobile manufacturers, and provide support in structuring and commercial alignments in device placement, promotional, and distribution agreements that maximize discovery, reach, and viewing for current and prospective members.
- You will develop and execute the partnership strategy and roadmap for this territory, identifying new bundling, distribution, and promotional opportunities, and prioritizing them based on business impact.
- You will own the deal lifecycle end-to-end - from business case development and support closing out commercial alignments to be reflected through contracting and ongoing account management - and will track partner performance against agreed goals.
- You will work closely with colleagues in Partner Engagement, Product, Marketing, Legal, and Finance to translate commercial agreements into successful technical integrations and go-to-market execution.
- You will analyze market data and competitive dynamics to identify trends and opportunities, and create compelling market and business analyses for internal leadership and partner-facing conversations.
- You will represent Netflix externally with senior partner stakeholders, and internally as part of the Rest of Asia Business Development and Partnerships team.
The Ideal Candidate
- Minimum 12 years of experience in Business Development, partnerships, or commercial roles with a technology, telecom, consumer electronics, or media company
- Experience partnering with telecom operators, PayTV/ISPs, consumer electronics manufacturers, or adjacent industries, ideally in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and/or Mainland China
- Proven track record in structuring, negotiating, and closing commercial partnership agreements
- Deep understanding of the streaming video landscape and consumer behavior in Greater China markets
- Ability to work effectively with cross-functional leaders across Product, Marketing, Legal, Finance, and Partner Engineering
- Experience drafting, negotiating, and closing term sheets and contracts
- Strong analytical and business-case skills; able to translate market data into strategy and clear recommendations
- Strong self-organization and prioritization abilities; comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy
- Fluent proficiency in Mandarin and English; Cantonese a plus

Carousell Luxury is growing, and this role sits at the centre of it. You’ll build and run our partner network, working with professional resellers, dealers and trade partners to unlock new growth for the business.

Recruit and manage professional resellers to exhibit at Carousell Luxury Brand Fairs, and grow partner participation event by event

Build B2B partnerships

Design partner processes end to end, working closely with Operations and Retail so they run smoothly without adding to the team’s workload
Negotiate terms, sign and manage partners, and track performance weekly
Make data-driven calls on when to scale, adjust or stop a pilot
Own the numbers
Set targets, track partner performance, and report progress to leadership every week

Experience in B2B partnerships, business development or wholesale, ideally in luxury, resale or retail
Strong commercial judgement: you can size a deal, negotiate terms, and know when to scale or exit a pilot
An operator’s mindset: you design processes that work on the ground
Comfortable owning targets and reporting against them weekly
Self-driven and at home in ambiguity, with a track record of building something new
A network among luxury resellers and dealers in Singapore is a strong plus

Build new partnerships and channels from the ground up, with real ownership and visibility to leadership
Work at the intersection of luxury, recommerce and marketplaces at Southeast Asia’s leading recommerce platform
A cross-functional role where your decisions directly shape how the business grows

Title: Senior Manager, Channel Partners
Description:
The Company
PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.
We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects hundreds of millions of merchants and consumers. We help merchants and consumers connect, transact, and complete payments, whether they are online or in person. PayPal is more than a connection to third-party payment networks. We provide proprietary payment solutions accepted by merchants that enable the completion of payments on our platform on behalf of our customers.
We offer our customers the flexibility to use their accounts to purchase and receive payments for goods and services, as well as the ability to transfer and withdraw funds. We enable consumers to exchange funds more safely with merchants using a variety of funding sources, which may include a bank account, a PayPal or Venmo account balance, PayPal and Venmo branded credit products, a credit card, a debit card, certain cryptocurrencies, or other stored value products such as gift cards, and eligible credit card rewards. Our PayPal, Venmo, and Xoom products also make it safer and simpler for friends and family to transfer funds to each other. We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.
Our beliefs are the foundation for how we conduct business every day. We live each day guided by our core values of Inclusion, Innovation, Collaboration, and Wellness. Together, our values ensure that we work together as one global team with our customers at the center of everything we do – and they push us to ensure we take care of ourselves, each other, and our communities.
Job Summary:
This role leads the Channel Partners program across IGM, shaping PayPal’s partner-led growth strategy and evolution. The focus is on Cars and strategic partner archetypes that can extend PayPal’s reach across international markets.
The Senior Manager owns Channel Partners strategy, capability maturity and commercial outcomes. Responsibilities include prioritising partner archetypes and markets, monitoring cart performance, creating repeatable go-to-market playbooks, leading multi-regional deals, negotiating roadmap commitments, aligning market GMs and global stakeholders, and establishing governance for consistent execution and measurable growth.
This is a capability-building role, not an administration or reporting role. You will design a commercial model for IGM, create scalable playbooks that reflect local needs, identify key partner opportunities, influence product and integration roadmaps, maintain the deal pipeline, and establish Channel Partners as a durable route to market.

About the Role
Join us as Senior Manager, Client Services & Business Delivery at AIA Investment Management!
At AIA Investment Management, we believe in creating long-term value for our clients and communities. We are seeking a dynamic Senior Manager, Client Services and Business Delivery to join our team. In this role, you will be directly responsible for leading institutional client relationships and overseeing the end-to-end delivery of client and business initiatives, ensuring exceptional service standards, operational excellence, and successful execution of strategic portfolio and business priorities, driving critical outcomes that strengthen client partnerships, enable sustainable business growth, and deliver impactful investment solutions that support AIA Investment Management's long-term objectives across the APAC region.
Key Responsibilities
As part of our high-performing team, you will directly influence client satisfaction, operational efficiency, and risk management, which are core to business continuity and growth through:
1) Client Relationship Management
Lead relationships with assigned institutional clients and serve as their trusted investment contact.
Develop a strong understanding of client objectives, portfolio structures, priorities and constraints.
Build effective relationships at all levels and manage complex stakeholder dynamics with sound judgement.
2) Portfolio Solutions
Partner with Front Office teams to translate client requirements into practical portfolio solutions and actions.
Facilitate discussions on investment strategies, portfolio changes and asset allocation.
Clarify requirements and apply knowledge of portfolio positioning and implementation to ensure solutions are effective and deliverable.
3) Client Service and Delivery
Deliver proactive, high-quality day-to-day service and own complex client matters through resolution.
Coordinate support functions on client instructions, documentation, reporting and servicing.
Track commitments and deliverables, ensuring timely follow-through and escalation.
4) Transitions and Implementation
Support new mandates, restructurings and other material portfolio changes from planning through implementation.
Coordinate front-to-back teams to clarify requirements, dependencies and risks.
Represent the client perspective and support timely resolution of implementation issues and trade-offs.
5) Senior Stakeholder Engagement
Lead senior stakeholder discussions on portfolios, strategy, investment updates, issues and new requirements.
Manage challenging or sensitive discussions with professionalism and credibility.
Ensure materials and communications are accurate, appropriately nuanced and clear for senior audiences.
Minimum Requirements
We are looking for professionals who possess:
Degree in business or a related discipline. A professional designation such as CFA would be an advantage.
Min 10 years of specialized investment / asset management related experience across the end-to-end investment control lifecycle with direct involvement in the client servicing, business support, management of investment asset change / infrastructure.
Specialized knowledge: Strong understanding of end-to-end investment processes across front and back office, including a good understanding of client onboarding processes in an asset management business
Excellent listening and strong communication skills both verbal and written.
Excellent interpersonal skills, experienced in working collaboratively to lead in team structure
Capable of working across a variety of organizational dimensions and managing across a diversity of disciplines and cultures, with proactive approach and a bias towards collaboration and reaching win-win outcomes
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
Ability to deal with and handle multiple and changing priorities.

About JOOLA
JOOLA is a globally recognised table tennis and pickleball brand with an expanding presence across Asia-Pacific. With over 70 years of heritage in racket sports and a strong commitment to innovation, we create products and experiences for players at every level - from everyday enthusiasts to elite athletes competing at the highest levels of the sport.
As JOOLA continues to grow, so do the opportunities for our people. Our expanding regional business offers exposure across markets, functions and cultures, as well as the chance to take on broader responsibilities and help build new capabilities. We want our people to develop alongside the organisation by deepening their expertise, broadening their experience and taking on new challenges as opportunities emerge.
We combine the energy and ownership of an entrepreneurial environment with the ambition of a global brand. At JOOLA, you will be encouraged to contribute ideas, work across boundaries and make a visible impact - not only within your role, but also on the next stage of our growth.
Our global headquarters is based in the United States, and our Asia-Pacific headquarters is based in Singapore.

Success in this role will be measured by the sustainable growth and commercial performance of the assigned markets, effective development of distribution partners and channels, and progress against JOOLA’s strategic market priorities.
As a key Commercial leader for APAC, you will play a pivotal role in developing markets, strengthening strategic partnerships and evolving JOOLA’s route-to-market as the business scales, while building the commercial foundations that support the next phase of the Company’s regional expansion.

- Develop and execute multi-year commercial strategies and annual business plans for assigned markets, aligned with APAC priorities
- Assess market potential, competitive dynamics and consumer and channel trends to identify growth opportunities and investment priorities

- Identify opportunities across categories, channels and strategic accounts to expand JOOLA’s presence and build sustainable market leadership

- Establish targets and commercial priorities, monitor performance and drive corrective actions where required
- Evaluate growth opportunities and commercial investments based on business impact and return
- Develop strong understanding and ownership of market-level P&L drivers, including revenue, margin, investment and cost-to-serve
3. Distributor Leadership & Capability
- Lead JOOLA’s commercial relationships with distribution partners, establishing clear business objectives, expectations and performance standards
- Drive structured business planning and performance reviews covering growth, inventory, channel development and key commercial priorities
- Strengthen distributor capabilities in commercial planning, forecasting, inventory management and market execution
- Evaluate partner effectiveness and identify new or alternative distribution partners where required to support JOOLA’s long-term market development
4. Channel, Product & Commercial Execution
- Develop appropriate channel and assortment strategies based on market maturity, consumer needs and JOOLA’s brand objectives
- Lead distributor readiness and commercial execution for key product launches and seasonal initiatives
- Drive pricing, trade-term and channel discipline in line with JOOLA’s regional commercial framework
- Partner with regional eCommerce expertise to integrate marketplaces and digital commerce appropriately within overall market strategies
- Monitor sell-in, sell-through, inventory and market performance to identify opportunities and proactively address business risks
5. Cross-Functional Leadership
- Act as the commercial lead for assigned markets, aligning regional functions and distribution partners around agreed market priorities
- Translate market needs and opportunities into clear commercial priorities while ensuring effective execution across relevant functions
- Provide structured market insights and recommendations to support regional decision-making, resource allocation and future growth
What We’re Looking For
- 10+ years of progressive commercial experience across sales, business development, general management, distributor management or related commercial functions
- Demonstrated experience leading multi-market distributor or partner-led businesses, ideally across Southeast Asia and/or Emerging Markets
- Strong track record of delivering revenue growth while developing markets, channels and long-term commercial capabilities
- Strong commercial and financial acumen, with experience in business planning, P&L drivers, route-to-market, forecasting and inventory management
- Strong strategic judgement, with the ability to assess opportunities, set priorities and make sound commercial decisions in complex or developing markets
- Strong leadership, negotiation and influencing skills, with the ability to lead effectively across external partners and cross-functional stakeholders
- Experience in sporting goods, consumer products, footwear, apparel, lifestyle or other brand-led industries is preferred; working knowledge of eCommerce and marketplace business models is an advantage

At JOOLA, you will have the opportunity to take ownership of your work and make a meaningful contribution. As part of a growing business, you will be able to learn, take on new challenges and develop your career.

Title: Senior Manager, Strategic Partnerships
Description:
About The Company
Founders today are building global companies from day one — but the systems that manage their money were built for a different era. Aspire exists to change that!
We’re building the financial operating system for global founders, bringing banking, software, and automation into a single platform so businesses can move faster across borders and stay focused on building.
Aspire is built by people who think from first principles, care deeply about solving hard problems, and take real ownership of their work. Our team brings global experience from leading fintech and technology companies, and many of us are former founders and operators who understand what it takes to build thoughtfully, make trade-offs, and deliver at scale in a global environment.
Backed by leading global investors including Y Combinator, Peak XV, and Lightspeed, Aspire has been trusted by more than 50,000 startups and growing businesses worldwide to manage their finances since 2018. Together with partners like J.P. Morgan, Visa, and Wise, we’re building for the next generation of global companies.
About The Role
Aspire is moving up-market, and partnerships is how we intend to get there. Mid-market companies — think 50 to 500 employees — don't choose their finance stack from a website. They choose it on the advice of their accountant, their ERP implementation partner, or the systems integrator who's been in their business for three years. This role builds Aspire's presence in that ecosystem across Singapore and Hong Kong.
You'll be building the partner motion, not inheriting one. That means defining the partner segments, signing the first partners in each, designing the commercial models and enablement, and standing up the co-sell motion with our direct sales team. You'll do it as an individual contributor with the full weight of the Partnerships, Sales, Marketing, and Product teams behind you — and with the expectation that what you build here becomes the template for the next market.
If you want a role where the programme already exists and your job is to run it, this isn't it. If you want to own a channel from a blank page and have the commercial results attributed to you, read on.
About The Team
Our Partnerships tribe builds and manages the relationships that extend Aspire's reach. You'll work with banks, platforms, and other partners to unlock new opportunities for our customers.
What You'll Own
- Own the partner-sourced revenue plan for mid-market across Singapore and Hong Kong, with broader APAC expansion as the motion proves out
- Identify, recruit, and sign the partners that mid-market finance teams already trust: large and mid-tier accounting firms, ERP vendors, systems integrators, ISVs, and technology consultants
- Build and manage the ERP reseller and VAR channel — partner tiering, margin and revenue-share structures, deal registration, and clear rules of engagement with direct sales
- Negotiate partnership agreements and design commercial models that hold up for both sides
- Run joint business planning and quarterly reviews with top partners: agreed targets, named pipeline, and a shared plan to deliver against it
- Build partner enablement — the collateral, training, and certification that lets a partner's own team position and sell Aspire without you in the room
- Build Aspire's relationships with trade associations, chambers of commerce, and industry bodies across Singapore and Hong Kong, negotiating access to member bases through endorsed supplier programmes, member benefit schemes, sponsorships, and speaking platforms
- Design joint programmes with associations that put Aspire in front of members with their credibility behind it — held to a pipeline outcome, not an attendance figure
- Build a repeatable association playbook so the sixth one takes a fraction of the effort of the first
- Design and run co-marketing campaigns, joint webinars, workshops, and industry programmes with partners, each with a pipeline target attached
- Represent Aspire at industry conferences, trade shows, and partner events across the region
- Measure programme ROI honestly and retire what doesn't convert
- Work with Aspire's product and engineering teams on integrations with the platforms our partners and their clients already run, feeding the field view back into the roadmap
- Run the co-sell motion with Sales: account mapping, lead routing, deal registration, and joint pursuit on named accounts
- Co-own the joint campaign and event calendar with Field and Partner Marketing, and the partner marketing spend behind it
- Share playbooks and reusable commercial structures across markets and partner types with the wider Partnerships team
What You Need To Be Successful
- You've built a partner or channel programme from close to zero and carried a partner-sourced revenue number against it — contributing to someone else's established programme isn't the same thing
- 6–8 years in strategic partnerships, channel sales, or ecosystem development
- Direct experience in the ERP, accounting software, fintech, SaaS, or B2B technology ecosystem — you understand how these partners make money and what makes a partnership worth their time
- A track record in partner-led demand generation — co-marketing, joint webinars, industry programmes — measured in pipeline rather than activity
- Strong commercial instincts: you can structure and negotiate a revenue share, a referral fee, or a reseller margin, and you know which one fits the situation

Title: Senior Manager, Strategic Partnerships & Fundraising
Description:
ABOUT EQUAL
EQUAL is an IPC-registered charity that delivers equine-assisted and animal-assisted services to support the mental and emotional wellbeing of children, youth, seniors, families, and communities. Our work sits at the intersection of human wellbeing, animal welfare, and experiential learning, and is delivered through a multidisciplinary team of programme professionals, equine specialists, operations staff, and volunteers. Fundraising is mission-critical to EQUAL’s ability to deliver safe, high-quality, and impactful programmes. As the organisation scales, EQUAL is strengthening its fundraising infrastructure, pipeline discipline, and stewardship capability to support sustainable growth.
ROLE SUMMARY
The Senior Manager, Strategic Partnerships & Fundraising is responsible for developing and securing corporate, philanthropic and institutional funding partnerships that support EQUAL's programmes and long-term sustainability.
The role takes ownership of assigned funding opportunities and works closely with the CEO and Board on major donor relationships and strategic partnerships.
The Senior Manager works within EQUAL's partnerships and fundraising function, supported by a Manager, Partnerships & Development and a Digital Marketing Consultant.
The Senior Manager focuses on revenue generation and relationship development, with administrative, stewardship, communications and grant-related support from relevant colleagues.
KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
Success will be measured through fundraising results, partnership development and the strength of the funding pipeline.
Success will be measured through:
Revenue generation: Delivering agreed annual fundraising targets through directly managed and collaborative funding opportunities.
New partnerships: Securing new corporate, philanthropic and institutional funding partners.
Pipeline development: Building, managing and converting qualified funding opportunities.
Partner retention and growth: Developing repeat and multi-year funding from assigned partners.
Strategic contribution: Supporting CEO- and Board-led major donor engagements and fundraising initiatives.
Annual revenue targets, individual responsibilities and performance milestones will be agreed with the CEO, taking into account organisational priorities, existing funding opportunities and available resources.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (6-12 month horizon)
Understand EQUAL's fundraising priorities, existing partners and funding pipeline.
Build and actively manage a qualified pipeline of new opportunities.
Progress priority prospects and convert funding opportunities where feasible.
Deliver against agreed revenue and pipeline targets.
Convert qualified opportunities into funded partnerships.
Develop repeat and multi-year funding opportunities.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Strategic Partnerships & Funding Development
Lead assigned corporate, philanthropic and institutional funding opportunities from prospect identification through to funding commitments and partnership growth.
Responsibilities include:
Identify and cultivate corporate partners, family offices, foundations and private donors aligned with EQUAL's mission.
Develop tailored funding proposals, sponsorship packages and CSR partnership opportunities.
Lead partnership discussions and funding negotiations for assigned opportunities.
Secure programme funding, sponsorships, multi-year commitments and strategic partnerships.
2. Partnership Pipeline Development
Build and manage a qualified partnership pipeline, ensuring opportunities are prioritised, actively progressed and accurately tracked.
Responsibilities include:
Identify and qualify new funding prospects.
Maintain clear opportunity ownership, funding potential, priorities and next steps.
Prepare donor briefings and ensure timely follow-up after meetings.
Review pipeline progress and revenue forecasts regularly with the CEO, supported by accurate CRM records.
3. Strategic Fundraising Campaigns & Initiatives
Develop funding and partnership opportunities that support EQUAL's key campaigns and fundraising initiatives.
Responsibilities include:
Secure sponsorships and partner funding for agreed fundraising campaigns and events.
Work with internal teams to develop funding propositions aligned with programme needs and impact.
Develop corporate engagement opportunities that support longer-term partnerships.
4. Major Donor & High-Value Partnerships
Work closely with the CEO and, where appropriate, Board members to develop and progress major donor relationships and high-value funding opportunities.
Responsibilities include:
Develop proposals, briefing materials and funding recommendations for major donor engagements.
Support relationship cultivation, strategic partnership discussions and multi-year funding opportunities.
Coordinate follow-up and progression of CEO- and Board-led funding opportunities.
The CEO typically leads selected major donor relationships, with Board involvement where appropriate. The Senior Manager's responsibilities for these opportunities will be agreed with the CEO.
5. Fundraising Events & Donor Engagement
Support EQUAL's major fundraising events and donor engagement activities, with a primary focus on securing sponsorships, funding partnerships and building donor relationships.
Responsibilities include:
Securing sponsorships and funding partnerships for key events and initiatives.
Engaging prospective donors through events, programme visits and other engagement activities.
Following up with prospects and partners to develop longer-term funding relationships.
Working collaboratively with colleagues to support the planning and delivery of major organisational events.\
Event planning and delivery are shared responsibilities across relevant teams, with the Senior Manager contributing as part of the broader organisational effort.
ROLE ACCOUNTABILITY & ORGANISATIONAL SUPPORT
The Senior Manager is accountable for developing and converting assigned funding opportunities, delivering agreed revenue and pipeline targets, and contributing to EQUAL's broader fundraising efforts.
The role is supported by:
CEO
: Leads selected major donor relationships and supports senior-level strategic partnership engagements.
Board and Fundraising Committee
: Strategic guidance and participation in selected donor engagements, where appropriate.
Manager, Partnerships & Development
: Partnership/key event coordination, donor stewardship, CRM administration and fundraising documentation.
Digital Marketing Consultant
: Communications and digital marketing support for agreed fundraising campaigns and partnership initiatives.
Programmes and Services teams
: Programme information, impact data and coordination support for agreed donor engagements.
The Senior Manager's primary focus is fundraising and partnership development, supported by colleagues in areas such as grant reporting, CRM administration, donor stewardship and communications. As part of EQUAL's collaborative working culture, the role also contributes to major organisational events and initiatives where crossteam support is required.
QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS
Substantial relevant experience, typically 8 years or more, in fundraising, strategic partnerships, business development or corporate engagement.
Demonstrated success in originating, developing and converting funding or commercial partnerships, with clear accountability for individual contributions and results.
Experience engaging senior corporate leaders, donors or institutional stakeholders.
Experience in nonprofit fundraising, major gifts or CSR partnerships is an advantage.
Core Competencies
Strong relationship-building and senior stakeholder engagement capabilities.
Proven ability to develop, manage and convert partnership opportunities.
Strong proposal development, negotiation and communication skills.
Sound commercial judgement and ability to prioritise opportunities.
Strategic thinking combined with disciplined, hands-on execution.
Key Attributes
Proactive and outcome-driven
Professional and credible with senior stakeholders
Highly organised and disciplined in follow-through
Comfortable operating in a lean team with shared responsibilities
Motivated by mission and impact
WHY JOIN US?
Make a tangible impact in a mission-driven team, grow across operations and systems, and work in a unique, nature-rich environment with meaningful outcomes.
HOW TO APPLY
Please email your updated CV and a short cover letter to
pradeep.thevar@equal.org.sg
with the subject line “Partnership & Development – Your Name”.
Founded in 2015, EQUAL (an IPC charity) strives to transform lives through Animal-Assisted Services. EQUAL partners with animals to provide experiential and educational programmes that help empower vulnerable persons such as children, youths, persons with special needs, families and seniors by enhancing their social and emotional well-being and supporting social integration in a safe environment — building resilience and inclusive communities.

Title: Senior Market Strategy and Partnerships Manager
Description:
Hey there!
We’re Fever, the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.
Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.
Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.
Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?
To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!
Ready to be part of the experience?
Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.
Meet The Team
At Fever, our Business Development team is both the face of Fever in the market and the voice of the market within Fever. Sitting at the core of our platform, they connect the world’s best experiences with the largest audiences, helping the live entertainment industry grow and evolve.
Our team builds trusted, long-term partnerships with leading brands across the ecosystem. We work closely with creators, producers, agencies, and cultural leaders to help them make data-driven decisions, expand their portfolios, and scale internationally. In doing so, we play a key role in shaping the future of the entertainment landscape.
This role goes far beyond relationship management. It requires strong strategic thinking and problem-solving across a wide range of topics, from marketing and pricing to operations and financing. The most successful team members take full ownership of their partners’ success, acting as true partners and advisors at every stage of growth.
Collaboration is at the heart of everything we do. Business Development works hand-in-hand with Marketing, Category Management, Partner Support, Operations, Tech, Product, and Finance to ensure every experience on our platform reaches its full potential.
Our team is diverse, entrepreneurial, and dynamic, bringing together talent from consulting, banking, big tech, and startups. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where creativity meets data, and ambition meets execution.
Join us if you’re passionate about discovering world-class experiences, building meaningful partnerships, and scaling some of the most exciting concepts across the globe.
The Role
In this role, you will drive Fever’s expansion across Singapore's entertainment industry by building and nurturing deep commercial relationships with top producers, creators, venues, and key stakeholders. You will develop and execute an innovative growth strategy to scale our market presence, expertly managing commercial strategies to ensure mutual value creation and build sustainable, long-term partnerships with event organizers. By collaborating closely with cross-functional teams both in Singapore and internationally, you will successfully balance a growing client base while serving as our in-house expert on the coolest trends and newest experiences in the entertainment landscape.
What You'll Do
- Create and cultivate deep business relationships with the biggest producers, creators, venues and key stakeholders in the entertainment industry.
- Develop and deliver a growth strategy for the market, with an innovative and effective approach to scaling Fever's presence in the region
- Expertly manage commercial strategy with large partners ensuring value creation for both parties, and a sustainable strategic partnership between Fever and event organisers
- Evidence strong organizational skills to effectively balance and grow a large base of clients
- Collaborate closely with cross functional stakeholders to successfully deliver on partner growth across Singapore and internationally
- Keep up to date with everything cool that’s happening in the entertainment; think of yourself as the expert for new and trending experiences
Who You Are

- At least 4+ years of top tier consulting or equivalent experience, with ideally an additional 4+ years of experience in relevant sectors (e.g. corporate management, tech companies, sport / music / arts)
- Strong business development and partnership management skills
- Self-starter mentality with an ability to work in a demanding, dynamic start-up environment
- Demonstrated data-driven approach to business and task prioritization
- Excellent communication skills both written and verbal along with strong attention to detail
- Comfort in working with Microsoft Office, Google docs, and a Sales CRM (Sugar CRM is preferred)

You will build and maintain key relationships across government agencies and institutional buyers, advance strategic sales opportunities, and work with a regional team of Partner Managers to manage pipeline and deliver results.
