Title: Sponsorship Fulfilment Associate Manager
Description:
The Sponsorship Fulfilment Associate Manager (12 months contract role) is responsible for managing confirmed sponsors and ensuring that all contracted sponsorship rights, benefits, exhibitor booth requirements, and deliverables are executed accurately and to a high standard.
This is a delivery-focused role and does not involve sponsorship prospecting, sales, or commercial negotiation. The Sponsorship Fulfilment Associate Manager will act as the primary day-to-day contact for confirmed sponsors, coordinating closely with the client, internal teams, venues, vendors, and event partners throughout the planning and delivery process.
The role requires a highly organised, detail-oriented professional who can manage multiple stakeholders, deadlines, and deliverables in a fast-paced event environment.
Key Responsibilities:
Sponsor Onboarding and Account Support
- Act as the day-to-day contact for an assigned portfolio of sponsors and exhibitors, and support the Sponsorship Fulfilment Manager on key and high-value accounts from onboarding through to post-event reporting.
- Review sponsorship agreements with the Sponsorship Fulfilment Manager and help translate contracted rights and benefits into fulfilment plans, timelines, and deliverables.
- Coordinate and take part in sponsor onboarding meetings to confirm objectives, booth requirements, key contacts, deadlines, and approval processes. Lead these meetings for assigned accounts.
- Give sponsors timely updates, clear guidance, and responsive support throughout the event lifecycle.
- Build positive working relationships with sponsors by delivering a professional and attentive service.
- Track sponsor requests and flag potential risks, delays, or out-of-scope requests to the Sponsorship Fulfilment Manager promptly.
Sponsorship Fulfilment and Coordination
- Maintain and update the sponsorship fulfilment tracker covering contracted benefits, exhibitor booth requirements, submission deadlines, approvals, dependencies, and completion status.
- Collect sponsor assets, including logos, advertisements, speaker information, presentation materials, booth designs, activation plans, guest lists, and other required content, and follow up on outstanding items.
- Check sponsor materials and booth submissions against event specifications, brand guidelines, venue regulations, production requirements, and agreed timelines, and flag any issues for resolution.
- Coordinate the delivery of sponsorship benefits such as branding, exhibition space, speaking opportunities, hospitality, digital exposure, delegate passes, and promotional activations.
- Support exhibitor booth coordination, including booth allocation, design submissions, and operational needs.
- Liaise with sponsors, booth contractors, venues, and appointed suppliers on booth production, technical requirements, and approvals.
- Work with creative, marketing, content, production, operations, registration, and venue teams to make sure sponsor and exhibitor requirements are reflected in event plans.
- Manage the internal and external approvals workflow for sponsor-related content, branding, booth designs, and activations, and escalate where needed.
- Carry out regular checks on the progress of sponsorship commitments and booth requirements, and report any gaps to the Sponsorship Fulfilment Manager.
Event Production and On-Site Delivery
- Support the translation of sponsorship commitments, such as booth space, branding, speaking slots, hospitality, and activations, into production and operational requirements.
- Coordinate sponsor and exhibitor logistics across the event production timeline, with a focus on accuracy and attention to detail.
- Prepare sponsor briefing materials, exhibitor guidelines, schedules, contact lists, and on-site fulfilment checklists.
- Coordinate booth setup requirements, exhibitor access, contractor arrangements, and build-up and breakdown schedules.
- Support sponsor and exhibitor setup, rehearsals, speaker coordination, and activation readiness ahead of the event.
- Support the on-site sponsor and exhibitor experience. Act as the first point of contact for assigned sponsors and make sure contracted deliverables are fulfilled.
- Handle on-site sponsor and exhibitor issues promptly, resolving them directly where possible and escalating to the Sponsorship Fulfilment Manager or relevant teams as needed.
- Conduct on-site checks of sponsor branding, exhibitor booths, activations, and other contracted benefits.
Reporting and Post-Event Follow-Up
- Prepare regular status updates on fulfilment progress, outstanding actions, dependencies, and potential risks for review by the Sponsorship Fulfilment Manager.
- Maintain accurate records of sponsor communications, booth requirements, approvals, changes, and completed deliverables.
- Collect evidence of fulfilment, including photographs, attendance information, digital metrics, and other relevant records.
- Assist in preparing post-event sponsor reports and fulfilment summaries.
- Gather sponsor and exhibitor feedback and contribute recommendations to improve future sponsorship programmes and event delivery.
Qualifications and Experience
- Strong experience in sponsorship fulfilment, sponsor servicing, exhibitor management, account management, or event delivery.
- Demonstrated experience managing sponsorship programmes and exhibitor booths for conferences, exhibitions, or large-scale events.
- Good understanding of exhibition production, booth requirements, and venue regulations.
- Excellent project-management and organisational skills, with strong attention to detail.
- Ability to interpret sponsorship agreements and convert them into practical delivery plans.
- Strong stakeholder-management and communication skills, including experience working with senior representatives.
- Able to work independently while collaborating effectively with clients, internal teams, agencies, venues, contractors, and suppliers.
- Calm, solutions-focused, and comfortable working under pressure in a fast-paced event environment.
- Proficient in maintaining trackers, timelines, status reports, and fulfilment documentation.
- Experience with financial services or FinTech events would be an advantage.

The Senior Product Manager, Fleet and Mobility - Key Client serves as a hands-on, embedded technical partner working day-to-day with internal Visa teams and external partners to build, launch, and scale new fleet and mobility solutions, driving successful solution delivery. This role translates Visa platform capabilities - including VIP authorization, clearing, and payment processing frameworks - into clear, actionable implementation guidance, and leads technical problem-solving and solution design across markets and use cases alongside the Key Client.

- Drive strong stakeholder engagement across markets, building trust and influence without direct authority.

- Experience working across APAC markets and managing multi-country initiatives.
- Proven track record of identifying, developing and executing growth initiatives.
- Experience structuring and negotiating commercial agreements together with Legal and Finance.
- An established network across the APAC healthcare ecosystem (industry, providers, channel) is a strong advantage.
- Exposure to portfolio or segment strategy and pricing/value-based commercial models is an advantage.
- Strategic and commercially astute, with a strong growth orientation and sound judgement on which opportunities are worth pursuing.
- Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing capabilities across complex setups.
- Proven experience in partnership development, alliance management, and negotiation.
- Strong communication, presentation and storytelling skills, with ability to influence diverse audiences.
- Analytical mindset with ability to translate insights into action.
- Ability to balance long-term strategy with short-term results delivery.
- Working understanding of portfolio and pricing strategy across customer segments, and how they interact with partnership and channel choices.
- Creative and entrepreneurial, with the ability to see non-obvious connections between portfolios, customer needs and market shifts.

Company: Cambridge Centre for Advanced Research and Education in Singapore Ltd
Title: Strategic Partnerships Lead
Description:
Who are we?
We are the University of Cambridge research centre in Singapore called Cambridge CARES, sponsored by the
NRF CREATE program CAM.CREATE. Health-driven design for cities (HD4) is a collaborative research programme
between the University of Cambridge, NTU and NUS within Cambridge CARES.
The Health-driven design for cities (HD4) programme at Cambridge CARES will undertake research in the
following key areas: dynamic characterisation of the features of the environment that potentially impact health
in Singapore; understanding the links between environmental factors, individual behaviour and health
outcomes; observing the impact of environmental change on health in Singapore; simulating the impact of
potential changes on the health of Singaporeans; and working with government agencies to co-develop datarich
public health tools.
Who are we looking for?
Work Package 5 (WP5) is HD4's government and strategic partnerships work package. It exists to build and
sustain trusted relationships with the ministries, statutory boards, and agencies that hold the geospatial,
planning, and infrastructure data HD4's research depends on - and to translate HD4's research findings back into
forms that are directly useful for policy and strategic planning.
HD4 is looking for a Strategic Partnerships Lead to act as the programme's principal liaison with the Singapore
public sector for WP5. This is a senior, relationship-led role for someone who has served inside government and
understands how ministries and statutory boards operate, think, and make decisions - particularly agencies
involved in infrastructure, land use, and geospatial data (e.g. planning, transport, land administration, housing,
environment and Smart Nation / GovTech-related functions).
The successful candidate will work at the interface between government and research: opening doors to data
and problem statements, framing HD4's multidisciplinary research (spanning geospatial science, urban planning,
and public health) in terms that resonate with policymakers, and making sure research outputs land as
something agencies can actually use in evidence-based policymaking, strategic planning, and city-design
decisions that improve population health.
Key Responsibilities:
Government & agency engagement
Strategic liaison: Serve as HD4's primary point of contact for government ministries and statutory
boards engaged in WP5, building and maintaining senior-level relationships across relevant agencies.
Data access & partnerships: Work with agency counterparts to identify, negotiate, and facilitate access
to geospatial and related administrative datasets needed for HD4 research, navigating data-sharing
agreements, governance, and security requirements.
Problem-statement development: Engage agencies to surface real policy and planning problem
statements, and help shape these into well-defined, researchable questions that HD4's
multidisciplinary teams can act on.
Co-creation of research: Convene researchers and government stakeholders together to co-design
research questions, study designs, and pilots that are both scientifically rigorous and policy-relevant.
Strategic communications & knowledge translation
Strategic communications: Develop and drive HD4's communications strategy toward government
audiences - briefings, position papers, dashboards, and presentations that make complex,
multidisciplinary research (geospatial, planning, health) accessible to non-technical policymakers.
Evidence-to-policy translation: Translate HD4 research findings into actionable recommendations for
evidence-based policy, strategic planning, and city-design decisions aimed at improving population
health outcomes.
Decision-maker engagement: Prepare senior HD4 investigators and agency leadership for joint
briefings, working committees, and inter-agency forums; represent HD4 at relevant government
platforms and working groups.
Programme support
Internal bridging: Act as an internal “translator” between HD4 researchers and government partners -
helping researchers understand agency priorities, constraints, and timelines, and helping agencies
understand what research can (and cannot) deliver.
Stakeholder mapping & pipeline: Maintain a live map of government stakeholders, data-sharing status,
and collaboration opportunities across WP5, and report progress to HD4 leadership.
Multidisciplinary collaboration: Work comfortably alongside researchers, epidemiologists, urban
planners, data scientists, and public health colleagues, given the multidisciplinary nature of the HD4
programme.
What education, experience & skills do you have?
Education
Bachelor's degree required; a Master's degree is preferred - relevant fields include public policy, urban
planning, geography/geospatial science, public administration, engineering, public health, or a related
discipline.
Formal training or a track record in public policy or public administration (e.g. an MPA/MPP, or
equivalent Singapore Public Service leadership training) is an advantage.
No specific health/medical qualification is required - the emphasis is on the ability to work fluently
across disciplines, not on holding expertise in all of them.
Experience
Around 10-15 years of professional experience, including a substantial track record within the
Singapore Public Service at Senior Manager / Assistant Director level or equivalent (or comparable
seniority in a statutory board).
Cross-agency exposure: A career path that has rotated through, or included secondments/postings to,
ministries or statutory boards involved in infrastructure, land use, urban planning, or geospatial data -
example URA, SLA, HDB, LTA, JTC, PUB, NParks, MND, MSE, GovTech/SNDGO (OneMap and related
geospatial platforms), or similar.
Direct experience working with, or governing, geospatial or administrative datasets - understands datasharing
frameworks, data governance, and the practical realities of getting datasets released for
research or cross-agency use.
Experience engaging with, presenting to, or supporting senior government decision-makers (Directorlevel
and above), including preparing briefing papers, position papers, or Cabinet/inter-agency
committee materials.
Some exposure to, or comfort working alongside, the health or research sector is a strong advantage -
example prior collaboration with MOH, healthcare institutions, research institutes, or universities.
Experience managing multi-stakeholder projects or partnerships involving both public-sector agencies
and external partners (academia, industry or non-profits).
Track record of developing strategic communications materials (briefs, dashboards, reports) aimed at
senior non-technical audiences.
Skills
Stakeholder management: Proven ability to build and sustain trust-based relationships with senior
officials across multiple agencies simultaneously.
Strategic communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to produce clear,
persuasive briefing materials and to present confidently to senior audiences.
Negotiation & facilitation: Skilled at facilitating data-sharing discussions, aligning differing agency
priorities, and brokering agreement between parties with different incentives.
Data literacy: Comfortable discussing geospatial and administrative data at a conceptual level - does
not need to build the analysis, but must understand data-sharing mechanics, common data
formats/platforms (e.g. GIS, OneMap) and governance issues well enough to broker access.
Policy fluency: Understands how evidence feeds into Singapore public policy and strategic planning
processes, and how to position research findings to be actionable within those processes.
Project & programme management: Able to manage multiple concurrent agency relationships and
workstreams, track progress, and report clearly to programme leadership.
Cross-disciplinary collaboration: Comfortable working with researchers, epidemiologists and data
scientists as genuine thought partners, not just as a communications conduit.
(Desirable) Existing personal network across infrastructure, planning and geospatial agencies in
Singapore.
(Desirable) Prior involvement in a research collaboration, sandbox, living-lab or public-private
partnership initiative.
(Desirable) Familiarity with Singapore's Smart Nation initiatives and geospatial data platforms (e.g.
OneMap, national GIS infrastructure).
(Desirable) Experience with, or exposure to, health-in-all-policies, urban health or healthy-city design
concepts.

Title: Strategy & Programmes Lead, Rice Funder Collaborative (RFC) Secretariat
Description:
About Rice Funder Collaborative
The Rice Funder Collaborative (RFC) is a new, Asia-led philanthropic collaborative that aims to mobilise coordinated capital to transform rice farming systems, reducing emissions, building farmer resilience, and improving the livelihoods of millions of smallholder farmers across Asia. By 2030, the RFC aims to mobilise around US$30 million in philanthropic capital and catalyse a further ~US$100 million in aligned public and development finance.
The RFC initiative is hosted at the Asia Community Foundation (ACF) and the Secretariat team is led by Asia Philanthropy Circle (APC).
Asia Philanthropy Circle (APC) is a leading platform that mobilises Asia-focused philanthropists to deepen their practice of philanthropy and address systemic challenges collaboratively, through shared learning, peer exchange and joint action across the region.
Asia Community Foundation (ACF) is APC’s sister organisation, providing the infrastructure that makes collaborative action possible, including regranting, fiscal hosting, shared infrastructure and back-office support, so that philanthropists, funders and impact initiatives can focus on the work itself rather than the operational load.
For more details on RFC, you can find the overview document by visiting
https://tinyurl.com/yc8zd492
Role Overview
This is a full-time role on a 2-year contract (with the opportunity for renewal based on performance and regulatory approvals) with a preference for candidates living in and/or able to work in Singapore.
Reporting to the Interim Secretariat Director, and accountable to the RFC Steering Committee, the Strategy & Programmes Lead owns the RFC’s programmatic strategy and is responsible for its grantmaking. This role shapes the RFC’s shared vision into a coherent, fundable portfolio: developing and refining the strategy and theory of change, building and curating a high-quality pipeline, designing and overseeing grants across both aligned and pooled capital, and managing the portfolio for impact and learning.
The role leads a team of up to two Programme Officers and Programme Associate(s), oversees the Communications & Knowledge function on the programmatic and evidence side, and works closely as a peer with the Partnerships & Community Lead, who leads funder relations, the Community of Practice, and donor cultivation.
Key Responsibilities
1. Strategy and Theory of Change
Develop, operationalise, and continually refine the RFC’s overarching strategy, theory of change, and three-year implementation roadmap, validated with founding members.
Translate the four impact priorities and four pathways for change into clear grantmaking theses, funding priorities, and sequencing across geographies.
Establish the initial prioritisation framework for pooled fund grantmaking, adapting the mix to the readiness, opportunities, and needs of different countries.
2. Pipeline and Grantmaking
Build and maintain a high-quality, curated pipeline of investment-ready opportunities aligned with the strategy, including sourcing internally and incorporating funder-vetted opportunities, with a near-term target of approximately ten high-potential opportunities in the first year
Lead landscape scans and opportunity assessments, identifying priority gaps and areas for philanthropic collaboration
Design and oversee grantmaking strategies, processes, and guidelines for both aligned and pooled capital, and lead due diligence in coordination with ACF’s grant administration
Develop grant recommendations and present them, with clear rationale and evidence, to the Grants/Investment Committee
Ensure grantee support is effective, equitable, and aligned with the Collaborative’s broader goals
3. Pooled Fund and Portfolio Management
Programme the pooled fund’s investments in line with the shared strategy, ensuring grantmaking is informed by, and contributes to, the Secretariat’s learning and pipeline development
Manage the overall portfolio for impact: responsible for outcome and impact frameworks, tracking portfolio-level results, and conducting periodic reviews to shift capital towards the strongest-performing approaches
Build the monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) framework, with clear indicators for methane reduction, farmer outcomes, and ecosystem strengthening

Over the years, Hong Leong Asia (HLA) has grown into an established Asian multinational with operations across Singapore, Malaysia and China. 1. Sustainability Reporting & ESG Data Management
Support the preparation of the Group's annual Sustainability Report and sustainability disclosures in accordance with applicable reporting requirements and frameworks, including SGX sustainability reporting requirements, GRI Standards and other relevant sustainability disclosure standards.
Coordinate with reporting business units across Singapore, Malaysia and China to collect sustainability and ESG data, supporting information and explanations required for Group reporting.
Compile, consolidate and maintain ESG datasets covering areas including energy, fuel consumption, carbon emissions, waste and circularity, health and safety, people and community as well as supply chain indicators.

Assist in strengthening internal ESG data collection processes, definitions, controls and documentation across reporting business units.
Maintain appropriate audit trails and supporting documentation in preparation for internal review and external assurance.
Support external assurance exercises and respond to information requests from auditors, consultants and other relevant parties.
Identify recurring data gaps and recommend improvements to reporting processes and controls.
3. Sustainability Performance Monitoring
Maintain database of progress against the Group's sustainability targets and key performance indicators.
Assist in preparing quarterly sustainability performance reports and dashboards for Management and the Board Sustainability Committee and/or Board-level reporting.
Analyse ESG performance trends and highlight significant movements, gaps or areas requiring further explanation from business units.
Support the development of clearer performance indicators and reporting dashboards to improve management visibility of sustainability performance.

Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and comfortable working with large datasets from multiple business units.

Title: Technical Program Manager III, Amazon Leo Partner Services (ALPS)
Description:
DESCRIPTION
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable broadband connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From households to small businesses, schools, hospitals, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve communities and organizations operating in places without dependable internet access. With 38 signed distribution partners globally and service launch approaching, now is an exciting time to join a team that is actively shaping how satellite broadband reaches the world.
As a Technical Program Manager on the Amazon Leo Partner Services team, you will own and drive complex, externally facing technical integration programs with Amazon Leo's global distribution partners, including some of the largest internet service providers in the world. You will serve as the primary program leader responsible for ensuring partners successfully integrate, validate, and launch satellite internet service in their contracted territories and channels. This role sits at the center of partner-facing execution and internal product coordination, spanning API onboarding, BSS/OSS integration, network readiness, operational enablement, and launch milestones. You will work cross-functionally with Amazon Leo engineering, product, solutions architecture, and operations teams to ensure partner-facing deliverables are defined, prioritized, and delivered on time.
This position may require access to export-controlled information (ECI) subject to EAR and ITAR. Final employment decision is contingent upon satisfactory completion of export control screenings and obtaining any necessary export licenses or approvals, based on nationality, citizenship, and other factors considered by applicable export control regulations.
Key job responsibilities
- Own end-to-end partner technical integration programs from discovery through launch readiness, defining integration scope, success criteria, milestones, and deliverables across partner and Amazon Leo teams while identifying risks, dependencies, and critical path items early to drive mitigation plans.
- Lead recurring program reviews, executive checkpoints, and milestone tracking sessions with strategic distribution partners, translating partner integration requirements into clear internal execution plans and managing blockers through timely escalation.
- Coordinate delivery across multiple internal workstreams — including API releases, backend services, hardware readiness, and operational tooling — partnering with Product, Engineering, Solutions Architects, and Operations teams to align roadmaps with partner launch commitments.
- Develop and maintain standardized program artifacts such as integration plans, dependency maps, and executive status reporting, and implement repeatable frameworks for global partner onboarding and launch readiness.
- Analyze program data, track integration maturity metrics, and report launch risk to senior leadership, using insights to drive continuous improvement of the ALPS launch model and influence prioritization of partner-critical capabilities.
A day in the life
You will operate in a regional context, supporting distribution partners across your assigned region in coordination with central ALPS teammates and other regional Technical Program Managers. Your day may include leading a partner integration review in the morning, aligning with engineering on API readiness in the afternoon, and preparing an executive launch risk update for leadership. Beyond your regional portfolio, you will also own at least one global-scope initiative aimed at improving the partner experience across all ALPS regions, giving you visibility and impact well beyond your immediate territory.
About the team
The Amazon Leo Partner Services (ALPS) team is responsible for the onboarding, integration, and enablement of Amazon Leo's distribution partners worldwide. We work with telecom operators and regional service providers to deliver satellite internet service in inclusive regulatory and operational environments. With a rapidly growing partner network and service launch on the horizon, the team is scaling quickly to meet demand from some of the largest internet service providers in the world.
Our mission is to make Amazon Leo partnerships predictable, scalable, and launch-ready through technical rigor and disciplined program execution. Every team member owns a regional partner portfolio while also driving at least one global project that raises the bar on the partner experience across all markets. This combination of regional depth and global reach means you will build expertise in local market dynamics while shaping how ALPS operates at scale.

- 3+ years of software development experience
- 5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

Role Overview:
As a Key Account Management Specialist within the Africa Trade division, you play a pivotal role in driving the growth and expansion of Africa Trade activities by identifying strategic business opportunities, fostering and developing strong relationships with key customers.
Key Responsibilities:
Account Management
Lead the development of the yearly target per account, in line with the budget and customer rating, and the cargo mix strategy with the support of Heads of Lines, Senior Line Manager, Commercial Line Managers, Head Office, Regional Offices and Sales Agency.
Accountable to retain existing customers and enhance customer portfolio by anticipating market trends, customer expectations and new requirements.
Responsible to drive the development of the Lines Key Account team to be recognized as entry point for account performance monitoring, pricing, and customer related issue and/or new request.
Coordination and collecting information regarding the Group’s best practises, market information, and customer care support.
Customer Performance Monitoring
Attend QBRs coordinated by Sales / KAMs.
Provide regular reporting and communication to the Line Management such as customer performance follow up, pricing policy and allocation (CSA) adjustment, customer meeting requests.
Present weekly market insights report highlighting competitor / customer analysis and emerging trends for relevant stakeholders.
Tender Management
Develop and implement a comprehensive tender management process covering all stages from initial offer through nomination to final performance by 31 March 2027.

Title: Transaction Banking - Payments & Liquidity Sales (Director) - SG
Description:
Discover your future at Citi
Working at Citi is far more than just a job. A career with us means joining a team of approximately 219,000 dedicated people from around the globe. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact.
Job Overview
Citi Services provides global solutions that help corporations, financial institutions, public sector, and commercial clients optimize operations and drive their business forward. Through our five business lines – Liquidity Management Services, Payments, Trade & Working Capital Solutions, Investor Services and Issuer Services - we provide cash management, payments/receivables solutions, working capital solutions, post-trade securities services and issuer services across Citi’s global network.
The Payment & Liquidity Sales (Director) is a senior regional product sales role that deals with complex cash management requirements for the most demanding and sophisticated multi-national corporate clients operating across Asia Pacific region. This role is expected to develop and grow client relationships by understanding client needs and delivering solutions across the full range of cash management products and services that Citi can offer and will be a combination of event driven sales e.g. responding to large scale and/or complex regional tenders in the form of RFIs (Request for information), RFPs (Request for Proposals) and proactive sales e.g. targeted proactive engagement for select prospective clients or key defend clients for the firm. The key objective of the role is to increase penetration of the Bank’s TTS (Treasury & Trade Solutions) services within the existing regional client base as well as acquiring new clients for the Bank across Corporate Banking (CB) / Global Network Banking (GNB) client segments and is a driver in generating revenue through new TTS deals.
Responsibilities:
Plays a leading role in setting and executing overall deal strategy for each deal, which includes solution structuring, pricing strategy and negotiation, marketing/pitching approach
Responsible for coordinating internal deal processes e.g. obtaining internal approvals / sign-off, closing, handover to implementation
The individual is accountable for delivering against client (i.e. deal wins) and acts as a center of expertise / excellence in cash management solutioning to support focused regional client opportunities
Supports the firm’s effort in building profitable, long-term client relationships, orchestrating delivery of superior products and services to corporate clients adding value to their treasury processes
Works with external stakeholders to fully understand and ensure that customers’ needs / asks are addressed through our responses and marketing materials
Works with key deal team stakeholders for the preparation of responses to global/regional tenders e.g. . Proposal Unit, Client Coverage Team, Product Teams, Country Teams etc. to develop and deliver end-to-end high quality and customized Request for Proposal (RFP) & Request for Information (RFI) responses to best position Citi to win the mandate
For proactive engagements, the individual will work with the deal team to develop and deliver presentation and marketing collateral for effective selling and gaining client’s mind share
Be familiar with TTS positioning and messages from marketing materials and effectively incorporate into all client communication (written / verbal)
Champions ‘best practices’ for effective selling
Applies in-depth technical product & sales skills with client diagnostic and origination skills to design complex multi-product solutions, for Corporate, Public Sector and Financials Institutions clients
Keep abreast of customer needs & market trends through continuous interaction with clients, coverage & product
Evaluates competitive landscape and appropriately assess risk/reward of transactions when making business decisions
Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behavior, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency
Provides input / feedback for new product development and innovation
Be a leading example and provide active guidance to more junior members of the team
Qualifications/Experience:
Bachelor’s/University degree or equivalent experience
Master’s degree is Good To Have
15+ years of banking experience, with at least 10+ years of relevant transaction banking sales experience
Possess the curiosity to learn as well as the enthusiasm and tenacity to deal with challenges, often within a time constrained environment
Should be an accomplished Product, Sales, and Customer orientated person with ability to marry client needs and Citi’s product capabilities in order to develop customized solutioning to address client requirements
Has good knowledge of cash management products and how to deal with challenges faced by corporate treasuries
Proficient in MS Excel, MS Power Point, MS Word desirable

Title: Transactions Manager
Description:
Company overview
P.T. Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk, is a leading Indonesian bank providing comprehensive corporate banking solutions to support business growth and financial needs. The Global Syndication Desk (GSD) is responsible for originating, structuring, syndicating, and distributing loan transactions across BNI’s international network. The role supports business growth by enhancing client relationships, optimizing loan portfolio distribution, improving balance sheet management, and providing market intelligence and advisory services to Management and Credit Committees.
The position works closely with Overseas Branches (KLN), Head Office, borrowers, investors, and financial institutions to execute syndicated loan transactions and support strategic business initiatives.
Key Responsibilities
1. Loan Origination & Lead Arranger Activities
Support Overseas Branches (KLN) in identifying and originating syndicated loan opportunities.
Develop target client lists aligned with the Bank’s risk appetite and business strategy.
Prepare marketing proposals, financing presentations, and pitchbooks to secure financing mandates.
Conduct market analysis and recommend optimal loan pricing based on comparable transactions and prevailing market conditions.
Structure loan facilities and prepare term sheets that meet both client requirements and the Bank’s risk and return objectives.
Support internal credit approval processes through preparation of credit papers and presentations.
Assist in transaction execution, including documentation review, negotiations with borrowers, and syndication activities.
Build and maintain relationships with corporate clients, financial institutions, and key market participants.
2. Syndicated Loan Participation & Credit Support
Evaluate opportunities to participate in syndicated loan transactions arranged by other financial institutions.
Serve as a key liaison between Mandated Lead Arrangers (MLABs) and BNI’s overseas network.
Support negotiations with external arrangers to achieve favorable pricing and allocation terms.
Conduct financial and credit assessments of transactions and borrowers.
Prepare transaction analyses and recommendations for Management and Credit Committees.
Provide independent market views regarding deal structure, pricing, syndication progress, and risk considerations.
3. Global Loan Distribution & Portfolio Management
Lead the distribution of BNI-originated syndicated loans to financial institutions outside Indonesia.
Support bookrunning and syndication efforts across Corporate Banking, Financial Institutions, Non-Bank Financial Institutions, and Overseas Branch portfolios.
Develop and maintain relationships with regional and international investor banks.
Identify distribution opportunities to optimize portfolio management and balance sheet utilization.
Facilitate loan sell-down activities to improve capital efficiency and enhance return on equity (ROE).
Provide origination ideas that align with market demand and investor appetite.
4. Market Advisory & Intelligence
Monitor developments in the syndicated loan market and provide regular market updates.
Analyze sector trends, banking liquidity, investor appetite, pricing benchmarks, and comparable transactions.
Prepare investor call reports and market intelligence updates for senior management.
Advise business units, management, and Credit Committees on market conditions, transaction structures, pricing strategy, and syndication feasibility.
Contribute to strategic decision-making by providing insights into market trends and transaction opportunities.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s Degree in Finance, Banking, Economics, Business Administration, Accounting, or a related discipline.
Professional qualifications such as CFA, FRM, ACAMS, or other relevant banking and finance certifications will be an advantage.
Strong knowledge of syndicated lending, corporate banking, structured finance, credit analysis, and loan documentation.
Good understanding of financial markets, credit risk assessment, and portfolio management.
Strong financial modeling and financial statement analysis skills.
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

Title: Vice President, Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement
Description:
Vice President, Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement
Global | Permanent or 12-month rotational assignment
About Citco
Citco is a global leader in fund services, corporate governance and related asset services with staff across 50 office locations worldwide. With more than $1.8 trillion in assets under administration, we deliver end-to-end solutions and exceptional service to meet our clients’ needs.
For more information about Citco, please visit www.citco.com
About the Team & Business Line
Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.
Strategic Operations is a dedicated function within Private Assets. It brings transformation delivery, project execution, business analysis, operational initiatives and implementation support into one team, reducing the delivery burden on BAU Operations and maintaining ownership from design through adoption.
The group will be split across three distinct focus areas, aligned under two individual leaders:
Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions: led by the Operating Model & Product leader, this area will define how services should run end to end, shape scalable products and solutions, support complex client implementations, and ensure client commitments are operationally deliverable.
Data, Reporting & Platform Enablement: led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will define Operations requirements for data, reporting and platforms, strengthen data quality and lineage, and carry solutions through testing, deployment and adoption.
Digital Workflow, Automation & AI: also led by the Technology, Data & Delivery leader, this area will identify and deliver workflow, automation and AI opportunities, establish appropriate controls, and measure whether the expected benefits are realised.
The group works in close partnership with Operations, the Transformation Office, IT, Tactical Operations and Marquee Client teams. Roles may be permanent or approximately 12-month rotational assignments anchored in strategic locations. Rotational colleagues will join from the business, help shape and deliver change, and return to the line with broader project experience.
Your Role
You will deliver data, reporting and platform change from requirement definition through testing to deployment and adoption.
Define and document Operations’ data and reporting requirements, and agree them with IT and the Transformation Office.
Support platform change through build, and own the Operations-side test strategy including UAT and defect resolution.
Build the data and reporting outputs needed to evidence a problem and measure the benefit of a change.
Investigate and resolve data quality issues, tracing them to source rather than correcting downstream.
Support implementation of platform change across fund structures, new client setups and transitions.
Work with the Operating Model, Product & Client Solutions and Digital Workflow, Automation & AI focus areas where delivery depends on data or reporting capability.
Work directly with Operations teams to make sure change is understood, trained out and genuinely adopted.
Produce project documentation, status reporting and ad hoc analysis as required.
About You
You have 8+ years’ experience in private assets accounting or operations, with hands-on exposure to data, reporting or platform work.
Hands-on experience of reporting build, data analysis, system implementation or project delivery.
Strong technical knowledge of private assets processes and the data that underpins them.
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interrogate large data sets and evidence a recommendation.
Project management skills with attention to detail and a proven ability to multi-task.
Confident engaging both operational teams and technology partners.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Advanced computer skills (Microsoft Excel); familiarity with reporting, workflow or automation tooling an advantage.
Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance or Economics; professional accounting designation is preferred.
What We Expect of the Strategic Operations Team
Regardless of role or focus area, everyone in Strategic Operations is expected to demonstrate the following:
Deep technical and operational knowledge — genuine depth in how our processes, data and platforms actually work — the detail that only comes from having run the work.
Curiosity — the instinct to ask why a process looks the way it does, to challenge the answer, and to keep asking whether there is a better way.
A transformational mindset — comfortable redesigning end to end rather than patching, and prepared to see change through past go-live to the point where it is genuinely adopted.
Ownership through to adoption — accountability does not end at delivery; success is measured by whether the change sticks in the business.
Commercial and client awareness — an understanding of what we can genuinely run, so that what we commit to a client is deliverable.
Global mindset — working across regions, jurisdictions and time zones, and designing solutions that scale beyond a single desk, client or location.
Ambition to shape Citco’s future — an appetite to help build the operating model we will run for years, and to be measured on whether it works.
Our Benefits
Your well-being is of paramount importance to us, and central to our success. We provide a range of benefits, training and education support, and flexible working arrangements to help you achieve success in your career while balancing personal needs. Ask us about specific benefits in your location.
We embrace diversity, prioritizing the hiring of people from diverse backgrounds. Our inclusive culture is a source of pride and strength, fostering innovation and mutual respect.
Citco welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

Company: CLIFFORD CAPITAL MANAGEMENT SERVICES PTE. LTD.
Title: Vice President, Investments - Asset Management
Description:
Position Overview:
Clifford Capital Asset Management (“CCAM”) is a new line of business that was established in December 2024. CCAM is regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (the “MAS”) and holds a Capital Market Service License to conduct fund management activities for accredited and institutional investors. CCAM will focus on launching mandates as well as collective investment schemes. CCAM products are expected to invest in range of credit instruments including but not limited to senior credit, subordinated debt/high yield as well as hybrid instruments representing debt financing.
Primary Responsibilities:
Work closely with origination, corporate coverage and investor coverage teams to source, assess and execute infrastructure credit investment opportunities across CCAM-managed pools of capital
Lead credit due diligence, investment analysis, financial modelling, structuring assessment and risk evaluation for primary and secondary market opportunities
Build and maintain relationships with banks, sponsors, intermediaries, investors and other market participants to strengthen CCAM’s market presence and access to investment opportunities
Prepare and present investment recommendations, credit papers and portfolio updates to CCAM’s Investment Committee, senior management and relevant governance forums
Drive the internal credit application and approval process, coordinating inputs from origination, risk, legal, operations and other relevant stakeholders
Undertake upfront and ongoing relative value analysis, portfolio monitoring, asset performance review and portfolio management activities across relevant mandates and funds
Support investor marketing, fundraising and due diligence processes by providing investment insights, portfolio information and market perspectives as required
Act as deal captain for selected transactions, providing end-to-end transaction leadership and, over time, supervising and mentoring junior investment team members
Professional Experience / Qualifications:
At least 8 years of relevant experience in infrastructure credit, private credit, project finance, leveraged finance, structured finance, asset management or a related investment role within a financial institution or investment platform
Strong academic background, with demonstrated investment judgement and experience in credit analysis, investment structuring, financial modelling and investment committee processes
Strong understanding of infrastructure, private credit and APAC markets; experience across global infrastructure debt markets or cross-border transactions would be advantageous
Proven ability to manage multiple transactions and portfolio priorities independently, with strong execution discipline, commercial judgement and attention to detail
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the maturity and credibility to engage senior management, investment committees, investors, counterparties and external advisers
Business-level Japanese language skills are advantageous for engaging with Japanese investors and counterparties
Headquartered in Singapore and established in 2012, Clifford Capital is an infrastructure credit financing platform for real assets globally across the debt capital structure. The Group is increasingly pivoting towards areas such as clean energy, energy transition, social and digital infrastructure, electrification, and maritime decarbonisation to address the challenges posed by environmental, social and governance issues globally, and in particular within the Asia Pacific region. Its ambition is to deliver innovative financing solutions that positively influence sustainability and deliver commercial returns for its shareholders.
Clifford Capital aims to build a globally competitive alternative asset management and financing platform closely aligned to Singapore’s objectives of creating a centre of excellence in financial markets focused on sustainability and green finance.
Clifford Capital’s shareholders comprise Temasek Holdings, Prudential Assurance Company Singapore, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Standard Chartered Bank, DBS Bank, John Hancock Life Insurance Company (Manulife), and the Asian Development Bank.

Title: VP, Corporate Partnerships
Description:
About Us
Wavemaker is Southeast Asia’s leading early-stage venture capital firm investing in enterprise and deep tech companies that offer innovative solutions and add significant value. Over the last 13 years, we have invested in over 200 companies and our thesis has remained the same:
We invest in thoughtful founders who have built an internal conviction through experience and reflection and identified a huge opportunity because they see things differently from most other people.
We invest in scalable, capital-efficient, sustainable businesses that aim to create significant value by solving meaningful problems 10x better than existing options.
Today, we’re a team of 40+ incredibly driven and passionate people in the region, and we are looking for a VP, Corporate Partnerships to join our team.
What You'll Do
This role sits at the intersection of Wavemaker, our portfolio startups, and ecosystem partners — generating capital for Wavemaker and its portfolio companies, and connecting startups and corporates to accelerate outcomes for both.
Fundraising
- Generate top-of-funnel capital sources for Wavemaker across all fund strategies
- Generate top-of-funnel capital sources for managed portfolio companies, from both financial and strategic investors
- Surface and advance fundraising conversations as a natural extension of the broader relationship-building work
Partnerships & Portfolio Value Creation
- Develop a deep understanding of Wavemaker's portfolio companies, including growth drivers, strategic gaps, and potential exit pathways
- Identify and map corporate ecosystem partners that can accelerate portfolio traction, fundraising, and exit
- Facilitate strategic introductions between portfolio companies and corporates that may become customers, lenders, co-investors, and acquirers
Ecosystem Mapping and Development
- Build and maintain a structured map of corporate ecosystem players relevant to Wavemaker's investment themes and portfolio needs
- Develop and nurture executive-level relationships with key decision-makers across corporate partners
Scaled Exits Support
- Support the scaled-exits effort in older funds
- Apply financial literacy to assess asset value and viable exit routes for these positions
Project Management
- Partner closely with the General Partner to drive execution across active partnership, fundraising, and exit workstreams
- Bring structure and rigor to a fast-moving, relationship-heavy pipeline, ensuring nothing valuable is lost between an introduction and its outcome
Who You Are
- You have 8+ years of experience in partnerships, business development, venture capital, investment banking, consulting/corporate strategy, or a related ecosystem-facing role.
- You are a hunter: you have a track record of generating and closing capital relationships — from your own network, from cold outreach, or through structured fundraising processes — not just facilitating warm introductions.
- You have deep financial literacy, including comfort assessing and structuring the liquidation of assets from older fund vintages (scaled exits).
- You have been deeply embedded across founders, operators, and corporates, with a track record as a trusted connector in the ecosystem.
- You have a strong understanding of and curiosity towards business models and commercial drivers, in order to pitch opportunities credibly (both to startups and corporates).
- You are commercially minded, with a strong instinct for identifying and activating opportunities that create tangible outcomes.
- You are highly adaptable and can operate across multiple priorities and evolving scope with ownership and accountability.
- You are a strong communicator with executive presence and the ability to engage senior stakeholders effectively.
- You are relationship-driven and genuinely motivated to help founders and corporate partners succeed.

Title: VP, International Desk Manager
Description:
In International Wealth and Premier Banking, we serve 41 million customers globally, including 6.7 million who are international, from retail customers to ultra high net worth individuals and their families. We help our customers to take care of their day-to-day finances and to manage, protect and grow their wealth. Our international network and breadth of expertise enable us to deliver on HSBC’s purpose of opening up a world of opportunity by providing our customers with borderless banking and world-class wealth management through best-in-class, mobile-first capabilities and exceptional people. Our key areas of operations include Retail Banking and Wealth Management, Asset Management, Global Private Banking, Insurance, and Chief Operating Office.
We are currently seeking a high calibre professional to join our team as a VP, International Desk Manager
In this role you will:
Responsible for working with corridor partners to maximize inbound referral business through the International Banking Centre, Digital remote journeys, and Business Development Managers. For North Asia, this would include China, Taiwan and Hong Kong amongst others
Enable cross functional business referrals from Singapore to key corridor markets to fulfill multi-corridor needs for New to bank and New to Group customers
Work towards improving the fund flow from corridor partners to HSBC Singapore and from HSBC Singapore to other markets. Look at increasing the capture rate in both directions
Acquire Lead Generators (LG) in Singapore and look at building upon the cross-border LG opportunities in the markets that are enabled. In the absence of LG approvals, look at partnerships that can be developed
Working with Market Heads of their respective corridors to work towards RM referrals and self sourcing and build a sustainable pipeline for acquisition
Work with Propositions on events that can be done in Singapore and overseas to build acquisition opportunities. To look at communication material that could be developed
Run collaborative initiatives in support of SG plans to become an international wealth hub.
Design and enable rapid solutions for growth in response to market changes by resolving channel challenges and investigating their complaints or feedbacks with a view to recover service
To be successful you will need:
Strong knowledge of the retail banking landscape, and a good understanding of business functions in the context of offshore and international banking
Experience in acquisition or business development strategy, prior experience and deep knowledge of working with corridors is preferred
Clear and effective communication skills, particularly in non-face to face engagement
Strong interpersonal and relationship management skills, with sensitivity towards various cultural backgrounds
Efficient time management and project management skills, and ability to manage a diverse range of tasks under pressure
Drive New to Bank acquisition across various sources and continuously develop new acquisition channels and alliances
You’ll achieve more at HSBC.
HSBC is committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and opportunities to grow within an inclusive and diverse environment. Champion the company's culture and spearhead initiatives that strengthen it.

Sharp analytical ability, with confidence working with data and building financial models.
Outstanding written and spoken communication, including producing clear presentations and memos, and working effectively with colleagues at all levels.
Highly organised and self-directed, yet flexible when priorities shift, and energised by a fast-moving environment.

Title: Water Infrastructure Strategy Director
Description:
Want to be a part of Asia Pacific & Middle East's (APME) largest, most innovative, and rapidly growing data centre company?
AirTrunk is a technology company with a powerful purpose - to scale and sustain the relentless growth of the region’s digital future. We do this by continuously redefining and delivering hyperscale data centres that meet the needs of our customers - the world’s most transformational companies. And we’re doing so sustainably, for today and tomorrow.
Having opened Australia’s first and largest hyperscale data centres in 2017, we set our eyes on rapid expansion and now operate a platform of hyperscale data centres across the APME region. With backing from our investors, including Blackstone, this is just the beginning…
Come join the A-Team at AirTrunk, where the cloud meets the ground.
A Snapshot
At AirTrunk, we’ve all come together to deliver Data Centres that meet and grow with the needs of our large cloud, content and enterprise customers.
Water management is a key pillar of our sustainability commitments. We design and operate our Data Centers to source water responsibly, reduce reliance on potable water where appropriate, limit usage in water-stressed areas and improve water productivity to support energy, carbon and community outcomes. Through strong water stewardship, we seek to balance business growth with catchment-level resilience, responsible resource use and measurable sustainability impact.
In this leadership role, you will define and lead AirTrunk’s water strategy across the portfolio, managing a team of managers to deliver sustainable, commercially robust and operationally resilient water outcomes.
You will make your mark in a number of ways:
Set and own the regional water strategy for Data Center sites, ensuring scalable, sustainable and resilient water supply solutions across existing and future markets.
Lead, coach and develop a team of managers responsible for utility connections, upgrades, alternative supply options, water infrastructure delivery and site-level optimisation.
Oversee portfolio-wide assessment of water stress, supply risk and regulatory conditions, translating insights into long-term strategic plans and investment priorities.
Build executive-level partnerships with utilities, authorities, customers and solution providers to unlock recycled, industrial and alternative water sourcing opportunities.
Define the roadmap to water positivity, including on-site and off-site water solutions, reuse strategies, discharge optimisation and measurable sustainability outcomes.
Develop and implement a water stewardship framework that aligns site-level water decisions with regional sustainability objectives, local catchment conditions, stakeholder expectations and long-term operational resilience.
Establish governance, performance metrics and reporting cadence for water usage, metering, efficiency, risk management and delivery performance across the portfolio.
Influence design, site selection, development, commercial and operations decisions to ensure water strategy is embedded into major business and customer commitments.
Your Day to Day
Lead a team of managers, setting priorities, removing barriers, allocating resources and ensuring consistent delivery across markets and projects.
Represent AirTrunk with senior utility, government, customer and strategic partner stakeholders to shape water supply, infrastructure and sustainability outcomes.
Provide executive oversight of water projects, including supply connections and upgrades, infrastructure investments, commercial contracts, risk mitigation and delivery milestones.
Partner with customers at senior levels to understand water requirements, influence commitments and ensure AirTrunk’s water strategy supports customer growth and sustainability expectations.
Translate water sustainability strategy into practical implementation plans, including recycled water adoption, water reuse, efficiency initiatives, catchment partnerships, performance targets and transparent reporting.
Work with Design, Site Selection, Development, Commercial and Operations leaders to align water decisions with business strategy, technical requirements and long-term operating performance.
Prepare and present executive-level recommendations, investment papers, governance updates and performance reports for senior leadership forums.
Establish operating rhythms for the team, including portfolio reviews, cross-functional escalation, performance tracking and continuous improvement of water strategy delivery.
Requirements
Minimally 10 years of relevant experience e.g. water utilities, water project development and delivery, water sustainability water infrastructure services, water consulting, water treatment and recycled water, etc.
Strong understanding of the water supply landscape in several of our Asia-Pacific and Japan markets (including Singapore, Malaysia, Australia, Hong Kong and Japan)
Strong expertise in water supply design principles and various water technologies such as water treatment/recycling/recovery/capture
Relationships and networks in the water industry in the above markets
Strong analytical thinking and comfortable with data analysis and presentation (especially in PowerPoint and Excel)
Provide leadership, mentoring, and technical guidance to the regional team.
Demonstrated experience leading multiple concurrent large-scale projects or programs.
Excellent stakeholder management, communication, negotiation, leadership, and problem-solving skills. Ie. Build and maintain strong working relationships with consultants, contractors, suppliers, customer representatives, and internal stakeholders to ensure successful project delivery.
The AirTrunk Culture
Working at AirTrunk is a once in a lifetime opportunity to fast-track your career and amplify your impact. Whilst you’re helping scale our region’s digital future, we’ll help you Grow@Hyperscale and unleash your full potential.
The pace in which we operate means you’ll feel an electric atmosphere at AirTrunk. We are a team of challengers and collaborative problem solvers who break new ground every day. We do this by living our values, going above and beyond, and being dynamic, transparent, and responsive.
Every AirTrunker brings their own unique background and diverse perspective to find solutions to problems that matter. We make sure you have everything you need to make your mark and thrive in a flexible and safe working environment, where everyone feels welcome. Our benefits empower AirTrunkers to stay positively charged.
Now’s your chance to Grow@Hyperscale.

Perform continuous team’s portfolio analysis to identify potential client leads and opportunities
Detailed, meticulous and precise in identifying opportunities and gaps and ability to craft out quick business strategies to achieve business goals
Working closely with other members of the Wealth Management team, such as investment, insurance, treasury specialists to provide holistic solutions to our onshore banking premier clients

The successful candidate has strong academic qualifications and in depth knowledge in Wealth Management with a proven track record of leading a team
Strong understanding of financial markets and investment products
Strong interpersonal relationship skills to be able to work individually as well as to collaborate with stakeholders to meet overall team’s objectives
Highly driven and possess the ability to succeed within a challenging environment
Outgoing disposition, well-equipped with good communication and interpersonal skills
Down to earth and resilient individual with an entrepreneurial and collaborative mindset who is able to work independently and in a strong team environment
Highly driven to excel and be able to thrive within a challenging environment by effectively recognizing customers' personal banking and wealth management needs

Job Description – Workplace Event Lead (IFM - Singapore)
Summary:
Workplace Event Lead duties and responsibilities include leading a team of Workplace Ambassadors, planning, coordinating, and executing workplace events that enhance client’ss employee engagement, foster client’s company culture, and support client’s organization objectives.
This role requires to work closely with Workplace Experience team (Soft-Service), Engineering team, Senior Facilities Manager and the client, contributing to larger workplace & event experience for all offices. While the role requires someone highly proactive and independent, it also requires strong project management skills, creative vision, and the ability to manage multiple events and stakeholders simultaneously while staying within budget.
Responsibilities:
Team Leadership: This role provides direct supervision and mentorship to event ambassadors. Responsibilities include recruiting, hiring, and onboarding event team members, setting clear performance expectations and delegating responsibilities and empowering team members to make decisions, managing workload distribution to optimize team efficiency, fostering a collaborative and high-performing team culture, and conducting regular team meetings to align on priorities and share knowledge.
Event Program Management: Workplace Event Lead oversees the complete portfolio of workplace events across multiple categories and locations. This encompasses managing large-scale corporate events including town halls, leadership summits, and annual celebrations, awards ceremonies, wellness initiatives and health-focused events and cultural celebrations, department workshops, facilitating team-building activities and support community outreach and corporate events.
Budget Management: Managing substantial event budgets for the client is a core responsibility requiring basic financial acumen and strategic resource allocation. This includes developing annual event budgets, allocating resources across event portfolio based on strategic priorities, negotiating favorable vendor, tracking expenses and identifying cost-saving opportunities while maintaining event quality.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Management: Success requires effective collaboration with multiple departments and stakeholders throughout the client organization. This includes serving as primary liaison between events team and department stakeholders, collaboration with communications team on event messaging and internal communication, working closely Facilities team on space planning and operational support, coordinating with IT on technology infrastructure, audio-visual needs, and virtual platforms, and building relationships with different site stakeholders for multi-location coordination
Crisis Management & Problem Solving: The ability to manage unexpected challenges and maintain composure under pressure. This includes serving as primary point of escalation for event-related issues and emergencies, making real-time decisions to address logistical challenges and vendor failures, implementing contingency plans for unforeseen circumstances, managing stakeholder expectations during crisis situations with professionalism, maintaining calm and providing clear direction to team members during high-pressure situations.
Health & Safety Management: Ensuring all events meet safety standard, this includes developing comprehensive risk assessment frameworks for all event types, ensuring all vendors compliance with health and safety regulations including food handling, coordinating security requirements for high-profile or large-scale events, managing data privacy and information security for event registrations and attendee data and conducting post-event incident reviews and implementing corrective actions.
Event Planning & Strategy: The Workplace Event Lead develops comprehensive event strategies aligned with client organizational goals and company culture. This includes managing annual event calendars, defining event objectives and success metrics, and researching emerging trends in workplace experiences.
Event Execution & Management: Primary responsibility includes end-to-end management of all workplace events, from commencement to post-event evaluation. This encompasses venue selection, vendor management and relationship building, budget tracking, timeline creation and deadline management, and logistics coordination including catering and audio-visual equipment. The role also involves creating event materials such as invitations and signage, while managing event registration and attendance tracking.

Description:

is responsible for planning, implementing, and managing online marketing campaigns to promote a company’s products or services. They leverage digital channels such as social media, email, search engines, and websites to enhance brand awareness, drive traffic, and generate leads or sales.
Key Responsibilities:
Digital Strategy & Campaign Management
Develop and execute digital marketing strategies to achieve business goals.
Plan and manage online advertising campaigns (Google Ads, social media ads, etc.).
Analyze market trends and customer insights to optimize campaigns.
Social Media Marketing
Create and manage content across platforms (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, etc.).
Engage with audiences and monitor social media performance.
Develop influencer partnerships and collaborations.
Search Engine Optimization (SEO) & Search Engine Marketing (SEM)
Optimize website content for search engines to improve rankings.
Conduct keyword research and apply SEO best practices.
Manage PPC (pay-per-click) campaigns to drive traffic and conversions.
Content Marketing
Create and distribute engaging blog posts, videos, emails, and infographics.
Develop email marketing campaigns and newsletters.
Ensure content aligns with brand voice and marketing goals.
Analytics & Performance Tracking

Generate reports on website traffic, conversion rates, and ROI.
Make data-driven decisions to optimize marketing efforts.

Education & Experience:
Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related field.

· Build, lead and develop the brand and marketing function, including capability planning, objective setting, performance management and talent development.
· Work closely with the CEO and senior management to align brand and marketing priorities with Company strategy.
· Partner with product, business development, sales, operations, customer service, compliance, legal, finance and HR teams to deliver integrated initiatives.
· Manage external agencies, consultants, media, creative partners and other vendors where required.
· Establish clear standards, workflows and accountability to ensure high-quality and timely marketing execution.
7. Reputation, Communications & Brand Risk Management
· Oversee corporate brand communications and support reputation management across relevant external channels.
· Develop communication approaches for significant company announcements, partnerships, product developments and industry engagement.
· Work with Legal and Compliance teams to ensure external marketing and communications are accurate, appropriate and aligned with applicable requirements.
· Identify brand and reputation risks and establish appropriate escalation, review and response mechanisms.
· Support senior leaders in external communications and thought leadership where appropriate.
Requirements
· Bachelor's degree or above in Marketing, Communications, Business, Brand Management or a related discipline.
· At least 12 years of progressive experience in brand, marketing or integrated communications, including substantial experience in a senior marketing leadership role.
· Demonstrated experience developing and executing brand and marketing strategy across multiple markets, including brand positioning, integrated campaigns, digital/content marketing and marketing performance.
· Experience in technology, internet, SaaS, digital platforms, e-commerce, fintech or another international digital business is highly preferred.

As a community builder and sector leader, NVPC seeks to craft a compelling narrative and business case for companies to do well, do right and do good. In this role, you will design and implement effective go-to-market strategies and integrated marketing communications plans across digital channels, social media, marketing partnerships, editorial content and videos to grow our Company of Good network and inspire companies to join the profit with purpose movement. - Drive SEO and increase organic traffic to our website.

- Continually test, measure, learn and optimise marketing performance to maximise effectiveness of marketing efforts.

Active Social Listening & UGC Mining: Monitor comments & DMs to identify customer pain points for new content hooks & curate customer testimonials to deploy as high-converting growth assets

Automated Flow Management: Design & execute end-to-end email & WhatsApp automation (e.g., Welcome series, Post-Purchase care, Win-back flows & Replenishment Reminders)
Subscription & Loyalty Optimization: Craft compelling creative & copy for subscription programs, optimizing triggers to reduce churn, increase Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) & grow Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR)
WhatsApp Marketing: Integrate direct-to-consumer WhatsApp communication for personalized consultations, loyalty rewards & rapid promotions
Day-to-Day Marketing Operations & Brand Execution
Execute Business & Marketing Initiatives: Execute effective marketing & business development initiatives tailored to each health supplement brand to increase market share, achieve revenue & reach profitability targets in line with overall business objectives

Compliance & Brand Integrity
Regulatory Compliance: Safeguard brand credibility by ensuring all promotional messaging remain factual, align with company values & strictly comply with regional healthcare advertising standards & product claim guidelines

At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. Build Whats Next For Ai And Data In Asean
This is not a typical product marketing role.
At Snowflake, you’ll help shape how the ASEAN market understands, adopts, and accelerates the future of the AI Data Cloud. You’ll sit at the intersection of product marketing, technical evangelism, go-to-market strategy, and industry influence—bringing together customers, partners, sellers, and marketers around one of the most important technology shifts of our time.
If you thrive on turning complex technology into market momentum, love being in front of customers and communities, and want to make a visible impact in one of the world’s most exciting growth regions, this role was built for you.

Snowflake is scaling fast, and ASEAN is a strategic growth market. In this role, you won’t just support the business—you’ll help define how Snowflake wins in-region.
You’ll be the voice of Snowflake’s AI Data Cloud across the market, translating innovation into relevance for customers, shaping go-to-market strategy, and influencing adoption at scale. With more than 13,000 customers already using Snowflake to modernize data access, accelerate analytics, and unlock data-driven insight, you’ll help drive the next wave of growth powered by AI.

- Lead Snowflake’s Product Marketing and Evangelism efforts across the ASEAN market.
